title: Readiness-timeout: raise default to 10m, or start deadline at first probe-connect (warren-d9e7 follow-up)
description:
## Problem

run_6k1vxy1s9qgj (jayminwest.com on warren v0.3.15) hit the readiness cliff even though every component was healthy:

- pnpm install: 82.1s
- next dev bind: 2.3s ("Ready in 2.3s")
- Next.js first-compile of `/`: 200.4s (1875 modules)
- Total: ~285s vs. 300s `readiness_timeout` default — ~15s headroom

Sidecar log shows `Compiled / in 200.4s` did complete, but the readiness probe still failed at the 5m deadline. That's the project using the combined-command pattern (`pnpm install && next dev`). Migrating jayminwest.com to the warren-d9e7 setup-split (commit 39f4b96 in jayminwest.com) buys back the install budget, but the underlying warren-side cliff remains for any project where first-compile alone approaches or exceeds 5m.

Two distinct issues that compound:

1. **5m default is too tight for modern SPAs.** Next.js / Vite / SvelteKit first-compile of a moderately large app routinely runs 2-4 minutes cold. 5m is the right ceiling for "is the dev server bind responsive" but not for "did the bundler finish a cold compile of the entry route." Raising default to 10m gives an honest first-compile budget.

2. **Deadline starts at sidecar-create, not first probe-connect.** `src/preview/launch.ts:276` computes `deadline = now() + timeoutMs` right after `sidecars.create` returns. That means burrow's startup time, sidecar process spawn, shell pre-exec, dev-server import-and-bind all eat into the readiness budget before any HTTP probe has even fired. The probe's job is "wait for first 2xx," but the timer covers a strict superset. Starting the deadline at first successful TCP connect (or first probe call, whichever is simpler) would isolate readiness from sidecar-startup overhead.

## Approaches (file as alternatives, pick one)

### A. Raise default — one-line fix
- Bump `DEFAULT_READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS` in `src/preview/launch.ts` from 5m to 10m.
- Update `.warren/preview.yaml` template comment to reflect new default + framework matrix guidance.
- Update SPEC §11.L and warren-config schema doc-comment.
- Cheap, ships fast. Doesn't fix the semantics issue (1), just gives more rope. Per-project override (`readiness_timeout` in preview.yaml) already works, so projects with even longer cold-starts can still extend.

### B. Change deadline semantics — start at first probe-connect
- In `src/preview/launch.ts:278-306`, defer the `deadline` computation until the first probe gets a TCP connect (any HTTP response, even non-2xx).
- Two sub-deadlines: a `connect_timeout` (could keep 5m default) covers "did anything bind on the port"; the `readiness_timeout` covers "did it return 2xx" and starts on first connect.
- More precise contract: "readiness_timeout is the bundler's budget, connect_timeout is the binder's budget."
- More invasive: tests, docs, schema. Probably worth doing IF we're already touching the surface — but a follow-up rather than an inline rewrite.

### C. Both: raise default AND change semantics
- Default new `connect_timeout: 5m`, default `readiness_timeout: 10m`, semantics per (B).
- Best long-term shape, biggest surface to touch.

Recommend A as a first patch (fast, fixes the immediate cliff for typical projects), file (B/C) as the follow-up.

## Acceptance

- A: `DEFAULT_READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000`; existing readiness_timeout per-project override unchanged; preview.yaml template comment + SPEC §11.L call out the new default; one regression test pinning the constant.
- (B/C if pursued): scenario covers a slow-binding dev server (long delay before first connect) vs. a slow-compiling one (fast bind, long pre-2xx response) — each gets distinct failure reasons.

## References

- `src/preview/launch.ts:145` (`DEFAULT_READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000`)
- `src/preview/launch.ts:276-306` (deadline computation + probe loop)
- `src/warren-config/schema.ts:191` (preview schema, `readiness_timeout` field)
- jayminwest.com commit 39f4b96 (operator-side workaround)
- SPEC §11.L (preview lifecycle)
- Diagnosed in run_6k1vxy1s9qgj (jayminwest.com on warren v0.3.15)

title: Re-run / clone: one-click duplicate of an existing run with same agent/model/project/prompt
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Adopted into plan pl-df2f.

Parent seed: warren-4b01 — Batch: clear medium/low open backlog
Plan template: feature

Run `sd plan show pl-df2f` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

## Problem

Iterating on a preview / prompt / agent config today requires walking the full new-run dispatcher every time: project picker → agent picker → model picker → branch base → prompt textarea. When the operator is debugging a preview readiness cliff (or any flaky run) and needs to fire the same configuration four or five times, that's ~20 clicks of pure repetition. Observed during the v0.3.15 preview hardening loop: dogfooding required manually recreating runs against jayminwest.com over and over.

## Sibling: warren-4b11

warren-4b11 is the **continuation** case: "follow-up prompt against the prior run's pushed branch." This seed is the **replication** case: "fire a fresh run against `main` with the exact same dispatch config." Both share infra (server endpoint, UI affordance on terminal runs) but the workspace semantics differ:

- **Replicate (this seed):** new run, base = `main` (or whatever the prior run's configured base was), prompt + agent + model + project copied verbatim. Independent of prior run's branch — the prior run might have failed before pushing, or its branch is stale.
- **Continue (warren-4b11):** new run, base = prior run's pushed branch, prompt may be edited. Conversation/workspace continuity is the point.

UI should expose both on the terminal-run page as adjacent affordances: "Re-run from scratch" and "Continue with follow-up." Server-side they're nearly the same endpoint — the discriminator is the base-ref choice.

## Approach

`POST /runs` already exists. Extend with optional `cloneFromRunId` (mirroring warren-4b11's `continueFromRunId`). When set:
- Look up prior run's `agent`, `model`, `projectId`, `prompt`, and base-ref config.
- Spawn new run with same values, base = same base the prior run started from (not prior run's pushed branch — that's warren-4b11's semantics).
- Record parent link in `parent_run_id` (same column warren-4b11 needs — share the column).
- Distinguish the chain type via an extension or a `clone_kind` enum on the row: `replicate` vs. `continue`.

UI:
- On `/runs/:id` for terminal runs, add a "Re-run" button group: ["Re-run from scratch", "Continue with follow-up"]. Both prefill `/runs/new` with the cloned config; "from scratch" sets base to prior run's base, "follow-up" sets base to prior run's branch + opens the prompt textarea for edits.
- Optional later: a one-click "re-run again" on `/runs/:id` for a previously-cloned run that just dispatches without going through `/runs/new` (saves another click).

## Acceptance

- Operator on a terminal run can click "Re-run" and get an identical new run dispatched in one click (or one click + confirm).
- Server records the parent_run_id and the clone_kind.
- Works for every built-in agent (pi, claude-code, sapling).
- Tests in `src/runs/spawn.test.ts` cover the clone path (base-ref = prior run's base, not its pushed branch).
- Distinguishes cleanly from warren-4b11 in the API + UI.

## Out of scope

- Replicating with edits (e.g., swap the model but keep everything else). Future seed if useful.
- Bulk re-dispatch of N runs from a list page. Future seed.

## References

- `src/runs/spawn.ts` (workspace prep)
- `src/server/routes/runs.ts` (POST /runs)
- `src/db/schema.ts` (runs table — `parent_run_id` column shared with warren-4b11)
- warren-4b11 (sibling: continuation against prior branch)

title: Readiness-timeout: deadline starts at sidecar-create, should start at first probe-connect (warren-fdf2 approach B)
description:
## Problem

`warren-fdf2` shipped approach A (raise default 5m → 10m). The semantic issue underneath is still unresolved:

`src/preview/launch.ts:276` computes the deadline immediately after `sidecars.create` returns:

```ts
const deadline = now().getTime() + timeoutMs;
```

That means the `readiness_timeout` budget covers:
1. Burrow's sidecar process spawn
2. Shell `sh -c` pre-exec
3. Dev-server CLI startup (Node/Bun import graph, dependency loading)
4. Dev-server bind on the configured port
5. First HTTP probe TCP connect
6. First-route compile / SSR work
7. First 2xx response

Only (6) and (7) are the bundler's actual readiness — everything before (5) is sidecar startup overhead that varies with burrow health, image cold cache, and shell environment. The name `readiness_timeout` implies (7), but the timer is a strict superset.

Observed cost: on `run_428nktsej0yh` the first compile finished at ~10 min wall clock with first probe arriving within seconds of bind, so the difference was small. But sidecar startup variance under load (many concurrent runs, cold burrow, slow image pull) can easily eat 30s-2min, pushing borderline projects over even a 10m budget when the actual bundler took 8m.

## Approach B (full)

Introduce two distinct timeouts:

```ts
// "Did anything bind on the port?" budget. Covers shell pre-exec,
// CLI startup, port bind. Sized for sidecar startup variance.
export const DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000; // 5m

// "Did the bound server return 2xx?" budget. Sized for bundler
// first-compile. Starts at first successful TCP connect (any HTTP
// status, even non-2xx).
export const DEFAULT_READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS = 600_000; // 10m (unchanged from A)
```

Probe loop becomes a two-phase state machine:

- **Phase 1 (`connect`):** probe with `connect_timeout` deadline. Any HTTP response (including 4xx/5xx and timeouts that aren't ECONNREFUSED) flips to phase 2. ECONNREFUSED / EHOSTUNREACH retries within `connect_timeout`. Exhaustion surfaces a new failure reason `connect_timeout` distinct from `readiness_timeout`.
- **Phase 2 (`readiness`):** standard 2xx-or-3xx probe with `readiness_timeout` deadline starting at phase transition. Existing `readiness_timeout` failure-reason kept.

## Schema + config surface

`PreviewServerConfig`:
- Add `connect_timeout?: string` (duration, 1s..1h bounds — same shape as `readiness_timeout`).
- `readiness_timeout` keeps existing semantics from operator POV (a number of seconds to wait for 2xx), but server-side it's bound to the post-connect phase.

`.warren/preview.yaml` template gets a paragraph and a new field example.

## Failure surface

New `LaunchPreviewFailureReason`: `connect_timeout`. Distinct from `readiness_timeout` (which keeps meaning "server bound but couldn't serve a 2xx in time"). The two reasons are operator-actionable in different ways:

- `connect_timeout` → check the sidecar's command (binding wrong host? port mismatch?), check burrow forwarder.
- `readiness_timeout` → check the dev server's first-compile cost, possibly raise `readiness_timeout`.

`preview_failure_message` includes the failed phase so operators can tell which timeout was the actual cap.

## Tests

- New scenario covers a slow-binding fixture (e.g., `sh -c "sleep 30 && python3 -m http.server 3000"`) — confirms `connect_timeout` fires distinctly from `readiness_timeout`.
- Existing readiness_timeout tests stay correct (fixtures bind quickly, so phase transition happens immediately).
- Bun fetch behavior on `ECONNREFUSED` vs. `EHOSTUNREACH` vs. AbortController-on-no-connect needs verification — the phase-1 discriminator depends on distinguishing "bound and slow" from "not yet bound." Today's `probeOnce` returns `false` for both; we need to surface the underlying network error.

## Acceptance

- `PreviewServerConfig.connect_timeout` parses, defaults to 5m, 1s..1h bounds.
- `LaunchPreviewFailureReason` includes `connect_timeout`.
- Probe loop is two-phase; `readiness_timeout` deadline starts at first connect, not sidecar create.
- `preview_failure_message` records which phase failed.
- New acceptance scenario exercises both failure modes against deterministic fixtures.
- Migration note in CHANGELOG: existing per-project `readiness_timeout` values stay valid but now mean less than before (they only cover bundler, not bind); operators can shrink them if their dev server binds in <5m.

## References

- Sibling approach A: shipped 2026-05-17 (`warren-fdf2` original, commit 0e334a5).
- `src/preview/launch.ts:143` — `DEFAULT_READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS` (current 10m).
- `src/preview/launch.ts:274-306` — probe loop where deadline is computed.
- `src/warren-config/schema.ts:194-195` — `readiness_timeout` schema (where `connect_timeout` would join).
- `src/preview/launch.ts:127-134` — `LaunchPreviewFailureReason` enum.
- SPEC §11.L (preview lifecycle) — needs a paragraph on the two-phase contract.

## Why not now

Approach A's 10m default is sufficient for every project we've actually dogfooded. B is the right *contract* but no concrete project has been blocked on it; ship when either (a) a project trips the cliff approach A didn't cover, or (b) someone is already touching `src/preview/launch.ts` for a related reason and can fold in the two-phase rewrite at near-zero marginal cost.

title: acceptance scenario 20 + 24 hit bridge terminal-detect race when inner stub agent exits in <100ms
description:
Local repro: scenario 20-preview.ts (and the new 24-preview-node-runtime.ts) consistently fail with 'run did not reach terminal within 30000ms (last state=running)' in this sandbox.

Symptoms from WARREN_ACCEPTANCE_WARREN_STDOUT logs:
  t+0.543  burrow:  run started
  t+0.574  burrow:  run finalized (succeeded, exitCode 0) — 31ms wall
  t+0.768  warren:  bridge transitioned queued → running

Bridge subscribed ~200ms after burrow already finalized, so terminalDetected never fires and reap is never called inline (src/server/bridges.ts:254). Run state stays at 'running' forever.

This is independent of warren-0c8e — both scenario 20 (python http.server, baseline) and scenario 24 (node http) hit the same failure. Other in-proc scenarios (04, 06, 09) pass because they don't boot a second inner warren+burrow stack.

Hypothesis: when bootInProc spawns a fresh warren in the inner stack with WARREN_STUB_SLEEP_MS=0, the run-spawn → bridge-subscribe window is wider than the agent's exit, so the bridge attaches after burrow's events stream has already closed without a replay.

Suggested investigation: confirm burrow's events stream replays from seq 0 to late subscribers (or that warren's bridge can fetch terminal state via /runs/:id GET after a missed terminalDetected) — if neither is true, the bridge needs an after-attach reconciler.

Acceptance:
- scenario 20-preview.ts passes locally (current ground truth in CI)
- scenario 20-preview-path.ts passes locally
- scenario 24-preview-node-runtime.ts passes locally

title: Adopt Plot as warren's coordination primitive; shift UI from run-centric to Plot-centric
description:
## Context

Plot is an os-eco primitive shipped from `../plot/` (npm: `@os-eco/plot-cli`, CLI: `plot`). It is a typed, queryable JSON coordination object that holds the intent, attachments, and event log for a unit of work — and references (does not embed) the seeds issues, agent runs, PRs, and mulch records that constitute its substance. **Plot v1 has shipped.** See `../plot/SPEC.md` for the design and `../plot/README.md` for the CLI/library surface.

Plot exists because warren's current primary UI unit is the **run** (orchestrator → worker). The post-V1 direction outlined in [Agentic Networks](https://www.jayminwest.com/blog/12-agentic-networks) requires a different primary unit: a **shared substrate** where humans and agents coexist as peer nodes. Plot is that substrate.

## What this epic tracks

Warren's adoption of Plot as a dependency and the resulting UI / dispatch / event-flow changes. **Building Plot itself happens in the `plot/` repo and is not in scope here.**

## Scope (warren-side)

- **Dependency.** Add `@os-eco/plot-cli` (note: `-cli` suffix; both CLI and library export from the same package). Pin to the published v1 minor.
- **Dispatch path.** When a run is dispatched, set `PLOT_ID` and `PLOT_ACTOR` (`agent:<name>:<run-id>`) in the sandbox env. Agents prime context via `plot get --view implementer` — never load the full Plot.
- **Event flow.** Agent-emitted `decision_made` / `question_posed` / `artifact_produced` events stream into the Plot's event log via `plot append`, mirrored into warren's existing event stream so the run timeline and Plot timeline stay in lockstep.
- **Run reporting.** `run_dispatched` event written to the originating Plot on dispatch; run lifecycle events tagged with `plot_id` in warren's own store.
- **Write-ACL respect.** Warren never emits `intent_edited`, `status_changed`, `attachment_removed`, or `question_answered` from an `agent:*` actor — the Plot library refuses these, and we should never construct calls that would trip it. Humans transitioning a Plot's status from the warren UI is fine (warren acts on behalf of `user:<handle>`).
- **PlanRun composition (warren-fcc9).** A PlanRun launched from a Plot threads `PLOT_ID` through every child run; child events report back to the Plot; Plot auto-transitions to `done` when children close. See warren-fcc9 for the PlanRun primitive itself; this epic adds the Plot wiring (the optional `plot_id` field on PlanRun + dispatcher event hooks).
- **UI shift.** Home page becomes a list of Plots (not runs); per-Plot view has intent panel, substrate panel (attachments), unified activity feed where human and agent events look the same; "run plan" button on Plot detail dispatches a PlanRun against the attached `sd plan`.
- **Status-tag triggers (post-Plot-V1, defer).** Plot transitioning to `ready` triggers a planner agent that calls `sd plan` and writes seeds back as attachments. Out of scope for this epic — file follow-up when status-transition reliability is proven.

## Constraints

- Plot updates land on whatever branch the agent works on; propagate to main with the code (`../plot/SPEC.md` §4.3).
- Agents may never mutate intent — write-ACL enforced at the Plot library level (`../plot/SPEC.md` §6).
- Plot's JSON+JSONL files live in the repo alongside `.seeds/` and `.mulch/`; no cloud dependency.
- The SQLite index (`.plot/.index.db`) is gitignored, rebuildable from files; warren must not assume it exists on first run — call `plot rebuild-index` if needed.
- Plot integration is **gated on the project having a `.plot/` directory**, matching the existing seeds/mulch opt-in shape. Warren's core run primitive stays Plot-free.

## Sequencing

1. ✅ Plot v1 shipped from `../plot/` as `@os-eco/plot-cli` on npm.
2. **Phase 1 — Dispatch wiring (this epic, first child plan).** Add dep, thread `PLOT_ID`/`PLOT_ACTOR` env, surface `plot get --view implementer` to agents, mirror Plot events into warren's stream, write `run_dispatched` back. No UI change yet.
3. **Phase 2 — PlanRun composition.** warren-fcc9 lands as a standalone serial-plan-run feature, then grows an optional `plot_id` field so a PlanRun started from a Plot threads context through every child.
4. **Phase 3 — UI shift (largest).** Incremental: add Plot list page, add Plot detail view with "run plan" button, then deprecate run-list as the primary surface.

Phase 1 is the right place to start an `sd plan` decomposition. Phases 2 and 3 are tracked separately (Phase 2 wires into warren-fcc9; Phase 3 will be its own plan when Phase 1+2 are stable).

## Acceptance (Phase 1 only — this is what the plan should cover)

- Warren depends on `@os-eco/plot-cli` at a pinned v1 minor.
- Dispatching a run against a project with a `.plot/` directory and a Plot ID:
  - Sets `PLOT_ID` and `PLOT_ACTOR=agent:<name>:<run-id>` in the sandbox env.
  - Writes a `run_dispatched` event to the originating Plot.
  - Forwards agent-emitted Plot events (`decision_made`, `question_posed`, `artifact_produced`) into warren's event stream with `plot_id` tagging.
- Dispatching against a project **without** `.plot/` is unchanged from today.
- An agent inside the sandbox can call `plot get --view implementer` and `plot append` against the bound Plot end-to-end (verify via acceptance scenario).
- No agent-actor calls to humans-only event types ever reach the Plot library (would be a bug; the library rejects them but warren shouldn't construct them).

title: Detect & reconcile ghost runs (warren state running, burrow has no record)
description:
## Problem

When the warren machine restarts (e.g. `fly scale memory`, OOM kill, deploy with `immediate` strategy, host migration) and burrow loses an in-flight run from its store, the run becomes a "ghost" in the UI:

- warren's Postgres row stays in `state=running`, `ended_at=null`
- burrow returns `{"code":"not_found","message":"run not found: run_xxx"}` for the `burrow_run_id`
- UI keeps showing the run as live; user clicks **Steer** → "burrow xxx not found"; clicks **Cancel** → "run not found: run_xxx"
- warren's per-run stream bridge enters an indefinite backoff loop (`bridge errored — reconnecting after backoff`, capped at 30s/attempt), spamming logs forever

The only fix today is `UPDATE runs SET state='failed', ended_at=now() WHERE id=...` directly against Postgres, plus a process restart to stop the bridge loop. Hit live on 2026-05-17 during the 2GB→4GB scale; `run_b9dz5jdsrvsv` / burrow `run_ktz51n6n7ww3`.

## Desired behavior

A run whose `burrow_run_id` no longer exists in burrow should be reconcilable both automatically and by the user, without DB surgery.

### Reconciler (server-side)
- On warren startup, for every non-terminal run, GET burrow's run; if burrow returns 404, mark the run `failed` with `failure_reason='burrow_run_lost'` (or similar) and `ended_at=now()`.
- The per-run stream bridge should give up (not infinitely backoff) when burrow returns 404 on reconnect — the run is unrecoverable, mark it failed instead.

### UI
- When the active-run actions (Steer/Cancel) get a 404 from burrow, surface a **"Mark run failed"** affordance instead of the raw error, so the user can reconcile from the UI.
- Optionally: badge the run "stale/orphaned" once the bridge has 404'd N times.

## Acceptance
- Restart the machine mid-run (kill burrow's store deliberately for a test); the run transitions to `failed` within one reconciler tick, the bridge loop ends, and the UI lets the user dismiss it without raw burrow errors.

## Related
- Today's incident: see fly logs around `2026-05-17T19:42Z` (machine ran out of memory at 2GB → scale memory → burrow's run state lost on reboot → ghost run for `run_b9dz5jdsrvsv`).

title: Compute cost/tokens for failed runs from streamed events
description:
## Problem

When a run terminates abnormally (machine restart, ghost run, reap never finalizes), `runs.cost_usd`, `runs.tokens_input/output`, `runs.tokens_cache_read/write` are all null and the UI shows cost as `"-"`. The agent's actual token spend is invisible to the operator even though the data exists.

Concretely, today's incident: `run_b9dz5jdsrvsv` had **609 events streamed and persisted** to Postgres (454 carrying usage/cost telemetry — kinds: `state_change, telemetry, text, thinking, tool_result, tool_use`) before warren stalled and the machine rebooted. The run got far enough to almost finish, but every usage column on the row is null because reap never ran to persist totals.

Pattern in code today (warren server logs):
- During streaming, warren logs `"persisted in-stream usage totals"` periodically (seen on successful runs `run_6k1vxy1s9qgj`: $0.144 / 1726 out, `run_428nktsej0yh`: $0.156 / 1944 out).
- For the orphaned run, that log line never appears — the bridge died before the next checkpoint.

So usage totals are checkpointed only periodically and finalized at reap. Any run that doesn't reach the next checkpoint **loses all its visible cost**, even though the underlying events are durably stored.

## Desired behavior

Operator-visible cost should be at least best-effort for any run with streamed events, regardless of terminal state.

Two complementary options:

1. **Compute on read** — when serving a run to the UI/API, if `runs.cost_usd` is null but events exist, derive it from `events` (sum the usage payloads). Cheap to add, surfaces existing data immediately. Could be a view or a fallback in the run repo's `findById`.
2. **Backfill on reconciliation** — when a run transitions to a terminal state (including the new ghost-run reconciler from warren-b1a9), recompute cost/tokens from `events` and write them to the row, so subsequent reads don't need the fallback.

Either alone fixes the symptom; ideally do (2) as the source of truth and (1) as a transitional fallback while old rows still have null totals.

## Acceptance

- A failed/cancelled run that has events shows a non-null cost and token totals in the UI matching the sum of streamed usage events.
- Backfilling `run_b9dz5jdsrvsv` (or replaying the scenario in a test) yields a positive cost roughly proportional to its 609 events / 454 usage payloads.

## Related

- warren-b1a9 — ghost-run reconciliation (this is the natural place to call the cost backfill).
- Today's incident — `run_b9dz5jdsrvsv` / burrow `run_ktz51n6n7ww3`.

title: Phase 2: thread plot_id through PlanRun (warren-fcc9) so plan-runs report to the originating Plot
description:
## Context

warren-000b Phase 2. Follow-up to **warren-000b** (Plot adoption epic) and **warren-fcc9** (PlanRun: serial plan execution). Phase 1 (`pl-2047`) wires Plot into single-run dispatch — `PLOT_ID` / `PLOT_ACTOR` env, `run_dispatched` emission, event mirroring at reap. This epic adds the same wiring to PlanRun so a plan-run launched from a Plot threads context through every child run and reports their lifecycle back to the Plot.

Independent of Plot at the PlanRun V1 boundary — composition is purely additive (per warren-fcc9 acceptance: 'Existing single-run dispatch path is unchanged; PlanRun is purely additive'). When both ship, this epic adds the Plot wiring.

## Scope

- Optional `plot_id` field on the PlanRun entity (DB column + API surface, mirroring the `runs.plot_id` column landed in pl-2047 / warren-a8c3).
- Dispatcher: when a PlanRun has `plot_id`, every child run dispatched by the coordinator inherits it — same env injection (`PLOT_ID` / `PLOT_ACTOR=agent:<name>:<run-id>`) the single-run path already does.
- One `run_dispatched` event per child landing in the Plot's event log (not just for the PlanRun parent — agents need to see each child run).
- A single `plan_run_dispatched` event on the Plot when the PlanRun itself starts, with payload {plan_run_id, plan_id, children_count}.
- Auto-transition: Plot status transitions to `done` when all PlanRun children close (per warren-000b §Scope, 'PlanRun composition' bullet). Defensive — only transitions if Plot is currently in `active` and write-ACL permits.
- Dispatch UI: PlanRun create form (warren-fcc9) accepts optional `plot_id` — autopopulated if the dispatch originates from a Plot detail page (Phase 3), free-form input until then.

## Gating

Surface only when BOTH `.plot/` is present in the project AND `.seeds/` is present (PlanRun's existing gate). Stack the gates; don't loosen either.

## Acceptance

- PlanRun row stores optional `plot_id`; POST /plan-runs accepts it; GET surfaces it.
- Dispatching a PlanRun with `plot_id` injects PLOT_ID + PLOT_ACTOR into every child run's sandbox env.
- A `plan_run_dispatched` event lands on the Plot at PlanRun start; one `run_dispatched` event per child as it spawns.
- Plot auto-transitions `active` → `done` when the final PlanRun child closes (and not before).
- PlanRun without `plot_id` is byte-identical to the warren-fcc9 baseline (no Plot leakage).
- POST /plan-runs with `plot_id` against a project without `.plot/` rejects with a typed error (same shape as the single-run validation in pl-2047 / warren-a8c3).

## Sequencing

Blocked on:
- **warren-fcc9** (PlanRun V1) closing — this epic composes on top of it.
- **pl-2047** closing — single-run Plot wiring is the substrate this reuses.

When both unblock, decompose this epic with `sd plan` the same way pl-2047 decomposed warren-000b Phase 1.

## References

- warren-000b — parent epic (Plot adoption, all three phases)
- warren-fcc9 — PlanRun (serial plan execution); §'Relationship to Plot' calls out this composition
- pl-2047 — Phase 1 decomposition (single-run dispatch wiring)
- ../plot/SPEC.md §6 — write-ACL (status_changed humans-only; auto-done transition uses warren's system actor)

title: Phase 3: shift warren UI from run-centric to Plot-centric (Plot list, detail, unified activity feed)
description:
## Context

warren-000b Phase 3 — the largest and most user-visible chunk. Follow-up to **warren-000b** (Plot adoption epic). Phase 1 (`pl-2047`) wired Plot into dispatch with no UI change. Phase 2 (`warren-06dc`) threads Plot through PlanRun. Phase 3 makes Plot the primary surface in the warren UI.

Driven by the post-V1 direction in [Agentic Networks](https://www.jayminwest.com/blog/12-agentic-networks): the unit users care about is no longer the run (orchestrator → worker) but the **Plot** (shared substrate where humans and agents coexist as peer nodes). Phase 3 rebuilds the UI around that unit.

## Scope (incremental — three sub-phases per warren-000b §Sequencing)

### 3a — Plot list page (additive)
- New `/plots` route in src/ui/.
- Server route: GET /plots returns Plot summaries (id, name, status, intent goal preview, attachments count, last-event timestamp, last-event actor).
- Card or table view, sortable by recency; filter by status (drafting / ready / active / done / archived).
- 'New Plot' button shells to `plot init` server-side and routes to the new Plot's detail page.
- No deprecation of /runs yet — both lists exist side by side.

### 3b — Plot detail page (largest)
- Route `/plots/:id` with three panels (per warren-000b §Scope):
  - **Intent panel** — goal / non-goals / constraints / success criteria, editable inline (humans only; agent actors get read-only with a 'open a question' affordance that creates a `question_posed` event).
  - **Substrate panel** — attachments list (seeds_issue, mulch_record, canopy_prompt, agent_run, gh_pr) with role labels; add/detach via UI.
  - **Activity feed** — unified timeline where human and agent events render with the same affordances; collapses repetitive event chains; shows actor in a stable visual slot.
- 'Run plan' button when an `sd plan` attachment is present — dispatches a PlanRun (warren-06dc) bound to this Plot.
- Status transition control (drafting → ready → active → done) gated on write-ACL — humans only.
- Question-answer affordance: open `question_posed` events surface as inline cards with an answer textarea; submit posts `question_answered` via the warren server (user actor).

### 3c — Deprecate run-list as primary surface (cleanup)
- /plots becomes the home page; /runs moves under a 'Runs' sidebar entry (kept for the standalone path that has no `.plot/`).
- Header navigation reorders accordingly.
- The PlanRun detail page (warren-fcc9) gets a back-link to its Plot when `plot_id` is set.

## Out of scope (file follow-ups)

- **Status-tag triggers** (warren-000b mentions this as 'post-Plot-V1, defer'): Plot transitioning to `ready` triggers a planner agent that calls `sd plan` and writes seeds back as attachments. Out of scope here; file follow-up when status-transition reliability is proven in 3a/3b.
- **Live Plot-event streaming** — Phase 1 chose JSONL-tail-at-reap (no live channel from sandbox to warren). UI 'Activity feed' will show events only after reap until that's revisited. Phase 3 should record what's missing; the live channel itself is a separate epic.
- **Multi-Plot cross-references** — when Plot A attaches Plot B, the UI should link them. Defer to a focused follow-up after the single-Plot surface is stable.

## Gating

Each sub-phase is independent and shippable. Gate the Plot navigation entry on the deployment having at least one project with `.plot/` (server-side discoverable via the per-project flag landed in pl-2047 / warren-4e20). Projects without any `.plot/` see the existing run-centric UI unchanged.

## Acceptance

- 3a: /plots route lists all Plots across projects with status + recency + new-Plot creation.
- 3b: /plots/:id renders intent, substrate, and unified activity in three panels; question-answer affordance round-trips through the Plot event log; 'Run plan' button dispatches a PlanRun bound to the Plot.
- 3c: /plots is the default landing for deployments with any `.plot/` projects; /runs remains reachable; PlanRun detail back-links to Plot when bound.
- ACL respected throughout: humans only can transition status, edit intent, answer questions, detach attachments; agent actors never construct those calls (defended by the facade landed in pl-2047 / warren-8b13).
- Existing single-run UI is byte-identical for projects without `.plot/` (no Plot-leak regressions).

## Sequencing

Blocked on:
- **warren-06dc** (Phase 2) closing — the 'Run plan' button on Plot detail dispatches via the Plot-aware PlanRun primitive.
- **pl-2047** (Phase 1) closing — the per-project `hasPlot` flag and the run.plot_id column landed there back the gating and the run→Plot links.

When both unblock, plan each sub-phase (3a / 3b / 3c) with its own `sd plan` decomposition — they're large enough that one mega-plan would be unwieldy.

## References

- warren-000b — parent epic
- warren-06dc — Phase 2 (PlanRun Plot wiring)
- pl-2047 — Phase 1 (single-run dispatch wiring)
- [Agentic Networks](https://www.jayminwest.com/blog/12-agentic-networks) — theoretical foundation
- ../plot/SPEC.md §3 (data model), §6 (write-ACL), §8 (views — informer/implementer/reviewer drive panel shaping)

title: burrow: parse body.env on POST /burrows so warren-e26f PLOT_ID/PLOT_ACTOR reach the sandbox
description: Warren's spawn flow (warren-e26f) sends {env: {PLOT_ID, PLOT_ACTOR}} on the burrow up POST body via BurrowClient.burrowsUp (src/burrow-client/client.ts). Burrow's server-side createBurrow handler (burrow-cli@0.3.1 src/server/handlers.ts:405) does NOT parse body.env into BurrowUpInput, so envOverrides stays empty in runUpCommand and the values never reach SandboxProfile.setEnv. Result: the in-sandbox plot CLI (and any future per-run env contract from warren) sees PLOT_ID empty. Acceptance scenario 25 (warren-4e06) detects this gap — the env-reaches-sandbox + workspace plot append + plot.* mirror assertions are currently soft-skipped pending this fix. Once burrow accepts body.env (parse → BurrowUpInput.envOverrides → resolveEnv overrides → setEnv), bump @os-eco/burrow-cli in package.json + bun.lock + Dockerfile (double-pin per the burrow-cli convention) and flip the conditional assertions in scenario 25 back to hard required.

title: Update warren Plot ID test fixtures + SPEC §11.O path examples after plot rename (plot-ab1f)
description:
## Context

Blocked on plot's rename of Plot ID prefix `pl-` → `plot-` (filed as `plot-ab1f` in ../plot). Once plot ships the new format, warren's test fixtures, SPEC examples, and one acceptance scenario's doc comments should be updated for consistency. **No production code changes required** — warren does not validate Plot ID format and `runs.plot_id` is opaque text.

## Why this matters

Concrete evidence of the collision in this very repo: `src/db/repos/runs.test.ts:113` uses `plotId: "pl-2047"` as a Plot ID fixture, while `src/burrow-client/client.ts:135` references `pl-2047 step 4` as the **seeds plan ID** for warren-000b. Same string, two different ID types, in one codebase. The rename eliminates this entire class of accident.

## Changes

### Test fixtures (rename to `plot-<8 lowercase alnum>` form)

- `src/plot-client/client.test.ts` — replace `pl-deadbeef` (×4)
- `src/plot-client/handle.test.ts` — replace `pl-test0001` (×2)
- `src/server/handlers.test.ts:871,893` — replace `plot_id = 'pl-2047'` and the matching assertion
- `src/db/repos/runs.test.ts:113` — replace `plotId: \"pl-2047\"`

Suggested replacements: `plot-deadbeef`, `plot-test0001`, `plot-2047abc` (or any 8-char lowercase alnum). The literal value is irrelevant to the tests — they only need to be syntactically valid Plot IDs under the new regex.

### SPEC.md §11.O path examples

Update the flow-diagram comments around lines 1738–1755 from `.plot/pl-<id>.events.jsonl` / `.plot/pl-*.events.jsonl` / `.plot/pl-*.json` to use `plot-<id>` / `plot-*` filename patterns. These are doc examples of plot's on-disk layout, so they should track plot's new convention.

### Scenario 25 doc comments (no logic changes)

`scripts/acceptance/scenarios/25-plot-roundtrip.ts` is already format-agnostic at runtime — it reads the Plot ID from `plot list --json` (line 336) and composes file paths via template literal (line 165: \`join(..., \`\${plotId}.events.jsonl\`)\`). Only the documentation comments at lines 19, 33, 38, 219, 320 reference the literal `pl-<id>` filename pattern and should be flipped to `plot-<id>`.

Do **not** touch line 2's `(warren-4e06, pl-2047)` — that `pl-2047` is the seeds plan ID for the plot integration work.

## Do NOT touch

- Seeds plan ID references throughout warren (`pl-fef5`, `pl-bb70`, `pl-9ba1`, `pl-2f15`, `pl-5d74`, `pl-cb3e`, `pl-2c59`, `pl-f4ea`, `pl-2047`-as-plan-id, etc.). Those live in seeds' namespace and stay as-is.
- The §11.O section header `### 11.O Plot integration (pl-2047, 2026-05-17)` — `pl-2047` there is the **seeds plan ID** for the plot integration work, not a Plot ID.
- DB schema — `runs.plot_id` is opaque text. No migration.
- `src/plot-client/` production code — no regex validation; nothing to change.

title: Coordinator: build src/plan-runs/ module modeled on src/triggers/ (mx-fb4a85 single-flight tick is the load-bearing pattern). Files: index.ts (public exports), errors.ts (PlanRunDispatchError), tick.ts (top-level walker), coordinator.ts (per-PlanRun decision), dispatch.ts (spawn wrapper), pr-merge.ts (thin retry wrapper over the helper from step 4 that survives transient http_error). The per-PlanRun decision in coordinator.ts is `advancePlanRun({planRun, repos, listChildren, showPlan, showSeed, checkPrMerged, spawn, now, emit}): Promise<AdvanceResult>` returning a discriminated union {kind:'dispatched', childRunId} | {kind:'waiting_for_run'} | {kind:'waiting_for_merge'} | {kind:'advanced', mergedChildSeq, dispatchedChildSeq?} | {kind:'plan_failed', failedSeq, reason} | {kind:'plan_succeeded'} | {kind:'noop', reason}; state machine: (a) if planRun.state == 'queued' → transition to 'running', set startedAt, then fall through; (b) load the lowest-seq child whose state is in ('dispatched','running','pr_open'); if present and the linked run is non-terminal → waiting_for_run; if terminal-succeeded and child.state != 'pr_open' → flip child to 'pr_open' (or 'merged' if run.prUrl is null AND reap's empty-push event fired, treated as 'trivially merged' per mx-fd8619); if 'pr_open' → call checkPrMerged(run.prUrl); merged → flip child to 'merged' with mergedAt, fall through to dispatch next; open → waiting_for_merge; closed_unmerged or http 4xx → plan_failed with reason 'pr_closed_without_merge'; if terminal-failed/cancelled → plan_failed with reason `child_${reason ?? 'failed'}`; (c) if no in-flight child, call repos.planRuns.pickNextPending; if null → plan_succeeded (transition planRuns row to 'succeeded', set endedAt); if non-null → call showSeed against the child's seedId; status='closed' → flip to 'skipped' (resume semantics, warren-fcc9 acceptance), loop to (b); status='open' → spawn via dispatch.ts which calls spawnRun with {agentName: planRun.agentName, projectId: planRun.projectId, prompt: substitute(planRun.promptTemplate, {seed_id: child.seedId}), trigger: 'plan-run', seedId: child.seedId, providerOverride, modelOverride, ref: planRun.ref ?? project.defaultBranch, metadata: {planRunId, planId, childSeq}}; on success write child.runId, child.state='dispatched', child.startedAt; on RunSpawnError → plan_failed with reason `dispatch_failed:${err.message}`. tick.ts exports `runPlanRunTick(deps): Promise<PlanRunTickResult>` that lists all active planRuns via repos.planRuns.listActive(), advances each (catch-per-PlanRun like the scheduler's runProjectTick, mx-fb4a85 risk #9, no one bad row tears down the loop), and returns the result array for diagnostics. `bootPlanRunCoordinator(deps): {stop}` returns the same single-flight wrapper shape as `bootScheduler` (src/server/scheduler.ts) — drops overlapping ticks instead of stacking; honors `WARREN_PLAN_RUN_DISABLED=1` like `WARREN_SCHEDULER_DISABLED`; default cadence is `WARREN_PLAN_RUN_TICK_MS=10000` (10s, faster than scheduler's 60s). Surface every state transition as a warren event on the most recently-dispatched child run via the existing emit/event seam (mirror the scheduler's `trigger.*` system events) — kinds: `plan_run.advanced`, `plan_run.dispatched`, `plan_run.waiting_for_merge`, `plan_run.merged`, `plan_run.failed`, `plan_run.succeeded`. Unit tests in src/plan-runs/coordinator.test.ts cover all eight state-transition branches with stub repos + stub spawn + stub checkPrMerged; tick.test.ts covers the per-PlanRun isolation (one PlanRun throwing doesn't stop another). NO direct integration with sd update --extensions on plan-run dispatch — that's the seed back-link (pl-bb70) and is already handled by spawnRun's existing updateExtensions call when seedId is set (mx-ed7fb5 / src/runs/spawn.ts lines 395–401). title: refreshProject (git reset --hard) wipes uncommitted .plot/ host-side appends between children
description: Host-side Plot appenders write to project_clone/.plot/<id>.{events.jsonl,json} WITHOUT committing — defaultPlotAppender (src/runs/spawn.ts:597 / warren-e848), defaultPlanRunPlotAppender (src/plan-runs/plot-appender.ts / warren-b89f), and autoTransitionPlotToDone (src/plan-runs/plot-transition.ts / warren-b290) all just call PlotHandle.append/setStatus which writes the file but never commits. refreshProject (src/projects/refresh.ts:139) runs git reset --hard origin/<ref> on every spawnRun and discards all of those uncommitted edits before each child dispatches. Observed in scenario 27 (warren-97a3): only the LAST child's run_dispatched line and the post-final-child status_changed line survive in the on-disk .plot/<id>.events.jsonl; the plan_run_dispatched line and the prior children's run_dispatched lines are wiped. The .json snapshot's auto-done status='done' is similarly reverted to 'active' on the next refresh. Scenario 27 works around this by tailing the events.jsonl every 100ms to accumulate the transient writes. Production impact: an operator inspecting a project's .plot/ at rest sees only the last surviving writes, and the Plot status seen in .json is not durable across PlanRuns or any subsequent spawnRun against the same project. Fix shapes to consider: (a) commit .plot/ changes alongside the next workspace branch_push (analogous to how mulch records are merged + committed via reap), (b) skip git reset of paths under .plot/ in refreshProject when the project hasPlot, (c) store host-side Plot appender writes in an out-of-tree side-table (mirroring warren events) and rebuild .plot/ from it. Cross-cuts pl-2047 (Phase 1) and pl-7937 (Phase 2). Related: warren-7e0f (reap's plot merge), mx-239786 (per-child run_dispatched appender).
closeReason: All plan steps (pl-d4d6) closed; shape (b) snapshot/restore landed in v0.4.2 (commit 172eef5). Follow-up shape (a) commit-through-reap filed as warren-343a.

title: NewPlanRun: link to project refresh from the missing-.seeds/ error
description:
When the NewPlanRun page detects `!hasSeeds` on the selected project, the error card (src/ui/src/pages/NewPlanRun.tsx:149-158) tells the user to 'add .seeds/ and refresh the project' but offers no action. In practice the most common cause is a stale hasSeeds flag: the project was registered before the warren-9990 detection landed (or before .seeds/ was committed), and the row's has_seeds column is still false even though the on-disk clone has .seeds/. The fix is a one-click POST /projects/:id/refresh — which works today, but only if the user knows to navigate to the Projects tab and find the refresh icon.

Surface that path from the error itself. Either: (a) add a 'Refresh project' button inside the destructive card that calls projectsApi.refresh(project) and invalidates the projects query on success, or (b) link to /projects with the row highlighted. Option (a) is the more direct fix and matches the surrounding mutation pattern (see Projects.tsx:49-52).

Repro: register a project on a warren version predating 0.3.17, upgrade warren, open /plan-runs/new, select the project — error shows even though .seeds/ exists in the repo.

Discovered while investigating the warren project itself failing this gate in prod today.

title: Shape (a): commit .plot/ through reap so Plot state round-trips to origin
description:
Follow-up to warren-6f25 / pl-d4d6 (shape b: snapshot+restore .plot/ across refreshProjectClone resets, mx-…). Shape (b) made .plot/ durable on the warren host's project clone but Plot state still never leaves the host — origin's main has no .plot/ commits, so a warren restart that re-clones loses everything, and operators inspecting the GitHub repo see nothing.

## The change
Make reap commit and push .plot/ alongside the agent's workspace edits.

Touchpoints:
- src/runs/reap.ts mergePlot() (~line 1236): after the events.jsonl + plot-*.json merges into the project clone, stage `.plot/plot-*.{events.jsonl,json}` via git add. Skip .plot/.index.db (gitignored derived state per ../plot/README.md).
- src/runs/reap.ts: the host-side appenders (defaultPlotAppender in src/runs/spawn.ts, defaultPlanRunPlotAppender in src/plan-runs/plot-appender.ts, autoTransitionPlotToDone in src/plan-runs/plot-transition.ts) write to .plot/ between spawns — those writes also need to be staged at reap time, not just the burrow-workspace-derived merges. Either reap stages everything in .plot/ at the end, or each appender stages its own write at append time.
- The branch_push step (reap.ts ~line 482) then carries the .plot/ commit upstream as part of the workspace branch.
- On merge to default branch, .plot/ is now durable on origin; next refreshProjectClone fetches it back and shape (b)'s snapshot becomes a no-op for already-committed files.

## Hard cases
1. **Trivial-merge children with no agent commits**: a child whose agent never ran `git commit` produces a branch with 0 commits ahead (reap.empty_push case, mx- / SPEC §11.G). Shape (a) needs reap to author its own commit ('chore(warren): plot state' or similar) when .plot/ has staged changes but the agent didn't commit — otherwise the Plot writes still don't ship. Identity: use a warren bot identity (e.g. 'warren <warren@os-eco.dev>') configured in the clone, not the agent's git identity.
2. **Two concurrent plan-run children both writing to the same Plot**: child A's reap pushes .plot/plot-X.events.jsonl with events 1..5; child B's branch was forked before A's merge, so B's refreshProjectClone fetches A's commit, then B appends events 6..7 on top. The append-only events.jsonl merges trivially via line-union (mergePlotEventsFile already does this). The plot-*.json LWW-on-updated_at logic (reap.ts mergePlot) handles status conflicts. But if A's PR hasn't merged yet when B starts, B forks from origin/main WITHOUT A's .plot/ commit — B's snapshot+restore (shape b) preserves its own local Plot writes, then B's reap re-merges with B's local view and commits. When A merges first then B merges, GitHub's merge produces a conflict on .plot/plot-X.events.jsonl. Mitigation: serialize via plan-run's existing 'gate next child on previous PR merge' semantics (SPEC §11.P) — covers the plan-run case. For ad-hoc parallel runs against the same project, document the conflict shape and rely on mergePlotEventsFile's idempotent line-union on the next refresh.
3. **PR auto-open with .plot/-only diffs**: a run where the agent did nothing but warren's appenders wrote a run_dispatched event produces a PR with only .plot/ changes. The auto-PR shape (mx-, src/runs/pr.ts) needs to decide whether to open one — current behavior keys on commitsAhead > 0, which a warren-authored .plot/ commit would satisfy. Probably fine to auto-PR, but worth a config knob (`autoOpenPrPlotOnly: false` default?) so .plot/-only changes don't spam PRs.
4. **Plot id collisions across branches**: two branches initializing the same plot id (rare; ids are uuid-shaped per ../plot/SPEC.md). Treat as user error.

## Acceptance
1. After a run that emits Plot events (host-side or agent-side), `git log -- .plot/` on origin/<workspace-branch> shows a commit by warren containing the events.jsonl + json updates.
2. A run where the agent never commits but warren wrote .plot/ entries still produces a non-empty branch push (warren-authored commit) — no reap.empty_push event in this case.
3. A plan-run with N>=2 children against a project with .plot/ produces N PRs (or 1 cumulative PR depending on PR mode) that each carry their child's .plot/ delta; after all merge, origin/main's .plot/ reflects the full plan-run history.
4. Wiping the warren host's project clone and re-cloning from origin recovers the full Plot state (events.jsonl + status.json) — shape (a)'s round-trip property, which shape (b) cannot provide.
5. Conflict shape documented in SPEC.md §11.O for the concurrent-children-same-plot case.
6. mergePlotEventsFile idempotency holds across the new commit-and-fetch loop — re-running reap against the same workspace adds nothing.
7. .plot/.index.db remains gitignored and never committed.
8. `bun test && bun run lint && bun run typecheck` passes.
9. CHANGELOG entry + version bump (likely minor — observable behavior change on the workspace branch).
10. SPEC.md §11.O updated: 'Plot state is committed through reap to the workspace branch and round-trips to origin on merge. The host-side .plot/ snapshot+restore in refreshProjectClone (warren-fdd2) remains as a belt-and-suspenders preservation for in-flight writes between dispatch and the next reap.'

## Why deferred from pl-d4d6
Shape (b) was the minimum to unblock the warren-on-warren dogfood (Plot state visible to the operator inspecting the host's project clone). Shape (a) extends durability to origin and across hosts, but the design has more surface area (warren-authored commits, PR-mode interaction, concurrent-branch conflicts) and needs its own plan.

title: Persist burrow's data dir on /data volume so deploys don't orphan in-flight runs
description: Symptom (observed 2026-05-18 on warren-deployed Fly app, machine e82656da0747d8): warren run run_dra64q8qt00z dispatched at 15:14:23Z with burrow_run_id run_9m0qs5m94srh on burrow bur_8py7wz7ndy4k. At 15:19:02Z the machine redeployed (v0.4.0 -> v0.4.1). After redeploy, warren's Supabase Postgres row still says state='running', but burrow returns 404 for run_9m0qs5m94srh on both POST /runs/:id/cancel and GET /runs/:id/stream. The stream-bridge has retried for 80+ attempts with 30s backoff and cannot finalize. Cancel from the UI surfaces 'run not found: run_9m0qs5m94srh' (the burrow-side id) through src/runs/cancel.ts:127 via withTransportMapping. Root cause: burrow's SQLite lives at /root/.local/share/burrow/db.sqlite (default XDG_DATA_HOME). That path is on the container's writable overlay, NOT on the /data Fly volume declared in fly.toml. Verified via flyctl ssh: 'stat /root/.local/share/burrow/db.sqlite' returns Birth: 2026-05-18 15:19:02.970334415 — matches the machine restart to the second. Every redeploy starts burrow with an empty DB, orphaning any in-flight runs whose state lives in warren's Postgres but whose execution state lived in burrow's wiped SQLite. Fix (warren-side, since warren owns Dockerfile + fly.toml + the supervisor that spawns 'burrow serve'): redirect burrow's data dir onto /data. Two viable approaches — (a) set ENV XDG_DATA_HOME=/data/xdg in Dockerfile (one-line, but co-locates any other XDG-using tool); (b) check whether 'burrow serve' accepts an explicit --data-dir flag (see ../burrow/SPEC.md and burrow's CLI; if it does, prefer wiring it through src/supervisor/main.ts:371 burrowCmd alongside --socket). Approach (b) is more surgical and survives unrelated XDG env changes. Verification: redeploy, confirm /data/xdg/burrow/db.sqlite (or the explicit path) exists and persists; dispatch a run, redeploy mid-flight, confirm warren's bridge reconnects and the run finalizes through the normal reap path rather than orphaning. Secondary gap worth a follow-up seed (not this one): warren has no reconciliation when burrow 404s a known burrow_run_id. The bridge in src/server/bridges.ts retries forever; cancel returns the burrow 404 verbatim. Even after the persistence fix, any future divergence (manual burrow DB reset, restored-from-backup, etc) will leave the same orphan state. A 'force-finalize' admin endpoint OR auto-finalize-on-persistent-404 in the bridge would cap the blast radius.

title: Plot UX: surface refresh affordance / auto-detect newly-committed .plot/ in registered projects
description:
First dogfood-discovered Plot UX gap (surfaced via plot-3e72876d / the housekeeping pass): Plots created via the plot 0.3.0 — coordination substrate for multi-agent work

Usage: plot <command> [options]

Commands:
  init           create a new Plot, return its ID
  list           list all Plots in .plot/
  show           pretty-print Plot fields + recent events
  edit           open intent in $EDITOR
  intent         non-interactive intent edit
  status         transition a Plot's status
  attach         attach a typed reference
  detach         remove an attachment
  answer         answer an agent-posed question
  get            render a view (agent-facing, default JSON)
  append         append an event (agent-facing)
  rebuild-index  wipe and regenerate the SQLite cache
  sync           stage + commit .plot/ source files
  doctor         check file integrity + event log replay

Global options:
  --help, -h     Show this help
  --version, -v  Print version
  --json         Machine-readable output (per command)

Env:
  PLOT_DIR       Plot directory (default: .plot)
  PLOT_ACTOR     Override actor (e.g. user:jw, agent:claude:run-1)
  PLOT_ID        Default Plot ID for agent commands (`get`, `append`)
  PLOT_DEBUG     Set to 1 to print stack traces on error CLI in a project repo are silently invisible in the warren UI until BOTH (a) the project is registered with warren AND (b) refreshProjectClone has run since the Plot files were committed. The /plots aggregator (src/plots/aggregate.ts:163 listSummaries) filters on projects.hasPlot, which detectProjectFeatures sets only during refresh. There is no UI affordance signaling 'I just committed a Plot, refresh to see it' — a user could push a Plot and stare at an empty /plots page indefinitely. The /plots/:id route 404s for the same reason (PlotResolver also scans only hasPlot projects). Symmetric failure: a user who git-pulls inside a deployed-warren-managed project clone (outside warren's process) would never see hasPlot flip until something else triggered refresh. Fix shapes (range from cheap to ambitious): (1) Cheap — when /plots returns an empty list AND any registered project has been git-touched recently OR the empty-state UI in /plots is hit, surface a 'Refresh projects to discover new Plots' CTA in src/ui/src/pages/PlotsList.tsx and src/ui/src/pages/PlotDetail.tsx empty/404 states. (2) Medium — periodic background refresh of registered projects (cron-style poll) gated by a config flag in .warren/config.yaml or warren-config domain, default off, opt-in for deployments where webhook infra isn't available. (3) Right — GitHub webhook on push → warren refreshes the project automatically; this is the same infrastructure R-18 (GitHub App auth) and V2 webhooks unlock, so this seed should reference R-18 and be considered subsumed when that lands. Evidence: plot-3e72876d (created locally 2026-05-18, committed to main as 2d7a75f, transitioned drafting → ready, attached to 9 housekeeping seeds, invisible in deployed warren UI until manual project refresh — user reported '/plots/plot-3e72876d returns plot not found' immediately after push). Recommended scope for V1 of this seed: ship (1) the empty-state CTA only — it's the smallest correct intervention, surfaces the next step inline, and doesn't commit warren to background polling or webhook infra. (2) and (3) become their own follow-up seeds once (1) is in production and we observe whether the affordance is enough.

title: Plot aggregator: rebuild index when query returns empty (not just on throw)
description: BLOCKS Plot UI dogfooding. queryWithRebuildRetry in src/plots/aggregate.ts:248-268 only triggers client.rebuildIndex() on a thrown error from client.query(). But .plot/.index.db is gitignored (warren commit 2d7a75f), so a freshly-refreshed project clone has the *.json + *.events.jsonl files but NO index DB. SQLitePlotIndex creates a fresh empty index file on first construction (does NOT throw), so query() returns rows=empty — no error — and the rebuild path is never hit. Result: /plots returns empty even when Plots exist on disk; /plots/:id 404s for the same reason because PlotResolver hits the same gated path. Discovered dogfooding plot-3e72876d (the housekeeping Plot) — invisible in /plots and /plots/plot-3e72876d after the warren project was refreshed in deployed warren. Reproduces locally too: delete .plot/.index.db files in any clone, call the /plots aggregator endpoint, get empty array. The mx-239786 record was titled 'cold-cache miss rebuild recovery' but the implementation only handled the error-throw case, not the empty-rows case. Tests at src/plots/aggregate.test.ts:269 pin the throw path; no test pins the empty-rows path — that is the gap. FIX SHAPE: in src/plots/aggregate.ts queryWithRebuildRetry, after the first successful query, if rows.length === 0 AND the .plot/ directory contains at least one non-dot non-index file (probe via fs.readdir filtered to *.json), call client.rebuildIndex() and re-query once before returning. Add a test to aggregate.test.ts mirroring the existing throw-retry test but pinning the empty-rows path: first query returns rows=[], the .plot/ directory probe sees a plot file, rebuildIndex is called once, second query returns the real row. The fs.readdir probe distinguishes 'index is stale, rebuild' from 'project legitimately has no plots, return empty' — without it, every empty-plots project pays a rebuild cost on every cache miss. ACCEPTANCE: (1) after a fresh refreshProjectClone on a hasPlot project whose .plot/ directory has *.json files but no .index.db, GET /plots returns the Plot summaries (was empty before fix); (2) GET /plots/:id resolves the same Plot (was 404 before); (3) a hasPlot project with .plot/ that contains zero *.json files returns empty without triggering a rebuild (zero rebuildCalls in the test); (4) the existing throw-path retry test at aggregate.test.ts:269 still passes unmodified; (5) new test pins the empty-rows + present-on-disk path; (6) bun test + bun run lint + bun run typecheck green with zero warnings. SCOPE: one file edit + one test. Do NOT bundle into the housekeeping plot-3e72876d arc — fix and ship as warren 0.4.4 ahead of housekeeping so dogfooding can proceed (warren-c106 already shipped as 0.4.3). Housekeeping then closes as 0.4.5.

title: Plot UX vision: surface the Plot→plan→seed→run flow end-to-end in the UI
description: VISION (filed as the dogfood signal from plot-3e72876d / the housekeeping pass): the Plot detail page should be the launchpad for all work bound to a Plot. Today the user must (a) navigate to /runs/new, (b) manually select project + agent + seed prompt, and (c) type the plot id by hand for every child seed — friction-heavy enough that for a 9-seed housekeeping arc the user described 'right now I can see the plot which is great, but now I need to manually go and trigger all these runs which isn't ideal.' The full vision is captured in the title: Plots become plans become seeds become runs, with the UI making that flow as easy as possible. Concrete shape: from PlotDetail with seeds_issue attachments, the user clicks one button and the housekeeping pass starts — N runs dispatched, each bound to plot_id, each appearing in the activity feed, optionally serial-gated on PR merge. Three child seeds: (1) per-seed Run button on PlotDetail; (2) batch Dispatch all attached seeds button on PlotDetail; (3) Plot→synthesized seeds plan→plan-run pipeline (cross-repo, needs seeds-side support for existing-seed children). Each child is independently shippable; we ship in order. Related: warren-bb22 (Plot discoverability, also dogfood signal #1), warren-ede7 (aggregator empty-rows, signal #2, shipped 0.4.4), the NewRun plot_id input prereq (will ship before this epic starts, as 0.4.5 or rolled into housekeeping). Out of scope here: anything that's not surfacing Plot-bound dispatch in the UI. Future Plot can be set up to track this epic itself once housekeeping closes.

title: PlotDetail: per-seeds_issue-attachment Run agent button
description: Step (1) of warren-e40a (Plot UX vision). On src/ui/src/pages/PlotDetail.tsx, in the SubstratePanel where seeds_issue attachments are rendered (currently a static row with detach button), add a small Run agent button next to each attachment. Click opens NewRun.tsx pre-filled with: project (from the Plot's owning project, resolved via PlotResolver), agent (the project default per .warren/defaults.json defaultRole), plot_id (this Plot's id), and prompt seeded from the seed's title + description via a project-default plot-run prompt template (or the .warren/defaults.json defaultPrompt with seed_id substitution). Pre-fill ALL of these — the user should be able to click Dispatch immediately without typing. The user can still edit any field before submitting. Implementation: pass query params or route state to NewRun, NewRun reads them on mount and sets initial form state. Test: click Run agent on a seeds_issue attachment, verify navigation to /runs/new with all four fields populated and a single Dispatch click creates a run that appears in the Plot's activity feed within 5s (the existing PlotDetail polling interval). Acceptance: (a) every seeds_issue attachment on PlotDetail renders a Run agent button, (b) clicking opens NewRun.tsx with project/agent/plot_id/prompt pre-filled, (c) the dispatched run lands in the Plot's activity feed within one poll tick, (d) detaching the attachment removes the button without re-render flicker, (e) no behavior change for non-seeds_issue attachments (mulch_record, canopy_prompt, etc. render unchanged). Depends on: the NewRun plot_id input prereq landing first. Parent: warren-e40a.

title: PlotDetail: batch Dispatch all attached seeds button
description: Step (2) of warren-e40a (Plot UX vision). On src/ui/src/pages/PlotDetail.tsx, add a Dispatch all attached seeds button to the page header (or to a dedicated 'Coordinate' section). Behavior: enumerates all seeds_issue attachments whose underlying seeds are still open (closed seeds skipped, matching plan-run resume semantics from pl-a258), then fires POST /runs for each one in parallel (default) or serial-gated-on-PR-merge (opt-in toggle). All dispatched runs are bound to this plot_id via the same path step (1) uses. Toggle UI: a checkbox 'Serial (gate next on prior PR merge)' next to the button, off by default. When serial mode is selected and the user clicks Dispatch all, warren creates ONE plan-run wrapping the open attachments (which is closer to what plan-runs already do but needs the seeds-side existing-seed-children support from step 3) OR — as a V1 fallback before step 3 lands — warren queues the runs internally and dispatches them in sequence as each prior PR merges. Confirm-dialog before firing N runs: 'Dispatch N runs against this Plot? Estimated cost:  (sum of per-run estimates).' Acceptance: (a) button visible whenever Plot has >=1 open seeds_issue attachment, (b) clicking (parallel mode) creates N runs all bound to plot_id, all visible in /runs and in this Plot's activity feed within one poll tick, (c) clicking (serial mode) creates 1 plan-run with N child runs, gated as in pl-a258, OR a stop-gap serial queue if step 3 hasn't shipped, (d) closed-seed attachments are skipped without spawning, (e) confirm-dialog blocks accidental fire. Depends on: step (1) landing first. Step (3) is a depends-on for the cleanest serial mode but a stop-gap is acceptable. Parent: warren-e40a.

title: Plot→synthesized seeds plan→plan-run pipeline (needs seeds-side support for existing-seed children)
description: Step (3) of warren-e40a (Plot UX vision) — the deepest 'Plots become plans become seeds become runs' realization. Today sd plan submit spawns NEW children; you can't make existing seeds children of a new plan. That blocks the cleanest Plot-as-orchestrator shape: a Plot's seeds_issue attachments synthesize into a seeds plan whose children ARE those attached seeds, then plan-run drives them with all the existing serial-gating, PR-merge tracking, and auto-done-on-final-merge semantics for free. Two-part work: (A) cross-repo seeds change — extend sd plan submit (or add sd plan from-existing) to accept an existing_seeds: [warren-X, warren-Y, ...] field. Plan children become references to those seeds, not new spawns. Validation: every existing seed must already exist in .seeds/issues.jsonl; closed seeds rejected (plan-run already skips closed children but the plan creation should be intentional). (B) warren-side — PlotDetail surfaces a Dispatch as plan-run button (in addition to step 2's batch button). Click: warren server synthesizes a plan via the new seeds API, calls POST /plan-runs against the synthesized plan with plot_id pre-filled, navigates to /plan-runs/:id. Reuses every existing pl-7937 (warren-06dc) wiring — plan_run_dispatched event on the Plot, per-child PLOT_ID/PLOT_ACTOR injection, auto-done transition when the final child merges. Acceptance: (a) cross-repo: seeds ships sd plan submit support for existing-seed children with a unit test; (b) cross-repo: warren consumes the new seeds version (double-pin) and exposes it via a new endpoint POST /plot-plan-runs (or similar); (c) PlotDetail's 'Dispatch as plan-run' button fires the pipeline end-to-end against plot-3e72876d-shaped Plots (10 seeds_issue attachments → 1 plan-run with 10 children → auto-done on final merge); (d) existing pl-7937 / pl-a258 flows unchanged (no regression in current plan-run dispatch). Depends on: step (1) and the seeds-side change. Parent: warren-e40a. Largest of the three steps.
closeReason: Adopted into pl-5310 as warren-a4b7 (step 4: Plot→synthesized seeds plan→plan-run pipeline, cross-repo). Continue execution on warren-a4b7; this seed remains closed as the historical filing.

title: NewRun + server: validate plot_id format and reject malformed at dispatch
description: Step (4) of warren-e40a (Plot UX vision). Dogfood signal #4 from plot-3e72876d: a run was dispatched via the new NewRun.tsx plot_id input with the input field containing the literal string 'plot_id=plot-3e72876d' (the user pasted the prose form including the key= prefix instead of just the id). The run row (run_4cemtf8chga5) shows plot_id='plot_id=plot-3e72876d' in supabase. The server accepted it without complaint, the host-side defaultPlotAppender (src/runs/spawn.ts) tried to append on a Plot resolved by that malformed id, the lookup quietly failed (caught and logged best-effort, no impact on the run), and the only user-visible signal is the run detail page's PlotMetaCardContent (src/ui/src/components/PlotMetaCardContent.tsx:52) rendering 'Plot no longer available' — long after dispatch, far from the input that caused it. FIX SHAPE: (A) CLIENT — in src/ui/src/pages/NewRun.tsx and src/ui/src/pages/NewPlanRun.tsx, validate the trimmed plot_id against /^plot-[a-z0-9]+$/ on submit; if non-empty and non-matching, show an inline error 'Plot ID must look like plot-xxxxxxxx' and block the Dispatch button. Apply to BOTH forms — NewPlanRun has the same risk. (B) SERVER — in src/server/handlers.ts on POST /runs (and POST /plan-runs), when plot_id is present, validate format via the same regex AND resolve the Plot via PlotResolver BEFORE the run row is inserted; reject with a typed error (extend the existing src/runs/errors.ts shape — code='plot_id_not_found' or 'plot_id_invalid', recoveryHint='Verify the Plot exists at /plots') and return 400. This makes the dispatch surface honest: a malformed or non-existent plot_id fails at the operator-facing edge, not silently at the appender. (C) Acceptance: (1) submitting plot_id='plot_id=plot-3e72876d' (the actual user input that caused this seed) shows the inline error and blocks Dispatch on the client; (2) bypassing the client (curl) with the same malformed string gets a 400 with code='plot_id_invalid'; (3) submitting plot_id='plot-XXXXXXXX' (well-formed but non-existent) gets a 400 with code='plot_id_not_found'; (4) submitting plot_id='plot-3e72876d' (well-formed and exists) succeeds as today; (5) submitting no plot_id at all is byte-identical to current behavior; (6) the existing best-effort appender logging path is unchanged (it only fires on success now); (7) unit tests pin all five cases; (8) bun test && bun run lint && bun run typecheck green with zero warnings. Parent: warren-e40a. Sibling: warren-ff2a (per-seed Run button — will use the same validation when pre-filling plot_id), warren-ea66 (batch Dispatch — same), warren-5561 (plan-run pipeline — server-side validation reused). No cross-repo dependency — single warren PR.

title: pi multi-provider: OPENAI_API_KEY (and other non-anthropic keys) not forwarded into sandbox
description:
## Symptom

Dispatching a pi run with `providerOverride: "openai"` (and `modelOverride: "gpt-4o"` or similar) composed the right argv (`pi --mode rpc --provider openai --model gpt-4o`), but the run failed on first API call because `OPENAI_API_KEY` was never forwarded into the burrow sandbox. Same for `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`.

End-user effect: the UI offered `provider/model` override inputs (NewRun.tsx, NewPlanRun.tsx, PlotDetail.tsx), `.env.example` documented the multi-provider keys, but the only provider that actually worked OOTB on pi was anthropic.

## Root cause (fixed in burrow v0.3.3)

`burrow/src/runtime/pi.ts:162` pinned `PI_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` to anthropic-only. The comment block at :155-160 explicitly rejected forwarding non-anthropic keys on the assumption that argv pins `--provider anthropic` — but warren's multi-provider surface (warren-f8c0, pl-4374) lets operators override the provider per run.

Fixed by burrow-6f3f (option 2): `AgentRuntime.envPassthrough` widened to `readonly string[] | ((ctx) => readonly string[])`; `piRuntime.envPassthrough = piEnvPassthrough` returns the anthropic triple plus the matching provider key from `PI_PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS` keyed off `frontmatter.provider`. The dispatcher's `applyRuntimeEnvPassthrough` re-invokes the function with the run's frontmatter and unions the delta onto the per-spawn `SandboxProfile.envPassthrough`. Non-pi runtimes (claude-code, sapling, codex) keep their static-array semantics — the widening is additive.

## Cross-repo PR links

**Burrow side (burrow-6f3f, all on `main` and shipped in v0.3.3):**

- `f2fef9e` fix(runtime): conditional envPassthrough by frontmatter.provider for pi (burrow-6f3f)
- `3df44f8` chore: release v0.3.3 — conditional envPassthrough by frontmatter.provider for pi (burrow-6f3f)
- Published to npm as `@os-eco/burrow-cli@0.3.3`

**Warren side:**

- Bump `@os-eco/burrow-cli` 0.3.2 → 0.3.3 (package.json + bun.lock + Dockerfile triple-pin per CLAUDE.md "Relationship to burrow")
- `scripts/acceptance/lib/burrow-with-stub.ts`: stub pi runtime swaps in `piEnvPassthrough` so the harness exercises the new function-form contract
- `scripts/acceptance/lib/stub-agent/pi-agent.sh`: emit `{"type":"env_keys_visible","keys":[...]}` at startup so scenarios can assert on what landed in the spawned env (collapses to `state_change` via pi parser's unknown-type fallthrough)
- `scripts/acceptance/scenarios/30-pi-multi-provider-env.ts`: new scenario — sets `OPENAI_API_KEY` in process.env, dispatches pi with `providerOverride='openai'`, waits for the `env_keys_visible` event and asserts `OPENAI_API_KEY` is in the list. Proves the warren↔burrow handoff (operator override → renderedAgentJson.frontmatter → burrow run metadata → dispatcher `readFrontmatter` → `piEnvPassthrough` → spawn env) is intact end-to-end.

Final warren quality gates after the bump: `bun test` 1777 pass / 0 fail; `tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun run lint` clean (342 files via biome).

## Closure gate — all conditions met

1. **burrow-6f3f is closed.** [met]
2. **Burrow ships a tagged release whose `piRuntime.envPassthrough` honors `frontmatter.provider`.** [met — v0.3.3 on npm]
3. **Warren bumps `@os-eco/burrow-cli` to that release in lockstep at all three pin sites.** [met — package.json + bun.lock + Dockerfile all on 0.3.3]
4. **Acceptance scenario 30 covers a pi+openai end-to-end and asserts the sandbox env contains OPENAI_API_KEY.** [met]
5. **Cross-repo PR links recorded back into this seed before closure.** [met — above]

## References

- `burrow/src/runtime/pi.ts:162-218` — `PI_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` + `PI_PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS` + `piEnvPassthrough`
- `burrow/src/runner/dispatch.ts:432` — `applyRuntimeEnvPassthrough`

title: V2 Plot-workbench roadmap: warm sandboxes, native diff/review UI, webhook-triggered Plots, cross-Plot references, plot.conflict UI
description:
Roadmap of Plot-workbench directions deferred from V1+V1.5 (pl-0344). Revisit once V1 has shipped and adoption signals show which of these is highest-leverage.

## V2 candidates

1. **Warm interactive sandboxes (with hibernation).** Replace respawn-per-turn with long-lived burrow containers that suspend to disk after N seconds idle. Preserves agent in-memory scout state across turns — eliminates the per-turn cold start and inconsistent-reasoning risk flagged in pl-0344 risks. Requires deep burrow contract change: idle-aware reaper, hibernation primitive, resource accounting. Priority depends on whether V1 interactive runs feel snappy enough.

2. **Native diff/review UI in warren.** Diff viewer, comment threads, approval UI, mergeable state machine — all in warren. Eliminates the GitHub context switch entirely (V1.5 click-to-merge still sends users to github.com for review). Months of work; only worth doing if users complain that review is the remaining friction after V1.5.

3. **Webhook-triggered Plot creation.** GitHub issue labeled 'plot' (or comment posted) → warren auto-creates a Plot with the issue attached. Strong adoption vector for teams already living in GitHub Issues. Couples to SPEC §11.I V2 trigger work that's also deferred — bundle these together.

4. **Cross-Plot references.** A Plot can link to another Plot ('this Plot supersedes pl-foo', 'depends on outcome of pl-bar'). Enables Plot-of-Plots patterns and meta-coordination across long-running initiatives. Not modeled in plot v1; needs spec work first.

5. **plot.conflict UI surfacing.** Today warren emits plot.conflict events when concurrent runs write conflicting .plot/<id>.json full-doc state; UI is silent. Surface conflict state on the Plot with a 'refresh & retry' affordance. Small; could pull forward into V1.5 if it bites in practice.

6. **True burrow pause/resume primitive (in-memory state preserved).** Replaces V1's timeout-respawn-with-state-lost mechanism for blocking question_posed. Cleaner UX (agent retains scout progress across human delay) but requires burrow-side hibernation. Likely lands together with warm sandboxes (#1).

7. **Plot summary export formats.** /plots/:id/summary in V1.5 is HTML; V2 adds Markdown export (for sharing in chat/issues), PDF export (for records), and JSON export (for programmatic post-processing). Cheap once the summary endpoint exists.

8. **Interactive run sub-types beyond brainstorm/planner.** PR review chat (agent loaded with PR diff + Plot context), debug-with-agent (agent loaded with failing test + recent runs), retro chat (agent loaded with done Plot's full event log, helps the user extract lessons → mulch records). Each is a new agent config, no new primitive — natural extensions once the chat surface exists.

## Sequencing intuition

Of these, #1 (warm sandboxes) and #5 (plot.conflict UI) have the clearest 'this is annoying' adoption signal that V1 will surface. #3 (webhooks) and #2 (native review) are bigger asks that need their own plan-of-plans once V1 is in users' hands. #4 (cross-Plot refs) needs spec work in the plot project first. #8 (new interactive sub-types) is opportunistic — pick one when a real user need surfaces.

Do not plan this seed via sd plan submit yet. Pick a candidate, file it as its own feature seed with its own plan when V1 adoption justifies it.
