title: Stop forwarding raw Error.message on unhandled 500s (src/server/errors.ts:85-90)
description:
Step 1 of pl-b82d (phase 0 — security). Prerequisite for the response-projection work in steps 14-16: as long as any handler can emit a raw Error.message, projecting the happy path is pointless.

PROBLEM
`src/server/errors.ts:85-90` forwards `error.message` verbatim on any unhandled 500. Subprocess stderr, filesystem paths, and driver strings escape from EVERY route, including ones that will be anonymous. `src/server/handlers/projects.ts:100-102` already concedes in-comment that `SeedsCliError` bubbles out this way.

SCOPE
- `src/server/errors.ts` — split the response body from the log record. Known/typed application errors (ValidationError, NotFoundError, ProjectLacksSeedsError, and friends) keep their message; anything else returns a generic message plus a correlation id.
- Emit the full error (message + stack) to the pino logger at error level with that same correlation id, so operators lose nothing. `src/server/main/redact.ts` already covers the log side.
- Audit every `throw` reachable from a handler for typed-vs-untyped classification; grep `src/server/handlers/` for raw `throw new Error(`.
- Update `src/server/__golden__/responses/*` fixtures whose bodies change, and `responses.golden.test.ts`.

ACCEPTANCE
- A handler throwing an untyped Error returns a body containing no filesystem path, no subprocess output, and no driver text — only a generic message and a correlation id.
- The same request logs the full message and stack, findable by correlation id.
- Typed application errors are unchanged in body and status.
- New test asserts an untyped throw does not leak `process.cwd()` or a `/data/` path into the response.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Remove secret-adjacent disclosure from /readyz and /metrics diagnostics payloads
description:
Step 2 of pl-b82d (phase 0 — security). A live disclosure on the current deployment, independent of any public demo.

PROBLEM
- `src/diagnostics/checks-preview.ts:151` publishes **`WARREN_API_TOKEN.length`** in the `/readyz` payload. Token length is a real search-space reduction and there is no reason to expose it.
- `src/diagnostics/checks-config.ts:269-279` surfaces raw DB driver errors including host, port and user.
- The payload also carries server filesystem paths and project ids.

SCOPE
- `src/diagnostics/checks-preview.ts` — replace the length disclosure with a boolean `configured: true|false`.
- `src/diagnostics/checks-config.ts` — classify driver errors into a fixed set of reasons (`unreachable`, `auth_failed`, `migration_pending`, `unknown`); log the raw text, never return it.
- Sweep the rest of `src/diagnostics/` for absolute paths in check details; return basenames or a boolean.
- `src/server/handlers/diagnostics.ts` and `src/server/handlers/metrics.ts` stay auth-gated — do NOT add them to `isAuthExempt` (`src/server/handlers/index.ts:330-347`). Step 13 will hard-block both for anonymous callers; this step reduces the blast radius for an operator-token holder and for anyone who later relaxes the gate.
- Update golden fixtures under `src/server/__golden__/responses/`.

ACCEPTANCE
- `/readyz` contains no token length, no DB host/port/user, and no absolute filesystem path.
- Operator diagnostic value is preserved: each degraded check still names what is wrong via a stable reason code.
- Test asserts the `/readyz` body does not match `/[0-9]{2,}/` for the token check and contains no `/data/` substring.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Stop embedding the bearer token in preview-login URLs (client.ts buildPreviewLoginUrl, RunDetail href)
description:
Step 3 of pl-b82d (phase 0 — security).

PROBLEM
`src/ui/src/api/client.ts:288-292` (`buildPreviewLoginUrl`) embeds the raw bearer token in a URL query string. It is rendered as a clickable `<a href>` at `src/ui/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx:409` and `:435-445`. Tokens in URLs land in browser history, `Referer` headers, and any proxy or analytics log in the path. On a public instance this must never render at all; on the private instance it is already a leak.

SCOPE
- Replace the query-string handshake with a POST that sets the preview session cookie server-side, or a short-lived single-use handoff token minted by the server and distinct from `WARREN_API_TOKEN`.
- Server side lives behind the preview-login exemption regex in `src/server/handlers/index.ts:330-347` — keep the exemption narrow and update it to match the new shape.
- `src/ui/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx:409,435-445` — the affordance becomes a button, not an href.
- Check `src/preview/` for any other place the token is threaded into a URL.

ACCEPTANCE
- No code path places `WARREN_API_TOKEN` (or any bearer) into a URL, query string, or `href`.
- Preview login still works end to end against a live preview.
- Test asserts `buildPreviewLoginUrl` (or its replacement) returns a URL whose query string contains no token-shaped value.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Cap concurrent event-stream connections on GET /runs/:id/events (idleTimeout:0 + single replica DoS)
description:
Step 4 of pl-b82d (phase 0 — security/availability).

PROBLEM
`src/server/server.ts:55` sets `idleTimeout: 0` server-wide so long-lived NDJSON event streams survive quiet stretches. Combined with a single-replica control plane (`deploy/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:18-23`, `strategy: Recreate`, no horizontal scaling available because of SSE stickiness and an RWO PVC) and no connection cap anywhere, `GET /runs/:id/events?follow=1` is an unbounded connection-exhaustion vector. A Show HN spike hits this even without malice.

SCOPE
- Add a global and per-IP concurrent-stream cap enforced where streams are established — `src/server/handlers/runs/events.ts:25` and the plan-run twin at `src/server/handlers/plan-runs.ts:316`. Over the cap returns 503 with `Retry-After`, not a hang.
- Make the caps env-tunable with sane defaults (suggest global 200, per-IP 5) and document them in `.env.example`.
- `src/runs/events.ts` `RunEventBroker.subscriberCount(runId)` already exists — reuse it rather than adding a parallel counter where possible.
- Consider a per-connection max lifetime so a wedged client cannot hold a slot forever.
- Emit a metric for current stream count so `/metrics` shows saturation.

ACCEPTANCE
- Exceeding the per-IP cap returns 503 + `Retry-After`; existing streams are unaffected.
- Exceeding the global cap does the same and logs at warn.
- Caps are configurable via env with documented defaults.
- Test opens N+1 streams and asserts the last is rejected and the first N still deliver events.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Add scripts/version-bump.ts porting burrow's, extended to README status line, openapi regen, and a drafted [Unreleased] section
description:
Step 5 of pl-b82d (phase B1 — release machinery).

CONTEXT
CLAUDE.md:290-291 and `.claude/commands/release.md:14` both state there is no `version:bump` script here. Burrow has one — `/Users/jayminwest/Projects/os-eco/burrow/scripts/version-bump.ts`, 62 lines, atomic two-file rewrite with rollback on failure at `:50`. Port it and extend.

SCOPE
- New `scripts/version-bump.ts` + `"version:bump"` in package.json. Accepts `major|minor|patch|<explicit>`.
- Rewrites, atomically: `package.json` `version`, `src/index.ts` `export const VERSION`.
- Runs `bun run gen:openapi` so `docs/openapi.yaml:6` (auto-derived from package.json by `scripts/generate-openapi.ts:169-173`) stays synced.
- Rewrites the README status line — currently `README.md:38` reads `Stable (0.9.10)` against an actual 0.10.1.
- Drafts a `[Unreleased]` section into CHANGELOG.md from `git log <last-tag>..HEAD` PR titles, clearly marked as a draft for a human to edit down. **Assistive only — this is not enforcement.** Per the plan's alternatives, CHANGELOG curation stays human and there is no per-PR CI gate.
- Prints exact next steps (commit, push, what will fire).
- Co-located test, following burrow's.
- Delete the "there is no version:bump" claims from CLAUDE.md:290-291 and `.claude/commands/release.md:14`.

ACCEPTANCE
- `bun run version:bump patch` updates all four version sites and leaves a draft CHANGELOG section.
- A failure partway through rolls back cleanly (burrow's `:50` pattern).
- No CI or PR gate is added by this step.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Add check:version-sync gate covering package.json, src/index.ts, docs/openapi.yaml and the README status line
description:
Step 6 of pl-b82d (phase B1). Blocked on step 5 (warren-16b5).

PROBLEM
Version lives in five places. `release.yml:46-54` verifies only `package.json` vs `src/index.ts` — and only at release time, on the release branch. README has drifted two releases (`README.md:38` says 0.9.10, actual 0.10.1) and `docs/openapi.yaml` drift is invisible because CI does not run `gen:openapi:check` (step 7 fixes that half).

SCOPE
- New `scripts/check-version-sync.ts` asserting agreement across: `package.json` `version`, `src/index.ts` `VERSION`, `docs/openapi.yaml` `info.version`, and the README status line.
- Also assert the burrow-cli pin agrees between `README.md:75` and `Dockerfile:93` — they currently disagree (0.3.12 vs 0.3.15). Same class of drift, same script.

Note `scripts/check-all.ts` is byte-identical to `templates/l5-toolkit/scripts/check-all.ts` and must NOT be edited — per CLAUDE.md all per-repo variation comes from package.json, filtered against the frozen canonical gate order. If the canonical order has no slot for this gate, fold the assertions into an existing gate rather than editing the frozen script.

ACCEPTANCE

title: Add gen:docs:check and gen:openapi:check to ci.yml, and make check:ci-parity bidirectional
description:
Step 7 of pl-b82d (phase B1).

PROBLEM
`gen:docs:check` and `gen:openapi:check` are in the `check:all` GATES manifest (`scripts/check-all.ts:46-47`) and defined in package.json, but `.github/workflows/ci.yml` never invokes them. `check:ci-parity` cannot catch this because `scripts/check-ci-parity.ts` is ONE-DIRECTIONAL: it only asserts that scripts CI does run are reachable from `check:all`, never that every manifest gate is present in CI. Net effect — `docs/openapi.yaml` drift is invisible to CI, and gates can silently vanish from CI without tripping anything.

SCOPE
- Add `gen:docs:check` and `gen:openapi:check` steps to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (after line 22).
- Make `check:ci-parity` bidirectional: every gate in `GATES` must be transitively reachable from some CI step, with the existing `scripts/ci-parity-config.json` `ciOnly` list gaining a documented inverse (`localOnly`) for any gate deliberately excluded from CI. Justify every entry in the config's `$comment`, per CLAUDE.md.
- CONSTRAINT: `scripts/check-ci-parity.ts` is byte-identical to `templates/l5-toolkit/scripts/check-ci-parity.ts` and exempt from Biome formatting to preserve that. Changing it means changing the l5-toolkit template too and keeping both byte-identical — coordinate that, or express the new assertion in `ci-parity-config.json` if the frozen script already supports it.

ACCEPTANCE
- Deleting a gate step from `ci.yml` fails `check:ci-parity`.
- `ci.yml` runs both generated-artifact checks.
- Frozen scripts stay byte-identical to their l5-toolkit counterparts.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Publish the warren control-plane image to ghcr.io with semver tags threaded through workflow_call
description:
Step 8 of pl-b82d (phase B1). The single biggest unlock for the public story — today the "one container, 5-minute self-host" claim is false because `docker-compose.yml:21-25` builds from source.

PROBLEM
Nothing publishes to a public registry. `deploy-gke.yml:92-129` builds three images to a PRIVATE GCP Artifact Registry, tagged `:$SHA` and `:latest` only — never semver. `npm view @os-eco/warren-cli` 404s and stays that way (mulch mx-834a3a: container-only distribution is deliberate; see the plan's alternatives).

SCOPE
- `.github/workflows/deploy-gke.yml` `build-push` job: add `permissions: packages: write`, a second `docker/login-action` step for `ghcr.io` using `${{ github.actor }}` + `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` (no new secret provisioning), and `ghcr.io/jayminwest/warren` tags on the control-plane image step.
- Thread a `version` input through `workflow_call` — `release.yml` already has it as `steps.version-check.outputs.version` — and tag `:vX.Y.Z` and `:X.Y` alongside `:$SHA` and `:latest`. Without semver tags self-hosters can only pin a SHA or ride `latest`.
- Only the control-plane image needs GHCR; `warren-agent` and `warren-workspace-init` only ever run on GKE and can stay in Artifact Registry.
- Flip `docker-compose.yml` to `image: ghcr.io/jayminwest/warren:<tag>` with the `build:` block retained as a commented fallback for contributors.
- Make the package public on first publish.

OUT OF SCOPE
Multi-arch. `deploy-gke.yml:88-91` pins `linux/amd64` with a comment that Autopilot CrashLoops on arm64. A manifest list would solve it correctly but costs QEMU build time; file a follow-up seed rather than doing it here.

ACCEPTANCE
- A release publishes `ghcr.io/jayminwest/warren` tagged with the SHA, `latest`, `vX.Y.Z` and `X.Y`.
- `docker compose up` on a fresh clone pulls rather than builds.
- The package is publicly pullable without auth.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Harden the release job: run check:all, hard-fail a missing CHANGELOG section, drop the double build and the k8s-migration deploy branch, add a post-deploy /version smoke test
description:
Step 9 of pl-b82d (phase B1). Blocked on step 8 (warren-26be).

SCOPE — four fixes in `.github/workflows/`:

1. **Release runs the real gate suite.** `release.yml:28-31` runs only install/lint/typecheck/test — 4 of 12 gates. `ci.yml:19-32` runs 12. Replace with `bun run ui:install && bun run check:all` so a release cannot ship code CI would have rejected.

2. **Missing CHANGELOG section becomes a hard failure.** `release.yml:73-106` awk-scans for `## [$VERSION]` and on miss silently falls back to `--generate-notes` (`:98-106`). Make the miss exit non-zero. This is the ONLY changelog enforcement in the plan — deliberately at release time, not in PR CI (see alternatives).

3. **Kill the double build and the dead deploy branch.** `deploy-gke.yml:24-28` fires on `push: main` AND is called via `workflow_call` from `release.yml:114-124`, so every release builds twice (serialized by the `gke-build-deploy-${{ github.ref }}` concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: false`). Drop `push: main` and let `release.yml` be the only builder. Also delete the `k8s-migration` entries at `:28` and `:137-139` — that branch merged in v0.10.0 and anyone pushing it currently deploys prod. Delete the stale remote branch too.

4. **Post-deploy smoke test.** After the existing image-SHA verification (`deploy-gke.yml:254-267`), curl the ingress `/version` and assert it equals the released semver. `README.md:90` already describes `/version` as the rollout-confirmation endpoint; nothing uses it.

TRAPS — do not break these:
- `release.yml`'s `deploy` job MUST stay a `workflow_call`, never a `release: [published]` trigger. GitHub suppresses workflow runs from GITHUB_TOKEN-authored events (warren-cb81). `scripts/deploy-trigger.test.ts:32-59` asserts this and will fail if "simplified".
- `deploy-gke.yml:210-216` — the Ingress JSON6902 surgical replace exists because a strategic merge on `spec.rules` drops `http.paths` and 404s every API path. Do not refactor it.
- `deploy-gke.yml:185` hardcodes `warren` as the AR repo segment in the kustomize image-match key, so `vars.GCP_AR_REPO` set to anything else silently deploys the wrong image. Fix while here.
- `AUTO_MERGE_PAT` is a silent single point of failure: GitHub suppresses runs from GITHUB_TOKEN-authored pushes, so PAT expiry stops releases with no failed run. Add an expiry check or heartbeat.

ACCEPTANCE
- Releasing with no CHANGELOG section fails loudly.
- One build per release; `k8s-migration` cannot deploy.
- `scripts/deploy-trigger.test.ts` still passes.
- Post-deploy `/version` mismatch fails the workflow.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: CHECKPOINT: split the CHANGELOG archive, backfill [Unreleased] from the 16 unreleased PRs, and cut v0.11.0 through the new machinery
description:
Step 10 of pl-b82d — **RELEASE CHECKPOINT**. Blocked on steps 5-9. Proves the new machinery by using it.

STATE TODAY
`CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` (line 8) is empty while 16 merged PRs sit unreleased since v0.10.1 — the entire conversations deletion (#616-#620), the entire plot deletion (#621, #622, #626/#627, #628, #632), plus K8s fixes (#625 pod-watcher zombie reconcile, #631 auto-plan-run seed loss, #629 release→deploy trigger, #630 trivial-merge scoring). Zero of those PRs touched CHANGELOG.md. The file is 250 KB / 4,743 lines — the second-largest in the repo and itself Show-HN clutter.

- CHANGELOG.md is under ~40 KB.

title: Widen AuthOk into a capability-carrying Actor and thread it through RouteContext (pure refactor, no behavior change)
description:
Step 11 of pl-b82d (phase A — public instance). The critical path to Aug 16 starts here. **Pure refactor: no behavior change, no new capability.**

WHY THIS SHAPE
PHILOSOPHY.md:67 already lists `AuthProvider` as a planned seam with `token` + `github` implementations; sequencing step 4 pays for it with the GitHub App. The public demo is a real feature arriving early and paying for the same seam (rule 1: features pay for seams). Rule 7 ("capabilities, not conditionals") forbids the obvious alternative — a `WARREN_READ_ONLY` boolean — and rule 3 says `ServerDeps` only shrinks, so nothing here adds a dep field.

STATE TODAY
`src/server/types.ts:331-333` — `AuthProvider { authorize(request: Request): AuthOutcome }`. `AuthOutcome = AuthOk | AuthDenied` where `AuthOk` is literally `{ readonly ok: true }` (`types.ts:318-320`) — no actor, no scope, no capability. Two impls in `src/server/auth.ts`: `NoAuthProvider` (`:25-29`) and `BearerTokenAuth` (`:31-65`), resolved by `resolveAuth()` (`:91-101`), wired at `src/server/server.ts:222-227` and `src/server/main/index.ts:377`.

Note `authorize()` receives the full `Request`, so method + path policy is expressible today — but it runs BEFORE `matchRoute` (`server.ts:222-227`), so it has no route pattern or params, and nothing it returns reaches handlers.

SCOPE
- Widen `AuthOk` to `{ ok: true, actor: Actor }` where `Actor` carries an identity discriminant and a capability set (suggest `readPublic`, `readOperator`, `dispatch`, `admin` — name them for what they permit, not who holds them).
- Thread the actor into `RouteContext` (`src/server/server.ts:229-235`) so handlers can consult it.
- Both existing providers return a full-capability actor. **Behavior is byte-identical after this step** — `NoAuthProvider` and `BearerTokenAuth` grant everything they grant today.
- Do not add fields to `ServerDeps`.
- Follow the `RuntimeProvider` house style (`src/runtime/contract.ts`, `src/runtime/registry.ts`): provider-neutral DTOs, capability flags, fail-loud on unknown selection.

ACCEPTANCE
- Every existing auth test passes unchanged.
- Golden response fixtures unchanged.
- `RouteContext` exposes the actor; no handler consults it yet.
- `ServerDeps` field count is unchanged (28).
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Add PublicReadProvider as the third AuthProvider impl behind a WARREN_AUTH boot-resolved registry, fail-closed on absent config
description:
Step 12 of pl-b82d (phase A). Blocked on step 11 (warren-1ff0). Unblocks steps 13-18.

SCOPE
- New `PublicReadProvider` in `src/server/auth.ts` (or `src/auth/` if the seam warrants its own directory — PHILOSOPHY.md:67 names `src/auth/contract.ts` as the eventual home; splitting now is fine and cheap).
- Grants an anonymous actor with only the `readPublic` capability. Every other capability is absent, so mutations fail at the policy layer in step 13 rather than inside handlers.
- Boot-resolved registry keyed on `WARREN_AUTH` (`token` | `public`), resolved once at boot exactly like `WARREN_RUNTIME` in `src/runtime/registry.ts`, with a fail-loud `UnknownAuthProviderError` on an unrecognized value. `token` stays the default so the fresh-install path is untouched.
- **Fail closed, always.** `resolveAuth()` (`src/server/auth.ts:91-101`) already throws when no token is set — preserve that. A missing, empty, or unparseable `WARREN_AUTH` must resolve to `token`, never to `public`. Registering a private repo on an instance that silently degraded to public is the worst outcome this plan can produce; assert it in a test.
- `public` mode still accepts an operator bearer token — a token holder gets the full-capability actor, an anonymous caller gets `readPublic`. That is what makes one deployment serve both spectators and the operator.
- Document `WARREN_AUTH` in `.env.example` with an explicit warning about what `public` exposes.

ACCEPTANCE
- `WARREN_AUTH` unset or invalid → `token` provider, existing behavior, no anonymous access.
- `WARREN_AUTH=public` + no `Authorization` header → actor with `readPublic` only.
- `WARREN_AUTH=public` + valid bearer → full-capability actor.
- `WARREN_AUTH=nonsense` → boot fails loudly.
- Test asserts every degenerate config value fails closed.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Classify all 39 ROUTE_TABLE entries into a declarative public-read policy table, hard-blocking inbox, finalize-intent, readyz, metrics, analytics/cost, triggers and warren-config
description:
Step 13 of pl-b82d (phase A). Blocked on steps 2 (warren-51de) and 12 (warren-851b).

SCOPE
Add a declarative policy to `ROUTE_TABLE` (`src/server/handlers/index.ts:200-263`, 39 entries / 36 unique paths) mapping each route to the capability it requires. Enforce it in one place — `handleRequest` in `src/server/server.ts:190-227`, the single chokepoint every request passes through. Exhaustive: a route with no policy entry must fail the build, not default to open.

PUBLIC-READ (capability `readPublic`) — the demo surface:
`GET /healthz`, `GET /version`, `GET /runs`, `GET /runs/:id`, `GET /runs/:id/events`, `GET /projects`, `GET /projects/:id`, `GET /agents`, `GET /agents/:name`, `GET /plan-runs`, `GET /plan-runs/:id`, `GET /plan-runs/:id/events`, `GET /analytics/runs`. All of these still require the projections from steps 14-16 before they are actually safe.

HARD-BLOCKED for anonymous callers:
- `GET /readyz` — even after step 2, it is operator diagnostics.
- `GET /metrics` — `handlers/metrics.ts:35-72` exposes cumulative `warren_cost_usd` and full operational shape. Note it was deliberately un-exempted from auth for warren-682a; keep it that way.
- `GET /analytics/cost` — per-run USD rollups (`runs/lifecycle.ts:122-164`). Per-run cost IS shown on run detail by deliberate choice; the analytics rollup is not.
- **`GET /runs/:id/inbox` — DESTRUCTIVE ON READ.** `src/runs/pause-resume.ts:67-83` atomically flips unread→delivered. Anonymous access would silently drain steering queues: an availability bug, not a leak. Assert this specifically in a test.
- `GET /runs/:id/finalize-intent` — machine-to-machine pod callback carrying branch/commit/push instructions; pollable to race the pod.
- `GET /projects/:id/triggers`, `GET /projects/:id/warren-config` — trigger prompt text, `qualityGate` executable command strings, admission caps (`src/triggers/summary.ts:28-40`).
- `GET /preview/config` — discloses `WARREN_PREVIEW_HOST`. Borderline; block it.
- **Every POST and DELETE** (16 routes) — this is the "minus dispatch" half of the product scope.

SCOPE NOTES
- Reconcile with `isAuthExempt` (`src/server/handlers/index.ts:330-347`) — `/healthz`, `/version`, the preview-login regex, and non-API paths. The policy table should subsume it rather than duplicate it.
- Non-API paths (SPA shell + assets) must keep loading anonymously.
- Regenerate `docs/openapi.yaml` and `docs/http-api.md` if the route metadata shape changes.

ACCEPTANCE
- A route added to `ROUTE_TABLE` without a policy entry fails typecheck or a gate.
- Anonymous requests to every hard-blocked route return 403 (or 401), asserted per route.
- Anonymous POST/DELETE returns 403 on all 16 routes.
- Dedicated test asserts `GET /runs/:id/inbox` anonymously does not mutate inbox state.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Add public projections for GET /runs and GET /runs/:id: drop renderedAgentJson, burrowId, previewFailureMessage and the instance-wide cost rollup; keep prompt and per-run cost
description:
Step 14 of pl-b82d (phase A). Blocked on steps 1 (warren-4385) and 12 (warren-851b). This and steps 15-16 are the real work — there is NO prior art for response projection in this codebase; `src/server/main/redact.ts` is pino log redaction only and has never touched an HTTP body.

PROBLEM
`GET /runs` (`src/runs/lifecycle.ts:65-100`) returns the full `RunRow` plus a top-level `costTotalUsd`. `GET /runs/:id` (`:102-111`) returns the same row unwrapped.

PROJECTION FOR `readPublic` — drop:
- `renderedAgentJson` — the complete rendered system prompt. This is prompt-engineering IP and pure noise for a spectator.
- `burrowId` / `burrowRunId` — internal sandbox handles; also render as empty "—" cards on the K8s instance today.
- `previewFailureMessage` — free-text, can carry subprocess output.
- top-level `costTotalUsd` — an instance-wide all-time number that becomes a headline out of context. The aggregate belongs in a deliberately framed ledger view, not an unlabeled field on a list endpoint.

DELIBERATELY KEPT:
- `prompt` — the user prompt is the interesting half of the demo ("here's what we asked, here's what it did").
- per-run `costUsd` and token counts — cost-per-merged-PR is the campaign's ownable metric, this is os-eco's own spend on public repos, and hiding per-run cost while publishing a ledger reads as inconsistent.
- state, failureReason, agent, project, seedId, branch, prUrl, timestamps, duration.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
- Build the projection as an explicit allowlist ("pick these fields"), never a denylist. A denylist leaks every field added later, which is exactly the failure mode this plan exists to prevent.
- Put the projection next to the route handler's response construction, and derive the operator response from the same source so the two cannot drift.
- Coordinate the field list with steps 15 and 16 so all three projections share one mechanism.

ACCEPTANCE
- Anonymous `GET /runs` and `GET /runs/:id` bodies contain none of the dropped fields and all of the kept ones.
- An operator-token request is byte-identical to today.
- Test enumerates the projected field set explicitly, so adding a `RunRow` field fails the test until it is classified.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Add public projections for GET /projects, GET /agents, GET /agents/:name and GET /analytics/runs: drop localPath, renderedJson and resolvedFrom
description:
Step 15 of pl-b82d (phase A). Blocked on step 12 (warren-851b). Same mechanism as step 14 — coordinate the shared projection helper.

PROJECTIONS FOR `readPublic`:

`GET /projects`, `GET /projects/:id` — drop `localPath` (server filesystem paths, `src/db/repos/projects.ts:51-62`; also rendered in the UI at `ProjectDetail.tsx:96`). Keep `gitUrl` (public repos only, enforced by step 17), name, `hasSeeds`, timestamps.

`GET /agents`, `GET /agents/:name` — drop `renderedJson` entirely (contains `sections.system`, i.e. the full system prompt, and `sections.burrow_config`) and `resolvedFrom` (source paths). Keep name, description, provider, model, source tier. Note `pages/Agents.tsx:421-441` currently renders the full system prompt in the UI — step 19 must hide that panel for anonymous callers.

`GET /analytics/runs` — drop `topSeedsByContext` and aggregate USD. This endpoint is public-read per step 13 but only for run-count/state distribution; if that leaves it uninteresting, consider hard-blocking it instead and say so.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES

- Reuse whatever helper step 14 lands; if step 14 has not merged, build it here and have step 14 adopt it.

ACCEPTANCE

- Operator responses unchanged.
- Field-enumerating tests as in step 14.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Add a secret scrubber and public projection for the run event stream (events.payload_json raw agent transcripts)
description:
Step 16 of pl-b82d (phase A). Blocked on step 12 (warren-851b). **The highest-risk step in the plan** — and the one that makes the demo worth watching. Without the live event stream the demo is a table of rows.

PROBLEM
`events.payload_json` (`src/db/schema/sqlite.ts:240`) is the raw agent transcript: `tool_use` inputs including shell command lines, `tool_result` outputs including file contents and stack traces. It is served as NDJSON from `GET /runs/:id/events` (`src/server/handlers/runs/events.ts:25`) and the plan-run twin (`handlers/plan-runs.ts:316`), rendered unredacted in the UI via `JSON.stringify(event.payload)` at `RunDetail.tsx:783-785,800-802`.

SCOPE
- A secret scrubber applied to the event projection for `readPublic` callers. Known key shapes at minimum: `sk-ant-`, `sk-`, `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghs_`, `github_pat_`, `AKIA`, `ASIA`, `xoxb-`/`xoxp-`, PEM blocks, `Authorization: Bearer <...>`, and any value matching a name in the instance's own secret env set. Replace with a visible `[redacted]` marker rather than deleting, so a viewer can tell scrubbing happened.
- Scrub the NDJSON projection server-side, not in the UI. The stream is the API (PHILOSOPHY rule 5); anything relying on client-side redaction is not redacted.
- Drop or project any event kind that is purely internal (finalize-intent plumbing, inbox delivery).
- The scrubber must be cheap — it runs per event on a live stream on a single-replica control plane.
- Co-located test with a fixture corpus of real-shaped payloads.

RESIDUAL RISK, EXPLICITLY ACCEPTED

FALLBACK IF CONFIDENCE IS LOW

title: Enforce a public-instance org allowlist: refuse to register non-allowlisted orgs at boot and at POST /projects when public mode is on
description:
Step 17 of pl-b82d (phase A). Blocked on step 12 (warren-851b). This is the STRUCTURAL mitigation that makes steps 14-16 tolerable: if only public repos can ever be on the instance, a redaction miss exposes already-public content.

PROBLEM
A misconfigured public instance that registers a private repo is the worst outcome this plan can produce. Nothing prevents it today — `POST /projects` accepts any `gitUrl` (`src/server/handlers/projects.ts:35-50`, `src/projects/manage.ts:73-104`).

SCOPE
- New config (suggest `WARREN_PUBLIC_ORG_ALLOWLIST`) consulted only when `WARREN_AUTH=public`.
- Enforce at BOOT: if public mode is on and any already-registered project falls outside the allowlist, refuse to start with a message naming the offending projects. Do not silently continue.
- Enforce at REGISTRATION: `POST /projects` rejects a non-allowlisted org with a clear 400.
- Consider also asserting the repo is actually public via the forge, not just that its org is allowlisted — an allowlisted org can still hold private repos. If that requires a network call at registration, note the tradeoff and pick one.
- Fail closed: public mode with an EMPTY or absent allowlist must refuse to boot, not allow everything.
- Note `src/projects/manage.ts:78-82` — registration is not idempotent (existing project throws `ValidationError`) and a pre-existing clone directory makes it refuse. Step 22's re-registration script has to handle both.

ACCEPTANCE
- Public mode + a non-allowlisted registered project → boot fails, naming it.
- Public mode + empty allowlist → boot fails.
- `POST /projects` with a non-allowlisted org → 400, nothing cloned.
- Token mode is entirely unaffected.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Attach a Cloud Armor security policy and BackendConfig to the GKE Ingress for L3/L7 abuse control
description:
Step 20 of pl-b82d (phase A — infra). No application code.

WHY
No HTTP rate limiting exists anywhere in warren (the 36 grep hits are K8s dispatch admission caps in `src/runtime/k8s/admission.ts` and the scheduler's per-project notice throttle in `src/triggers/tick.ts:90` — neither is a per-IP gate). Cloud Armor is the right layer for a Show HN spike: it needs no code, handles L3/L7 volumetric abuse the app cannot, and does not consume the single-replica control plane's CPU. In-app limiting stays scoped to the expensive endpoint (step 4's stream cap).

CONSTRAINT
Cloudflare DNS for `app.warren.run` must stay DNS-only / grey-cloud — Google's HTTP-01 ManagedCertificate validation fails behind Cloudflare's proxy (`deploy/k8s/overlays/gke/managedcertificate.yaml:11-12`). So Cloudflare gives no WAF or rate limiting, which is exactly why Cloud Armor is needed.

SCOPE
- Cloud Armor security policy: per-IP rate limiting with a sane threshold, a ban duration, and preconfigured WAF rules where they do not false-positive on an API.
- `BackendConfig` referencing the policy, attached to the Service consumed by the GCE Ingress. Add it to `deploy/k8s/overlays/gke/` alongside `frontendconfig.yaml` and `managedcertificate.yaml`, and wire it into the overlay `kustomization.yaml`.
- Note the deploy pipeline regenerates the gitignored `gke-live` overlay in CI from repo vars (`deploy-gke.yml:171-239`) — the committed `gke/` overlay is the template, so the policy must live there.
- Document the thresholds and the kill switch in `docs/RUNBOOK-K8S.md`.
- Set a budget alert on the GCP project; the instance holds live `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `warren-secrets`.

ACCEPTANCE
- Policy is attached and visible on the backend service.
- A synthetic burst from one IP is throttled without affecting a second IP.
- Long-lived NDJSON event streams are NOT killed by the policy — verify explicitly, this is the likeliest false positive.
- Runbook documents thresholds, kill switch, and budget alerting.

title: Add an automated public-exposure acceptance scenario asserting no blocked route answers 200 anonymously and no redacted field appears in any anonymous response
description:
Step 21 of pl-b82d (phase A). Blocked on steps 1, 2, 4, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20. **This is the regression guard that makes the whole phase durable** — without it, the next agent to add a field or a route silently re-opens a leak.

WHY IT MATTERS
Every projection in steps 14-16 is an allowlist that a future contributor can widen by accident. A one-day-clean grep is not a gate (PHILOSOPHY rule 4: a seam is not done until a check fails on a violation).

SCOPE
New scenario under `scripts/acceptance/scenarios/` using the helpers in `scripts/acceptance/lib/`, deterministic and idempotent per the repo convention, run against a stack booted with `WARREN_AUTH=public`. Assertions:

1. **Blocked routes.** Every route classified hard-blocked in step 13 returns 401/403 anonymously — enumerated from the policy table itself, so a newly-added blocked route is covered automatically. Explicitly includes `/readyz`, `/metrics`, `/analytics/cost`, `/runs/:id/inbox`, `/runs/:id/finalize-intent`, `/projects/:id/triggers`, `/projects/:id/warren-config`, `/preview/config`.
2. **No mutations.** All 16 POST/DELETE routes return 403 anonymously.
3. **Inbox is not drained.** `GET /runs/:id/inbox` anonymously leaves inbox rows unread — assert state before and after.
4. **No forbidden substring in any anonymous response.** Walk every public-read route and assert the serialized body contains no `renderedAgentJson`, `localPath`, `resolvedFrom`, `burrowId`, `previewFailureMessage`, `costTotalUsd`, no absolute path matching `/data/` or `/home/`, no `Bearer `, and nothing matching the step-16 key shapes.
5. **Error bodies.** Force a 500 and assert the body carries no raw message (step 1).
6. **Stream cap.** Exceeding the per-IP cap returns 503 (step 4).
7. **Fail-closed.** Booting with `WARREN_AUTH` unset/invalid grants no anonymous access (step 12); booting public mode with a non-allowlisted project fails (step 17).

Wire it into CI. Note the acceptance suite (`scripts/acceptance/run.ts`) currently runs in NO workflow — either add this scenario to `ci.yml` specifically or bring the suite in; say which and why.

ACCEPTANCE
- Scenario passes against a local public-mode stack.
- Deliberately removing one projection makes it fail.
- It runs in CI, not just locally.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: CHECKPOINT: cut over to a fresh database, script the re-registration of os-eco repos, enable public mode on app.warren.run, and cut the release
description:
Step 22 of pl-b82d — **PUBLIC LAUNCH CHECKPOINT**. Blocked on steps 10 (warren-222c) and 21 (warren-c405). Everything before this is reversible; this is the step where strangers can see it.

TOPOLOGY DECISION (from the 2026-07-27 audit)
`app.warren.run` on GKE BECOMES the public instance. Rationale: the deploy pipeline is hardcoded to exactly one instance — namespace `warren`, object names `warren`, static IP name `warren-ingress` (`overlays/gke/kustomization.yaml:102`), ManagedCertificate name `warren` (`:103`), concurrency group `gke-deploy-warren` (`deploy-gke.yml:145`), RWO PVCs, and no GitHub Environments exist. Reusing the existing instance needs ZERO CI/repo changes; standing up a second GKE target needs 1-2 days of manifest surgery plus a new global IP and 15-60 min of cert provisioning. The private-instance story is handled separately and is out of scope for this plan.

DB CUTOVER
The live instance runs external Supabase Postgres (`docs/deploy/gke-deploy-prep.md:178-214`), not the PVC. Migrations are drizzle-generated and auto-applied at boot (`src/db/client.ts:150-190`, called from `src/server/main/index.ts:110-113`), so a fresh empty database builds its own schema. Steps:
1. Provision a fresh empty Postgres database. **Leave the existing one untouched — it is the rollback.**
2. Update the `warren-db-url` key in the `warren-secrets` k8s secret; restart. Rollback is a one-key flip.
3. **Verify the dialect immediately** via `/readyz`'s `db_reachable` check. `src/db/url.ts:76-79` silently treats an unrecognized DSN scheme as a bare SQLite path, so a typo yields a silently-empty local SQLite DB rather than a boot failure.

RE-REGISTRATION
Script it — do not click through. `POST /projects` needs only `gitUrl` (`src/server/handlers/projects.ts:35-50`); registration does a real `git clone` with a 120s timeout (`src/projects/clone.ts:31`). Agent discovery does NOT happen at registration, so follow with `POST /agents/refresh`. Handle non-idempotency: an existing project throws `ValidationError` (`src/projects/manage.ts:78-82`) and a pre-existing clone directory makes it refuse. Wall clock is dominated by the clones, ~15 min for 5-8 repos. Commit the script.

GO-LIVE
- Set `WARREN_AUTH=public` and `WARREN_PUBLIC_ORG_ALLOWLIST` in `warren-secrets`.
- Confirm the org allowlist boot assertion (step 17) passes with only os-eco repos registered.
- Deploy; run the step-21 acceptance scenario against the LIVE instance.
- Manually verify as a logged-out browser: browse runs, open a run, watch a live event stream, confirm no dispatch/steer affordance renders.
- Cut a release through the step 5-9 machinery.
- Set the GitHub repo `homepageUrl` to the demo URL and add repo topics (currently `repositoryTopics: null`).
- Dispatch a real run against an os-eco repo and watch it end to end from a logged-out browser.

ROTATE FIRST
`/Users/jayminwest/Projects/os-eco/warren/.env.deployed` holds live plaintext secrets on disk — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, a `github_pat_11…`, `WARREN_API_TOKEN`, the Supabase DB password and full `WARREN_DB_URL`, plus OpenAI/Gemini/ZAI keys. It is gitignored and uncommitted, but rotate everything before the instance is public and fix the stale "Fly + Supabase" header.

ACCEPTANCE
- A logged-out browser can watch a real run stream live at app.warren.run.
- The step-21 scenario passes against the live instance.
- Only allowlisted os-eco public repos are registered.
- Secrets rotated; rollback path verified.
- Repo has `homepageUrl` and topics set.

description:

ROADMAP.md is not stale, it is FROZEN. 1,724 lines / 91 KB. Last content commit was May 2026 (`e377e6c0`); the only July touch was a mechanical Fly.io strip (`3556640a`). Keyword counts: `canopy` 74, `burrow` 68, `mulch` 61, `sapling` 54 — versus `plot` 0, `plan-run` 0, `k8s`/`Kubernetes` 0, `RuntimeProvider` 0, `event bus` 0, `seams` 0, `PHILOSOPHY` 0. Its framing thesis (L3-17) is "an engineering org of 50+ ICs adopting on their own infrastructure" — a different product from the minimal-kernel one. **Every item on PHILOSOPHY.md's sequencing list has zero coverage, and the largest change since May (k8s) is not in it.** Open seed warren-0515 already names ROADMAP as needing this rewrite.

TRIAGE (from the 2026-07-27 audit of all 20 entries):

TARGET: ~180-230 lines / ~10 KB, sections:
`# Warren Roadmap` (framing + explicit contract: this file is DIRECTION; seeds is the work queue; SPEC is the design record) · `## Now — in flight` · `## Next — planned` (mirror PHILOSOPHY.md:158-188 verbatim so there is one source of truth for sequencing) · `## Shipped` (ONE table, one line each, linking SPEC section + CHANGELOG version) · `## Deliberately not in core` (PHILOSOPHY.md:98-100 already MANDATES this list with a recipe per refusal — name the extension tier that carries each) · `## Removed` (honest tombstones: plot, conversations, canopy, Fly.io, remote burrow workers — the strongest Show-HN signal in the file) · `## Under evaluation` (one line).

"Recently shipped" (L1448-1511) → delete, CHANGELOG owns it and it still leads with a Fly entry. "Cross-repo readiness" (L1512-1545) → delete, pins May 2026 versions. title: Hoist the canonical wire vocabulary out of db/schema/columns.ts into a shared home and fix the three confirmed type drifts
description:
Step 26 of pl-b82d (phase B3 — single source of truth). Unblocks steps 27 and 30.

THE PRINCIPLE BEING ENFORCED
One implementation of each capability in the domain layer; the HTTP API is a thin surface over it; CLI, SDK and UI are consumers, never reimplementations. The 2026-07-27 audit found the DOMAIN layer passes cleanly — all 12 CLI commands either go over HTTP via `src/client/` or call the SAME domain function the handler calls (`spawnRun` has exactly one implementation with four call sites; `addProject`, `refreshAgentRegistry` and the diagnostics checks are shared). **The wire/type layer is where it fails.**

FOUR SOURCES OF TRUTH FOR ONE SURFACE
`ROUTE_TABLE` (39 routes, canonical) · `docs/openapi.yaml` (gated, but has NO `components:` section and zero response schemas — it validates that a route exists, never what it returns) · `src/client/types*.ts` (hand-written) · `src/ui/src/api/types.ts` (independent; `src/ui` imports nothing from `src/client`). 25 type names are defined in both client and UI; 7 of those are ALSO in `src/db/schema/columns.ts` — triplicated: `RunState`, `RunFailureReason`, `PreviewState`, `PlanRunState`, `PlanRunChildState`, `RUN_TERMINAL_STATES`, `PLAN_RUN_TERMINAL_STATES`.

THE THREE CONFIRMED DRIFTS — fix all three:
1. **`RunFailureReason`** — canonical `src/db/schema/columns.ts:175-187` has 11 values; `src/client/types.ts:16-25` and `src/ui/src/api/types.ts:12-21` each have 9, both missing `finalize_failed` and `evicted`. Neither string appears anywhere under `src/client` or `src/ui/src`. Two real failure modes the server persists are unrepresentable in both surfaces.
2. **`RunRow.mode`** — `columns.ts:43` is `RUN_MODES = ["batch"]` with an explicit comment that `interactive` and `conversation` were dropped (warren-d622, warren-ee27). `src/client/types.ts:101` is correct. `src/ui/src/api/types.ts:114` still says `mode: "batch" | "interactive"`, plus `:217` and `:218` `interactiveAgent?`.
3. **`RefreshAgentsResponse.removed`** — server truth is `string[]` (`src/registry/refresh.ts:46`, passed through verbatim at `src/server/handlers/agents.ts:96`). `src/client/types.ts:76` is correct. `src/ui/src/api/types.ts:267` says `{ name: string }[]`. Currently latent (`pages/Agents.tsx:151,176` only read `.length`) but one `.map()` from rendering `undefined`. The UI also lacks the `projects` / `projectErrors` fields the server returns.

SCOPE
- Create a shared home for the canonical wire vocabulary — suggest `src/core/wire.ts`, since `src/core/` is already the kernel (105 LOC, errors + ids) and both surfaces can import it without either importing the other.
- `src/db/schema/columns.ts` re-exports from it (or defines and `src/core/wire.ts` re-exports — pick one direction and document why).

title: Add the check:wire-types gate forbidding redeclaration of canonical wire names outside their shared home
description:

title: Generalize check-burrow-boundary.ts into a data-driven check:layers gate and fix the ~6 existing violations
description:
Step 29 of pl-b82d (phase B3).

CONTEXT
`scripts/check-burrow-boundary.ts` is the ONLY architectural gate in the repo — 1 of 7 declared seams is enforced (PHILOSOPHY rule 4). title: Bring src/ui under the quality gates: remove the biome, check:size and check:debt exclusions with a grandfather pass
description:

Add a bounded `biome.json` override allowlist for existing files with a `$comment` explaining it is a ratchet, and seed `scripts/file-size-budgets.json` from the measured current sizes. Note `src/ui/src/api/types.ts` is 693 lines against a 500-line threshold — step 26's hoist should bring it under; if it does not, budget it explicitly with a comment.

title: De-duplicate defaultSpawn's three copies and tighten check:dups to see cross-layer clones
description:
Step 31 of pl-b82d (phase B3). Lowest priority; cheap and satisfying.

TWO SMALL THINGS

**1. De-duplicate `defaultSpawn`.** Three identical ~28-line copies: `src/cli/output.ts:62`, `src/server/main/utils.ts:23`, `src/server/handlers/index.ts:92`. Each carries a self-justifying comment — *"One of three identical copies… the duplication is deliberate so neither surface imports the other."* That rationale is a false dichotomy: **all three already import** `resolveSpawnEnv`, `SpawnFn`, `SpawnOptions` and `SpawnResult` from `src/projects/clone.ts:33-68`. The shared home exists; only the function body was copied. Move the body there, import it from all three sites, delete the comments. ~10 minutes, zero behavioral risk.

**2. Tighten `check:dups` so it can see cross-layer clones.** jscpd currently runs at `minTokens: 100` with `threshold: 3%` and ignores `src/db/schema/**`. Measured today: 23 clones at 0.86% — **the gate passes green while every clone below exists**, and the canonical enums are invisible to it by construction.
- Add a second, scoped jscpd invocation over `src/cli src/client src/ui/src/api src/server/handlers` at `--min-tokens 40 --threshold 0`, paired with a small explicit clone allowlist (false-positive risk is real at 40 tokens).
- Stop ignoring `src/db/schema/**` in the main run.
- Known cross-layer clones it should catch: `src/client/types.plan-runs.ts:25` ↔ `src/ui/src/api/types.ts:545` (33 lines, plan-run state unions — step 26 should already have removed this); `src/client/ndjson.ts:22` ↔ `src/ui/src/api/client.ts:437` (17 lines, **the NDJSON stream parser implemented twice** — `ndjson.ts:12-15` even documents that it mirrors the UI copy); `src/cli/output.ts:62` ↔ `src/server/main/utils.ts:26` (24 lines, `defaultSpawn`, fixed above).
- The NDJSON parser duplication is the one worth actually fixing rather than allowlisting — consider whether the UI can consume `src/client/ndjson.ts` directly, which is the first step toward collapsing the two API clients entirely. If that is too large here, file a follow-up seed.

ACCEPTANCE
- `defaultSpawn` has one definition.
- The scoped jscpd run is in `check:dups` and green, with every allowlist entry commented.
- Known cross-layer clones are either eliminated or explicitly allowlisted with a reason.
- `bun run check:all` green.

This is that separate decision: the mandate is to remove .canopy/ and every canopy reference entirely, so the seed drop relocates and warren's own .canopy/ directory is deleted.

WHY: .canopy/agent.json is warren's OWN output, not canopy's. src/runs/seed.ts:71 buildSeedFiles() unconditionally writes the rendered AgentDefinition envelope to ".canopy/agent.json" in every workspace. Deleting the tracked file and relocating the drop to an untracked, gitignored path removes the collision at the source, rather than papering over it with .git/info/exclude or update-index --assume-unchanged (warren-aced's fix options 1 and 2). warren-8d95 was an earlier partial attempt at the same problem.

title: runs.project_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting a project orphans its runs and event transcripts instead of removing them
description:
Deleting a project does NOT remove its runs. `runs.project_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` (`src/db/migrations/postgres/0000_init.sql:74`, mirrored at `src/db/schema/postgres.ts:94` and `sqlite.ts:128`). The runs survive with `project_id = NULL`, and because `events.run_id` is `ON DELETE no action` (`0000_init.sql:72`) their `payload_json` agent transcripts survive with them.

This was deliberate, not an accident — the sqlite migration that introduced it is literally named `0003_orphan_runs_on_project_delete.sql`, preserving run history across project de-registration. That is defensible for a private instance. It is a leak vector for a public one.

## CONFIRMED LIVE (measured 2026-07-27 against warren-dogfood, biaxgkadzaruhrqsjnmi)

This is not a latent risk. It is already the majority of the production database:

- **685 of 1,182 runs (58%) are orphaned** — `project_id IS NULL`
- Those orphans carry **2,206,133 events — 81% of the 2,708,279-row table**
- The database is 11 GB, essentially all of it `events`
- Nothing identifies which repo any orphaned run came from; `project_id` was the only discriminator and it is already gone

Query used:

```sql
SELECT COALESCE(p.git_url, '<<ORPHANED>>') AS repo,
       count(DISTINCT r.id) AS runs, count(e.id) AS events
FROM runs r
LEFT JOIN projects p ON p.id = r.project_id
LEFT JOIN events   e ON e.run_id = r.id
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC;
```

## WHY IT MATTERS UNDER WARREN_AUTH=public

Three things line up badly:
1. Orphaned runs keep `prompt`, which the public projection deliberately KEEPS (warren-946f), plus their full event stream.
2. The boot assertion iterates projects only (`assertRegisteredProjectsAllowlisted`, called at `src/server/main/index.ts:137`), so it passes clean over a database full of orphaned private-repo transcripts.
3. `src/server/projection.ts` only picks fields — it never filters on project — so orphaned runs are listed and streamed to anonymous callers.

Net: the warren-1841 cleanup as originally scoped (delete non-allowlisted projects, keep the rest) would have published 685 unattributable runs and 2.2M transcript events, with the boot assertion reporting success. The plan was changed to a full wipe of all eight public tables partly because of this finding, which removes the live exposure but leaves the underlying defect in place.

## OPTIONS

- Change the FK to `ON DELETE cascade` and drop the orphan-preservation intent.
- Keep SET NULL but make the public read path refuse rows with `project_id IS NULL` (fail-closed projection), and extend the boot assertion to count orphaned runs.
- Keep SET NULL and add an explicit purge path that deletes runs+events before the project row.

The second is the smallest fail-closed fix and does not change existing private-instance behavior.

Note the post-launch recurrence: once the public instance is live, deleting any project through the UI or API re-creates this condition immediately. The full wipe clears today's orphans; it does not stop tomorrow's.

## ACCEPTANCE

- A run whose project was deleted is not reachable anonymously (list, detail, or event stream).
- A check fails when an orphaned run exists on a public instance, rather than serving it.

Found while planning the warren-1841 database cleanup.
closeReason: Converted runs.project_id and events.run_id to ON DELETE CASCADE in both sqlite (0032) and postgres (0026) dialects, so deleting a project now cascade-removes its runs and their event transcripts instead of orphaning them with project_id=NULL. Updated deleteProject docs, UI delete dialog copy, and the delete-project test to assert runs+events are gone. bun run check:all green.

title: Add a CI gate that builds the container image
description:
Two consecutive releases (v0.12.0, v0.12.1) were tagged with no publishable image, because nothing between a PR and a release build ever runs `docker build`.

v0.12.0 died on TS2307: warren-b229 moved the wire vocabulary into src/core/wire.ts and src/ui/src/api/types.ts imports it across the package seam, but the Dockerfile's UI stage copied only src/ui, so the specifier pointed outside the build context.

v0.12.1 died on `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: the dependabot jscpd 4->5 and typescript 6->7 bumps landed in package.json without a lockfile regen.

Both were invisible to all 12 gates. check:all runs against an already-installed tree, and no gate installs from a frozen lockfile or builds the image. The class is 'the release artifact is only ever built at release time', so the first sighting is always a failed release.

Cheapest fix: a CI job on PRs running `docker build` (build only, no push). It catches both failures above and every future one. Layer caching keeps it affordable; it need not push anything.

Found while cutting the public-launch release (warren-1841).
closeReason: Added docker-build job to .github/workflows/ci.yml — runs docker build (build only, no push) on every PR via docker/build-push-action@v6 with type=gha layer caching, catching Dockerfile/lockfile breakage before release. CI-only job, parity-neutral (not a bun run step / check:all gate).

title: Public event stream leaks burrowId in reap.workspace_destroyed payload
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Adopted into plan pl-61a4.

Parent seed: warren-d49c — Batch: finalize-contract hygiene + public-instance security fixes (dogfood plan-run)
Plan template: feature

Run `sd plan show pl-61a4` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

warren-946f dropped `burrowId` from the GET /runs and GET /runs/:id public projections, but the run event stream (warren-1cb7) still emits it: the `reap.workspace_destroyed` system event's payload carries `burrowId`.

Observed anonymously against the live public instance:
  GET /runs/run_xh5pk5jgep8a/events
  {"kind":"reap.workspace_destroyed","stream":"system","payload":{"archived":false,"burrowId":"run-run-xh5pk5jgep8a",...}}

Impact is low, not zero. The value is `run-run-<runId>`, derived entirely from the run id the caller already has, so it discloses no new fact today. It is filed because the field was judged redactable on the run projections and survives here — an inconsistency that becomes a real leak the moment burrowId stops being a pure function of the run id.

Scenario 39 does not catch it: its leak sweep seeds its own database and that seed has no reaped run, so no reap.workspace_destroyed event exists to inspect. Extending the seed to include one would close the gap in CI.

Found by an anonymous live probe during the public-launch checkpoint (warren-1841).

title: reap misclassifies harness-written .claude/settings.local.json as dropped_commit, failing 4 of 5 runs on the live public instance
description:
Incomplete fix of warren-89b0.

Observed on the live public instance (app.warren.run, v0.12.2, WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s): 4 of 5 runs are in state failed with failureReason=dropped_commit, including prompts that were explicitly read-only and instructed the agent not to edit anything.

Evidence, run_39bd85h95w92 reap event payload:
  {"dirty": true, "branch": "warren/run_39bd85h95w92", "dirtyPaths": [".claude/settings.local.json"], "droppedCommit": true,
   "message": "git push exited zero and the workspace still has uncommitted changes - agent staged work but never committed"}

Root cause: the claude-code harness itself writes .claude/settings.local.json into the workspace at runtime. classifyEmptyPush (src/runs/reap/util.ts:196) treats any dirty path outside BOOKKEEPING_ARTIFACT_PREFIXES (src/runs/reap/util.ts:159 - currently .mulch/, .seeds/, .plot/, .canopy/) as lost agent work and flips an otherwise-succeeded run to failed. The agent never staged anything; the harness did.

Impact: the public dashboard - the spectacle surface for the whole campaign - advertises an ~80 percent failure rate that is not real. It also blocks credible dogfooding: any showcase run across models or providers will render as a failure.

Fix direction (pick one, prefer the first):
1. Exclude harness-owned state from the workspace git view at init (.git/info/exclude), so it never appears dirty.
2. Add harness-state paths to the bookkeeping allowlist. Note this list is about warren-managed paths that warren commits on the agent behalf; harness scratch state is a third category and may deserve its own constant rather than overloading BOOKKEEPING_ARTIFACT_PREFIXES.

Acceptance: a read-only prompt that touches no files reaps as succeeded with noChanges=true, and the live instance stops reporting dropped_commit for runs that changed nothing.

Found during the 2026-07-28 hardening inventory by probing the live instance anonymously.

title: Run pods receive the full-capability operator token (WARREN_API_TOKEN grants admin), so an injected agent can control the instance
description:
src/runtime/k8s/provider.ts:289-298, src/runtime/k8s/pod-env.ts:169.

Every run pod is given WARREN_API_TOKEN - the same instance token that carries the admin capability - alongside ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the GitHub PAT. Any code executing inside the pod can therefore call the control plane as operator: DELETE /projects/:id, POST /runs, read every operator-only body, and exfiltrate both credentials.

On a public instance this matters more than it looks. The input driving the agent is public: issue text, PR bodies, and repo contents. Prompt injection from a poisoned repo is a live attack class and the master plan explicitly assumes attempts during the Autonomous Month. The repo test and build scripts the agent runs are also attacker-influenced on any contributed branch.

There is no network-layer backstop today - see the NetworkPolicy issue filed alongside this one.

Fix: mint a per-run, run-scoped credential valid only for that run callback surface (/runs/:thisId/inbox, finalize endpoints) with a lifetime bounded by the run, instead of injecting the instance operator token. The provider already gates WARREN_API_URL on the presence of a token (provider.ts:293-298), so the seam to swap the credential is in one place.

Acceptance: a token captured from inside a run pod cannot dispatch a run, delete a project, or read any operator-only body.
closeReason: Fixed by 6390fb10: run sandboxes now receive a per-run HMAC-scoped callback token (signed with the operator token, bound to one run id) instead of the operator bearer. runScopedAuth admits a narrow 'run' actor; the request gate confines it to its own run's callback surface (inbox + finalize legs), pins the :id param, and rejects once the run is terminal (runActivityCheck). Single injection seam (injectWarrenCallbackEnv) covers both local and k8s topologies. RunTokenMinter is the R-18 App-token seam. Tests prove a captured run token cannot dispatch/delete/read operator bodies, is accepted on its own surface, and is rejected once terminal.

title: Anonymous GET /runs/:id/events materializes the entire run transcript in memory before streaming, risking OOM on the single replica
description:
src/runs/events.ts:217-231 and src/db/repos/events.ts:76-90 (listByRun - the handler never passes opts.limit).

The non-follow snapshot builds the full event slice for a run into an array before yielding the first byte, so per-connection memory equals the whole transcript. The control-plane pod limit is 1Gi (deploy/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:205) and the deployment runs a single replica. A handful of concurrent replays of a long run can OOM-kill it.

The global stream cap (200) is not a real bound here because the per-client key is spoofable behind the GCE load balancer - see the X-Forwarded-For issue filed alongside.

Fix: pass a bounded page limit (order of 5k rows) to listByRun for the snapshot and require ?since paging beyond it. Stream rather than materialize where practical.

Acceptance: memory per event-replay connection is bounded independent of transcript length; scenario 39 asserts an anonymous replay cannot exceed the bound.
closeReason: Bounded event-replay snapshots in src/runs/events.ts: tailRunEvents now passes a 5000-row page limit (DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT_PAGE_LIMIT, overridable via snapshotLimit) to events.listByRun. Non-follow returns one page (clients page with ?since); follow pages through history via the new pageHistory helper so live replays aren't truncated. Seq high-water-mark dedup unchanged. Tests added in src/runs/events.test.ts. check:all 12/12.

title: Anonymous GET /analytics/runs with to= and no from= applies no window bound and scans the entire runs table
description:
src/server/handlers/runs/analytics.ts:296 -> src/server/handlers/runs/lifecycle.ts:268 (resolveAnalyticsFrom) -> src/db/repos/runs-queries.ts:159 (listForAnalytics, no LIMIT).

When to is supplied and from is absent, resolveAnalyticsFrom returns undefined and no lower bound is applied at all. The 30-day default is skipped. The query becomes a full scan of runs including the large rendered_agent_json blobs, and hydrateRunsUsage then runs a second unbounded inArray scan over events.

Anonymous, uncached, and repeatable. Verified reachable against the live instance on 2026-07-28:
  GET https://app.warren.run/analytics/runs?to=2030-01-01  ->  200

Impact is small today only because the table holds 5 runs. It scales directly with table growth, and against Supabase it is billable egress and CPU on a single-replica deployment. This is one of only two anonymous levers that can degrade the instance (the other is the event-replay issue filed alongside).

Fix: apply the default window whenever from is absent regardless of to, and clamp the total span server-side (reject or clamp spans beyond ~90 days). Add a LIMIT to listForAnalytics as a second line of defence.

Acceptance: no anonymous request can cause an unbounded scan of runs or events; scenario 39 asserts it.
closeReason: Replaced resolveAnalyticsFrom with resolveAnalyticsWindow in src/server/handlers/runs/lifecycle.ts: the 30-day default window now applies whenever from is absent (including when to= is present) and the from..to span is clamped to 90 days. Added ANALYTICS_MAX_ROWS LIMIT to listForAnalytics in src/db/repos/runs-queries.ts as defense in depth. Unit tests in src/server/handlers/runs.analytics-window.test.ts; public-projections.test.ts updated for the always-bounded filter echo; scenario 39 (scripts/acceptance/scenarios/39-public-exposure.ts) now asserts the anonymous to=-without-from window is bounded and clamped.

title: Event-stream secret scrubber misses WARREN_DB_URL (the Supabase DSN with password), URL userinfo, and JWT shapes
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Step 2 of plan pl-1c02.

Parent seed: warren-24d0 — 0.13.x truth & hygiene batch — carried-over fixes, promotion completion, phase-0 hygiene
Plan template: feature
Plan approach: Work the batch as independent small PRs cut as 0.13.x patch releases, in the order set by seam-sequencing phase 0 + 0' remainders. Spawn new child seeds only for untracked work; adopt the already-tracked issues (warren-6fa0, warren-cd3b,…

Run `sd plan show pl-1c02` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

src/server/handlers/runs/event-projection.ts:122 (SECRET_ENV_NAME) and :93-113 (SECRET_PATTERN).

SECRET_ENV_NAME matches only _TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|PASSWORD|PASSPHRASE|CREDENTIALS?|DSN. It does not match WARREN_DB_URL - the Postgres DSN for the Supabase database, which embeds the database password - nor CANOPY_REPO_URL, which conventionally embeds a token.

SECRET_PATTERN has no alternative for scheme://user:pass@host userinfo, no JWT (eyJ...) pattern, no Google AIza..., and no npm_... So a Supabase service_role JWT or the DSN appearing in any transcript string is emitted in the clear on the anonymous event stream.

The scrubber gap is verified by reading the patterns. The end-to-end exploitation path - getting the control-plane DSN into a pod-sourced event - is an unverified hypothesis and should not hold up the fix; the cost of the gap is asymmetric.

Fix: add URL|URI|CONN to SECRET_ENV_NAME, plus a generic \w+://[^\s:@/]+:[^\s@/]+@ userinfo pattern and a JWT pattern, to SECRET_PATTERN.

Acceptance: a DSN, a JWT, and a userinfo URL planted in an event payload are all redacted on the anonymous stream, asserted in scenario 39.
closeReason: Extended event-stream scrubber: URL userinfo (postgres/Supabase DSN passwords, generic user:pass@host) and JWT (eyJ.eyJ.sig) shapes now redact; SECRET_ENV_NAME gained URL|URI|CONN suffixes (WARREN_DB_URL). Proven by new corpus fixtures (Supabase DSN, userinfo URL, service_role JWT) + negative cases (plain URL, foo.bar.baz) in runs.events-projection.test.ts and planted sentinels in acceptance scenario 39.

title: plan_runs and plan_run_children are served to spectators with no field allowlist, leaking promptTemplate, dispatcherHandle, overrides, and raw error strings
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Adopted into plan pl-61a4.

Parent seed: warren-d49c — Batch: finalize-contract hygiene + public-instance security fixes (dogfood plan-run)
Plan template: feature

Run `sd plan show pl-61a4` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

src/server/handlers/plan-runs.ts:183-209 (list) and :221-234 (detail - runs[] is projected, planRun and children are not).

These are the only readPublic bodies with no field allowlist, in a codebase whose stated rule is allowlist and never denylist. Fields reaching anonymous callers today: promptTemplate, dispatcherHandle, providerOverride, modelOverride, and failureReason.

failureReason is the sharp one. It is built as dispatch_failed:${formatError(err)} at src/plan-runs/coordinator.ts:319, i.e. a raw internal error string. Example shape from src/warren-config/load.ts:113:
  WarrenConfigUnavailableError: project clone missing on disk: /data/projects/<owner>/<repo>
That is the warren-4385 disclosure class arriving through an unprojected wire field rather than an error envelope, and it carries a host path that REDACTED_RUN_FIELDS withholds elsewhere.

Latent rather than active right now: verified on the live instance 2026-07-28, GET /plan-runs returns {"planRuns":[]}, so nothing is leaking until the first plan-run exists.

Scenario 39 structurally cannot catch this - its sweep derives forbidden names from the REDACTED_* constants, and plan-runs has none.

Fix: add PUBLIC_PLAN_RUN_FIELDS / REDACTED_PLAN_RUN_FIELDS (and the children equivalents) and route both handlers through pickFields. Classify failureReason with the body/log split used for collected error messages rather than exposing the raw string.

title: reap_failed and spawn_failed events leak absolute host paths and raw subprocess stderr on the anonymous stream
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Adopted into plan pl-61a4.

event-projection.ts deliberately keeps these kinds on the public stream and scrubs only credential shapes. It does nothing about filesystem paths or subprocess stderr, so a spectator can read exactly what REDACTED_RUN_FIELDS withholds from the run row (localPath, previewFailureMessage).

Scenario 39 would catch this - FORBIDDEN_PATH_FRAGMENTS already covers /data/ and /home/ - but it never seeds an event of these kinds, so the assertion never runs.

title: Per-client event-stream cap is bypassable: eventStreamClientKey trusts the left-most X-Forwarded-For hop, which GCLB lets the client set
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Adopted into plan pl-61a4.

Parent seed: warren-d49c — Batch: finalize-contract hygiene + public-instance security fixes (dogfood plan-run)
Plan template: feature

Run `sd plan show pl-61a4` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

src/server/stream-limits.ts:253-261.

eventStreamClientKey takes the left-most X-Forwarded-For value. The module comment assumes only a directly-exposed instance could have that forged, but the GCE load balancer appends to a client-supplied XFF (<supplied>, <client-ip>, <lb-ip>), so on this deployment the left-most hop is attacker-controlled.

Consequences: one IP rotates the header and consumes all 200 global slots (DEFAULT_MAX_EVENT_STREAMS), denying the stream surface to every other visitor; it also poisons the abuse logs, which key off the same value. Cloud Armor throttles at 600 req/60s per IP, roughly 3x the global cap, so it does not contain this.

This is also what makes the unbounded event-replay issue exploitable at scale.

Fix: key off ctx.clientIp, or count from the right-hand side with a configurable trusted-hop count.

Acceptance: a single source cannot occupy more than its per-client share of stream slots regardless of headers it sends; scenario 39 covers the global cap and the spoof attempt.

title: No NetworkPolicy anywhere in deploy/k8s: run pods can reach the control plane, their peers, and arbitrary egress
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Step 28 of plan pl-a37b.

Parent seed: warren-bc61 — v0.18.0 — the any-setup release: dispatch-context log, IssueTracker seam + RemoteTracker bridge, external-repo readiness
Plan template: feature
Plan approach: Five tracks, forward-chained. Track A (steps 1-5): the dispatch-context log as a core insert-only dispatch_context table keyed by run_id, written fire-and-log inside spawnRun (the verified single choke point covering all 8 dispatch sites),…

Run `sd plan show pl-a37b` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

DECISION 2026-08-04: deferred entirely past the 0.14.x polish pass, together with warren-cb93. Egress allowlisting needs FQDN-based policy (GKE Dataplane V2 / Cilium) because GitHub and model-provider CIDRs are unstable — that is a platform decision, not a polish item. Revisit after the Forge campaign.

Confirmed by grep across deploy/ and docs/ - no NetworkPolicy object exists. deploy/k8s/base/service.yaml:7 states the assumption outright (flat pod network) and RUNBOOK-K8S section 8 documents networkPolicy as coarse.

A run pod executes agent-driven code. Today it can reach the control-plane Service on :8080, its peer run pods in warren-runs, the repo-cache PVC node, and any external egress. Combined with the operator-token issue filed alongside, there is no network-layer backstop at all: the credential is in the pod and the path to use it is open.

Fix: add a default-deny ingress policy in warren-runs, plus explicit egress allows for DNS, the warren Service, and the external CIDRs an agent genuinely needs (GitHub, the model provider, package registries). Document the resulting egress contract in RUNBOOK-K8S so operators know what to widen.

Priority note: this should land before the Autonomous Month, when untrusted repo content starts driving agents at volume.
closeReason: Added deploy/k8s/base/networkpolicy.yaml (default-deny ingress for warren-managed run pods; restricted egress = DNS:53 + warren Service :8080 + 0.0.0.0/0 external; none/open egress modes). Wired into kustomization.yaml. Documented egress contract in docs/RUNBOOK-K8S.md §4.1. Offline-validated via kubectl kustomize base/kind/gke (4 NetworkPolicies each). kind/GKE live validation is operator follow-up.

title: No security headers on any response, and no Vary: Authorization on projected routes (a future CDN would serve operator bodies to spectators)
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->

Plan template: feature

Run `sd plan show pl-61a4` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
