src/server/response.ts:14-20 emits only content-type. Verified against the live instance 2026-07-28: no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, frame-ancestors, or Strict-Transport-Security on any response.

The operator bearer token lives in browser storage on the same origin, so the absence of CSP and frame-ancestors is not merely cosmetic.

Separately and more dangerous: /whoami is the only route declaring Vary (src/server/handlers/meta.ts:55), yet every readPublic body varies by Authorization - an operator sees more fields than a spectator at the same URL. Enabling Cloud CDN on the BackendConfig later would cache an operator response and serve it to anonymous visitors. That is a latent full-disclosure bug waiting on an infrastructure toggle.

Fix: add a small security-header pass in jsonResponse and createUiHandler, and emit Vary: Authorization on every projected route. Assert both in scenario 39.

title: Close scenario 39 coverage gaps: plan-run fields, path-bearing event kinds, unbounded queries, global stream cap, headers
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Adopted into plan pl-61a4.

Parent seed: warren-d49c — Batch: finalize-contract hygiene + public-instance security fixes (dogfood plan-run)
Plan template: feature

Run `sd plan show pl-61a4` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

Scenario 39 (scripts/acceptance/scenarios/39-public-exposure.ts) is the only scenario wired into CI and it covers a lot well: every blocked route refused anonymously (derived from API_ROUTE_POLICIES, so new routes are picked up automatically), 15+ mutating routes refused, the inbox not drained on anonymous read, value-level sentinels for every REDACTED_* field, host-path fragments, unredacted bearers, a forced 500 that says nothing, the per-client stream 503, and three fail-closed boot refusals.

Gaps found during the 2026-07-28 hardening inventory, each tied to a filed issue:
1. No field-level guard for plan_runs / plan_run_children - there are no REDACTED_* constants to derive from.
2. Only 4 event kinds are seeded, so path- and stderr-bearing kinds (reap_failed, spawn_failed, watchdog.terminal_reconciled) never get exercised even though the path assertions exist.
3. The pre-auth preview-proxy preamble is never touched.
4. No assertion that an anonymous request cannot trigger an unbounded query or an unbounded event replay.
5. Only the per-client stream cap is tested; the global cap is not, and the X-Forwarded-For key spoof is not modelled.
6. No assertion on Vary, cache-control, or security headers.
7. In-process only. Nothing runs against the live instance after deploy, so a manifest or ingress regression is invisible to CI.

Item 7 is the structural one: consider a thin post-deploy smoke variant that runs the same assertions against app.warren.run.

title: Postgres migrations do not enable RLS on new tables, so every table added after warren-b778 repeats the exposure
description:
warren-b778 and warren-062e enabled RLS across the then-existing tables. run_inbox was added afterwards and shipped with RLS disabled - caught by the Supabase security advisor at ERROR level during the 2026-07-28 inventory, and fixed manually that day (migration enable_rls_on_run_inbox; all 8 public tables now report rls_enabled=true with 0 policies, which is deny-all for PostgREST roles). The Supabase Data API has since been disabled entirely for the dogfood project, which is the stronger control.

The point of this issue is the process, not the table: nothing in the migration path enables RLS, so the next table added repeats it. Manual advisor checks are not a control.

Fix options:
1. Add ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY to the drizzle migration template or a post-migrate step, so new tables are deny-all by default.
2. Add a CI or release check that fails when a public table has rls_enabled=false.
3. Document in RUNBOOK-K8S that the Data API must stay disabled on any Supabase-backed deployment, since warren connects by DSN as table owner and never uses PostgREST.

Note the owner-bypass subtlety for whoever picks this up: all tables are owned by postgres with relforcerowsecurity=false, so enabling RLS does not affect warren own access. That is why this is safe to apply broadly.
closeReason: static RLS gate added: postgres migrations creating tables without ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY now fail lint; wired with CI parity intact

title: watchdog.terminal_reconciled event payload re-leaks burrowRunId (sibling of warren-5f59)
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Adopted into plan pl-61a4.

Parent seed: warren-d49c — Batch: finalize-contract hygiene + public-instance security fixes (dogfood plan-run)
Plan template: feature

Run `sd plan show pl-61a4` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

src/runs/watchdog-reconcile.ts:182-193 puts burrowRunId into the event payload.

burrowRunId is listed in REDACTED_RUN_FIELDS, and the bridge_* kinds were added to INTERNAL_EVENT_KINDS for precisely this reason - this kind was missed. Same class as warren-5f59 (reap.workspace_destroyed leaking burrowId), different code site.

Worth noting while fixing: under WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s these fields are not null as the UI comments claim. src/runtime/k8s/provider.ts:281 returns the pod name as sandboxId and src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts:259-262 stores it into runs.burrowId with the pod UID into burrowRunId. So on the live deployment this payload discloses a real Kubernetes pod UID, not a value derivable from the run id. That makes it a slightly stronger leak than warren-5f59.

Fix: drop burrowRunId from the payload, or add the kind to INTERNAL_EVENT_KINDS. Consider fixing both sites together with warren-5f59.

title: idleTimeout is disabled server-wide, so no route has slow-request protection (stream-lifetime half closed by warren-3995)
description:
src/server/server.ts:65 sets DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 0 and passes it into both Bun.serve binders (bindTcp server.ts:183, bindUnix server.ts:202). It exists to protect the long-lived NDJSON tail, but applies to every route, so no endpoint has slow-request protection. No per-route scoping exists anywhere in src/server/.

Fix: keep a per-request timeout as the default and disable it only for the two stream handlers (GET /runs/:id/events, GET /plan-runs/:id/events). src/server/preview-server.ts:44 has the same '?? 0' and needs the same treatment. src/server/server.test.ts:278 asserts the unscoped behaviour and must be updated alongside.

Also in scope: .env.example:170-175 and deploy/k8s/overlays/gke/backendconfig.yaml:28-29 still document the event-stream lifetime as unbounded by default. Untrue since warren-3995 / PR #693. .env.example:165 is stale too (describes the per-client key as the left-most XFF hop; warren-46a7 changed it).

REVISED 2026-08-08: the original second bullet (unlimited stream lifetime) is closed. warren-3995 turned on a 4h default cap (DEFAULT_EVENT_STREAM_MAX_LIFETIME_MS, src/server/stream-limits.ts:60), enforced at stream-limits.ts:239, wired into both stream routes. warren-25f6's concurrency caps are separate and also in place. Only the idleTimeout half survives.
closeReason: Fixed by PR #855 (commit 87e1e836, merged 2026-08-14): DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30 on server.ts and preview-server.ts, asserted in server.test.ts, documented in .env.example; stream-lifetime half was warren-3995

title: Pre-auth preview-proxy preamble runs on the public instance and is outside all test coverage
description:
src/server/server.ts:223 runs previewProxy before the auth gate, and src/server/main/preview-wiring.ts:57 enables it unconditionally in the default path mode.

An anonymous request to /p/<runId>, or any path carrying a crafted Referer, reaches src/preview/proxy/index.ts:148-168 and gets a run-existence oracle. The 501 branch at :157 echoes run.worker_id, which is a REDACTED_RUN_FIELDS value.

Actual impact today is nil: previews are unsupported under WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s (previewPorts capability is false) and workerId is no longer written on new runs. This is filed because the surface sits entirely outside scenario 39 and ahead of the auth gate, which is exactly where a future change would go unnoticed.

Fix: skip the preview preamble when the resolved runtime lacks the previewPorts capability. This is the capabilities-not-conditionals rule from PHILOSOPHY.md applied to a boot-time wiring decision.
closeReason: preview preamble gated on previewPorts capability; pre-auth /p/ surface covered by leak tests

title: UI shows burrow topology on a Kubernetes deployment, and the code comments asserting the fields are null under k8s are false
description:
The user-visible half of this is the confusing part; the comment half is what will mislead the next maintainer.

Established fact: under WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s these fields are NOT null. src/runtime/k8s/provider.ts:281 returns the pod name as sandboxId, and src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts:259-262 stores it into runs.burrowId with the pod UID into burrowRunId. So the values exist and are Kubernetes identifiers wearing burrow labels. Spectators are shielded only because the public projection redacts them (src/server/handlers/runs/lifecycle.ts:66-72); the logged-in operator sees the mislabel.

Sites:
- src/ui/src/pages/Runs.tsx:151 - landing-page subtitle reads "Agent runs dispatched into burrow sandboxes." Highest-visibility instance: it is the first line an anonymous visitor reads. Suggested: "Agent runs dispatched into isolated sandboxes."
- src/ui/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx:236-245 - "Burrow ID" and "Burrow Run" meta cards render the pod name and pod UID under burrow labels. The adjacent comment at :232-235 and src/ui/src/api/types.ts:116-122 both claim these are null under k8s. Both are wrong and must be corrected, not just relabelled.
- src/ui/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx:334-338 - cancel confirmation reads "Cancel forwarded (burrow: <state>)" where the state is a pod phase.
- src/ui/src/pages/Projects.tsx:95 - description shows anonymous visitors "GitHub repos cloned under $WARREN_PROJECTS_DIR", host-filesystem jargon that is meaningless on k8s.

Fix: runtime-neutral copy throughout, and correct the two false comments. The wire-level rename (BurrowSummary, SpawnRunResponse.burrow, CancelRunResponse.burrowRun) is tracked separately since it needs server, SDK, and UI to move together.
closeReason: Runtime-neutral UI copy and corrected false null-under-k8s comments: Runs.tsx subtitle now 'isolated sandboxes'; RunDetail.tsx meta cards relabelled Sandbox ID / Sandbox Run with a corrected presence-gating comment (pod name/UID under k8s, not null), cancel confirmation reads '(sandbox: <state>)' instead of '(burrow: ...)'; Projects.tsx description no longer references $WARREN_PROJECTS_DIR; api/types.ts burrowId/burrowRunId docblock corrected to say k8s populates pod identifiers. No wire-level renames.

title: Anonymous visitors to the Run stats page get a red HTTP 403 error card plus two permanently empty sections
description:
src/ui/src/pages/RunAnalytics.tsx:81-92, :173, :193-199, :226-229.

The page unconditionally issues GET /analytics/behavior, which carries the readOperator policy (src/server/handlers/index.ts:293-298). For every anonymous visitor this is a guaranteed 403, rendered as a red "Failed to load command behavior. HTTP 403" card on a page reachable from the main nav.

Alongside it, two cards ("Commands by category", "Stuck-command leaderboard") are permanently empty for spectators, and the "Top seeds by context" chart (:173, src/ui/src/pages/run-analytics/Charts.tsx:195-207) always reads "No data in this window." because topSeedsByContext is redacted server-side (src/server/handlers/runs/analytics.ts:202-204).

Net effect: a nav-visible page on the public demo instance looks broken to everyone who is not logged in.

Fix: gate the behavior query and its sections on caps.can("readOperator"), and hide the redacted chart for non-operators. The pattern already exists - PreviewCard does exactly this at src/ui/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx:400-411.

Related but separate: warren-0607 covers the analytics cost crash on the same page.
closeReason: Gated the /analytics/behavior query and its dependent sections (insight callouts, behavior error card, command-category chart, stuck-command leaderboard) on caps.can('readOperator') in src/ui/src/pages/RunAnalytics.tsx, mirroring the PreviewCard pattern from RunDetail.tsx; also hid the server-redacted TopSeedsByContextChart for non-operators instead of empty-rendering it. 12/12 check:all gates green.

title: Plan runs page defaults to an empty table: the filter pill labelled Active carries the value all, and the server disagrees with it
description:
src/ui/src/pages/PlanRuns.tsx:53-60 with src/server/handlers/plan-runs.ts:194-208.

The default filter pill is labelled "Active" but its value is "all". With no project selected the server returns active-only plan runs, so on a quiet read-only instance the default view is an empty table even when finished plan runs exist. With a project selected, the same pill returns all states. The label, the value, and the server behaviour are three different things.

A visitor has to guess and click "Succeeded" to discover the instance has ever run a plan.

Fix: add a real "All" filter, make the default view show recent history rather than active-only, and align the label with the behaviour on both code paths.

Also in this page and worth folding into the same change: src/ui/src/pages/PlanRuns.tsx:256-277 mounts a per-row GET /plan-runs/:id query refetching every 5 seconds. That is an N+1 that multiplies by concurrent public visitors (rows x visitors x 12 req/min) and makes the Children and Cost cells pop in late. Prefer server-side counts on the list envelope.
closeReason: Fixed by PR #856 (commit c9086020, merged 2026-08-14): 'All' is a real filter option and the default on the plan-runs page; folded-in per-row N+1 poll resolved via warren-f566 / PR #885; GH#769 closed

title: README tells users to pin a container image that is two minors old, and the two releases in between have no image at all
description:
README.md:56 reads: Pin a release with :v0.11.0, or track the moving minor with :0.11.

Current release is 0.12.2. Per CHANGELOG, v0.12.0 and v0.12.1 have no container image - the build was broken and was fixed by warren-1841 (5de0ad5d, copy src/core into the UI build stage). So :v0.12.2 is the first buildable 0.12 image, and that is exactly the number the README does not state.

A new user following the README today lands two minors behind on a release that predates the public-instance work. This is the single most consequential factual error in the front-door doc.

Fix: pin :v0.12.2 explicitly, and say why the intermediate tags are absent so nobody tries them. Consider whether the moving-minor advice (:0.12) is wise given two of its three tags are unbuildable.

Related: the container-build CI gate that would have caught this is tracked in warren-3380 - two releases have now died this way.
closeReason: README pin advice now points at :v0.12.2 (first buildable 0.12 image), explains why v0.12.0/v0.12.1 tags have no container image, and recommends the explicit pin over the :0.12 moving minor since two of three tags are unbuildable.

title: CONTRIBUTING.md tells contributors to do the exact thing check:wire-types now fails, and omits the dev loop and the real gate list

Three gaps in the doc an outside contributor reads first.

This is the pre-warren-02f2 guidance that CLAUDE.md now calls out as having sanctioned exactly the duplication that then drifted. A contributor who follows it for a wire-shaped type fails bun run check:wire-types. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md were corrected by warren-02f2; CONTRIBUTING.md was missed.

2. No local dev loop. The doc covers gates and conventions but never says how to actually run warren from a checkout - serve, the UI dev server, and how to exercise a run without standing up a full container or sandbox stack. That is the first thing a new contributor needs and the hardest to infer.

3. Gate expectations are understated. CONTRIBUTING.md:133 mentions lint, typecheck, and test; CI runs 12 gates. A first PR that passes tests can still fail nine other ways with no forewarning. List them, or point at the check:all manifest.

Also worth adding while in the file: how to find work. The good first issue label exists (.github/labels.yml:166, docs/labels.md:101) but no document tells newcomers to filter by it, and the Discord is not mentioned here.

title: Article IX auto-merge gate fails open: gh api /pulls/:n/files keys entries 'filename', not 'path', so the changed-file list was always empty
description:
The "Article IX check" step in .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml did not detect protected paths on ANY pull request. It failed OPEN — it armed auto-merge instead of refusing.

CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (the original filing guessed an async race; the evidence does not support that):

The step ran
  CHANGED=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}/files" --paginate -q '.[].path')
The REST files API keys each entry `filename`. There is no `path` key. Only gh's GraphQL-backed `gh pr view --json files` uses `path`.

Verified against the live API:
  $ gh api repos/jayminwest/warren/pulls/644/files -q '.[0] | keys'
  ["additions","blob_url","changes","contents_url","deletions","filename","patch","raw_url","sha","status"]

So `-q '.[].path'` emitted one EMPTY LINE per changed file. `echo "" | grep -qE "$PROTECTED"` never matched, hit=false every time. The protected-path regex was never the deciding factor and neither was timing — the input was structurally empty on every run.

WHEN IT BROKE: 36d58c95 (#609, K8s migration, 2026-07-17) switched the step from `gh pr view "$PR_URL" --json files -q '.files[].path'` (correct for that shape, introduced in 8d768264/#337 and working) to the REST endpoint, to fix the 100-entry pagination cap (warren-88e1). The `-q` selector was carried over unadjusted. The gate has been blind from 2026-07-17 until this fix.

WHY THE ORIGINAL RACE THEORY IS WRONG: the filing claimed run 30381672277 "correctly reports hit=true and skips enabling". It did not. Both runs on PR #644 executed the "Enable auto-merge (squash)" step to `success`:
  run 30381569739 — Article IX: success, Enable auto-merge (squash): success
  run 30381672277 — Article IX: success, Enable auto-merge (squash): success
Neither log contains the "protected paths changed" line. A race would produce an intermittent result; this was uniform. (An async race in the files API may well also exist — it is simply not what caused this.)

AUDIT (swept merged PRs from 2026-07-17 to 2026-07-28, matching each PR's then-current protected pattern):
  #616 — .warren/triggers.yaml, docs/CONSTITUTION.md   [auto-merge armed: Enable step ran, run 29851115872]
  #626 — .canopy/agent.json                            [auto-merge runs no longer listed for the branch]
  #629 — .canopy/agent.json                            [auto-merge armed: Enable step ran, run 30165956391]
  #644 — .canopy/prompts.jsonl, .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml, .warren/triggers.yaml, docs/CONSTITUTION.md
  #617 — src/registry/builtins/* — NOT a bypass; that prefix was only added to the pattern by #644 itself.
Four PRs touched then-protected paths while the gate was blind. #616 and #629 came from `warren/run_*` branches — agent-opened PRs amending the constitution and the cron triggers, which is precisely what Article IX exists to prevent. Nothing merged before 2026-07-17 is implicated; the earlier selector was correct.

FIX (landed):
1. Source the diff from git, not the files API: `git diff --name-only "${BASE_SHA}...${HEAD_SHA}"`, with a checkout pinned to `pull_request.head.sha` (the default `refs/pull/N/merge` ref is itself asynchronously computed). No API field name can silently empty the list again.
2. FAIL CLOSED. An empty list, or a diff that cannot be computed, now writes hit=true and refuses. A pull request always changes at least one file, so empty means the source was unreliable — never that the diff was clean. This is what turns any future breakage into a refusal instead of a bypass.
3. The step now logs the file count and its decision on every path, including the permit path, which previously printed nothing at all.

REGRESSION COVERAGE: scripts/article-ix-gate.test.ts — 15 tests. Parses the workflow YAML and executes the step's embedded shell against a scratch git repo: each protected prefix refuses; a protected path hidden among 120 ordinary files still refuses; an empty diff and an unreadable diff both refuse; ordinary PRs pass; `^`-anchoring is not over-eager; the merge step is gated on `hit == 'false'` (not `!= 'true'`, which would read an unset output as a pass); and the job stays scoped to `github.repository_owner`.
closeReason: Fixed by commit ba9abe3a (PR #649) on main: Article IX gate now reads the changed-file list from the git diff instead of gh api /pulls/:n/files 'path' keys, closing the fail-open; regression tests added

title: bundle-size-autoheal did not fire on an agent-pushed PR branch (PR #656) — verify trigger conditions
description: PR #656 failed CI only on check:bundle-size (+2068B over after a merge from main) — exactly the overshoot the autoheal workflow exists to fix by pushing re-baselined budgets back to the PR branch. It never ran; a manual re-baseline was required. Suspect the workflow does not trigger on branches updated by warren's push identity (same suppressed-event class as warren-a2dc) or its path/event filter missed the merge push. Verify and fix the trigger.
closeReason: Root cause confirmed in .github/workflows/bundle-size-autoheal.yml: job-level guard required workflow_run.event == 'pull_request', but warren pushes agent branches directly so PR-branch CI (e.g. PR #656) often runs as 'push' and was silently dropped. Fix: dropped the event-type guard; a new pr-gate step (gh api pulls?head=owner:branch&state=open) proves the branch has an open same-repo PR before any checkout/build, with remaining steps gated on it. Loop guard, fork skip (head_repository check), and App-token push semantics unchanged.

title: A release is published before its container image exists
description:
`release.yml` creates the GitHub Release in the `release` job, and `deploy` — the job that builds and pushes `ghcr.io/jayminwest/warren:vX.Y.Z` — is `needs: release`, so it runs afterwards. When an image build fails, the tag and the published Release already exist.

That is how v0.12.0 and v0.12.1 ended up tagged and released with no image. The `announce` job compounds it: its Discord embed footers `docker pull ghcr.io/jayminwest/warren:vX.Y.Z` for an image that was never pushed, and `/releases/latest` points self-hosters at the same dead tag.

The problem is the ordering, not the mechanism. Publishing as a prerelease and promoting after `deploy` succeeds would fix it; so would moving release creation after `deploy`; so would something else. Not proposing one here.

Worth noting a second beneficiary: any consumer that asks "what is the newest release I should point at" currently cannot trust the answer.
closeReason: release.yml now creates the GitHub Release as a draft, builds+pushes the image in deploy, then a new promote job (needs: [release, deploy]) flips the draft to final via 'gh release edit --draft=false --latest'; announce now needs [release, promote] so it only fires after both the image is pushed and the Release is public

Plan template: feature
Plan approach: Forward-chained in three waves. Wave 1 (steps 1-8) is single-source consolidation that the CLI then stands on: fix the live drift bugs, move the response envelopes into src/core/wire.ts so check:wire-types guards them for free, build the…

Run `sd plan show pl-882c` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

The `warren` command surface is only described by the commander chains in `src/cli/main.ts`. Anything that wants a CLI reference — a docs page, a consumer, a model reading the repo — has to parse that source, and a refactor of the `.command(...)` chains silently invalidates whatever did the parsing.

This repo already has the pattern for the fix: `docs/openapi.yaml` is generated from `ROUTE_TABLE` and held in place by `gen:openapi:check`, and `docs/http-api.md` is generated the same way. The CLI is the remaining public surface with no generated counterpart.

Deliberately not specifying the shape. Markdown, JSON, both, emitted at build time or on demand, gated or not — all open. The property that matters is that the command surface is readable without parsing the implementation, and that it cannot drift from the code.
closeReason: CLI reference is now a generated artifact: src/cli/reference.ts walks the live commander program into plain data (prime.ts consumes the same walk, so prime and the docs can never disagree); scripts/generate-cli-reference.ts renders docs/cli-reference.md (20 commands, global options, env contract, exit-code table) with a --check drift mode wired as gen:cli-ref:check inside the lint gate, mirroring gen:docs/gen:openapi. check:all 12/12 green.

title: Separate the design tokens from the UI stylesheet
description:
`src/ui/src/index.css` holds the token set — the `@theme` block and the `:root[data-theme="dark"]` overrides — inline with Tailwind imports, custom variants, font faces, and base element rules.

Two costs. A token change arrives as a diff buried in a general stylesheet, so a color moving is easy to miss in review. And anything that wants just the tokens has to locate the blocks by brace matching, which breaks whenever the file is restructured.

Splitting the token declarations into their own file, imported by `index.css`, would make the set independently reviewable and diffable. Whether that is one file or two, CSS or JSON or both, is open.

title: Run stats crashes for spectators: public projection drops costUsd/priced/totals.cost but UI types them required
description:
## Symptom

`/run-analytics` throws for an anonymous visitor and falls through to the error
boundary. Reproduced on the live instance (app.warren.run) and on a local
`WARREN_AUTH=public` boot. The nav entry for "Run stats" carries no capability
(`src/ui/src/components/Layout.tsx`), so a spectator can reach the page and
crash it.

## Cause

Wire-type drift between the server's public projection and the UI's hand-typed
copy — the same drift class as warren-b229.

The server redacts three fields for a `readPublic`-only caller
(`src/server/handlers/runs/analytics.ts`):

- `REDACTED_RUN_TOTALS_FIELDS = ["cost"]`
- `REDACTED_RUN_GROUP_FIELDS = ["costUsd", "priced"]`

`PublicRunAnalytics` models this correctly server-side. The UI does not:
`src/ui/src/api/client.ts` types `RunGroupBucket.costUsd` / `.priced` and the
totals `cost` block as REQUIRED, so the consumers dereference them unguarded:

- `src/ui/src/pages/run-analytics/KpiCards.tsx` — `totals.cost.total`
  → `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'total')`
- `src/ui/src/pages/run-analytics/Tables.tsx` — `formatCostUsd(b.costUsd)`
  → `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')`
- `src/ui/src/pages/run-analytics/TokenStats.tsx` — `costPer1M(b.costUsd, ...)`

Verify: `curl https://app.warren.run/analytics/runs?days=7 | jq .byAgent[0]`
has no `costUsd`.

## Why it matters now

warren-14fc (#641 / PR #664) just fixed the dead agent link and humanized the
failure-reason pie ON THIS PAGE, specifically for public visitors. None of that
is reachable for a spectator until this crash is fixed.

## Fix sketch

Make the UI types honest about the projection rather than patching each call
site. `RunGroupBucket.costUsd` / `.priced` and the totals `cost` block become
optional, and the three consumers render the same em-dash / omitted-cell
treatment the rest of the redacted-field surfaces already use — see the
`redacted wire fields render on presence (warren-f53e)` block in
`src/ui-tests/capability-layer.test.ts` for the established pattern.

Preferred: re-export the server's `PublicRunAnalytics`-aware shape rather than
maintaining a second hand-written copy, per the "Single source of truth"
section in CLAUDE.md. A second copy is what produced this bug.

## Acceptance

- Run stats renders for an anonymous visitor with cost columns absent (not
  zeroed, not crashed)
- Operator view unchanged: all cost figures still render
- A test pins the spectator shape so the drift cannot silently return

Found while reviewing PR #664; reported in that PR's description and split out
deliberately to keep #664 to one concern.
closeReason: Re-close: fix merged in PR #665 (16:47Z, run_702gb23bf7wk) — UI wire types made optional for redacted analytics fields, consumers render on presence, capability-layer test pins the spectator shape. The original close was lost when a duplicate warren-e274 row (open copy from a9747f2c vs closed copy from PR #665) was resolved to the open copy by subsequent .seeds merges (PRs #668/#669).

title: Deployed instance (0.12.2) still seeds .canopy/agent.json into run workspaces — warren-5585 fix is merged but unreleased
description:
Observed live on run_svzavkys559z (2026-07-30, app.warren.run): the pi builtin's system prompt tells the agent '/workspace/.canopy/agent.json is the rendered agent definition (warren seeded it)', and the 0.12.2 control plane seeds the envelope at that path. Main already fixed this — 3ca5d514 (warren-5585, #654) relocated the drop to gitignored .warren/agent.json and deleted the tracked .canopy/ tier — but that commit is in the unreleased block after v0.12.2, so the live instance keeps re-introducing .canopy/ into every workspace until the next release deploys.

Risk: the envelope lands on an untracked-but-not-ignored path in the clone; any agent 'git add -A' can sweep it into a PR (the exact failure class warren-5585 closed).

Fix: (1) primary — cut and deploy 0.13.0 so the deployed builtins/seed path match main (part of the release-integrity motivation alongside warren-3380/warren-89f2/warren-fe9f). (2) worth considering as defense-in-depth: reap-time seed-reset should also drop a stray .canopy/agent.json so a stale control plane can never ride the envelope into a PR.

UPDATE 2026-07-30 (dogfood pipeline): the predicted sweep HAPPENED — PR #667 (run_f9s8feqr0y9r, warren-3380) committed .canopy/agent.json into main via 'git add -A'. Removed from main in the pipeline wrap-up commit. Until 0.13.0 deploys, every run on the live instance re-seeds the envelope and any full-tree add can re-introduce it; the reap-time defense-in-depth drop suggested below is now evidenced, not hypothetical.
closeReason: Premise resolved: warren-5585 fix (PR #654) shipped in v0.13.0, released and deployed 2026-07-30 — the instance no longer runs 0.12.2

title: K8s runtime: concurrent run pods deadlock on the RWO repo-cache PVC (Multi-Attach); second run stalls in Init with no signal
description: RE-SCOPED 2026-08-01 (operator decision, dogfood session): resolve the RWO Multi-Attach deadlock by making the repo-cache OPT-IN and defaulting it OFF, rather than moving to RWX storage (GKE Filestore's 1TiB minimum ≈ $160-200/mo to share a ~$2/mo disk of small mirrors is not justified; direct clones cost seconds against 5-20min runs). The runtime fallback already ships: src/runtime/k8s/workspace-init.ts falls back to a direct GitHub clone when WARREN_K8S_REPO_CACHE_PVC is unset — no runtime code change needed. Deliverables: (1) remove the WARREN_K8S_REPO_CACHE_PVC env (and its comment block) from deploy/k8s/base/deployment.yaml so the default topology has no shared volume across run pods; (2) remove the warren-repo-cache PersistentVolumeClaim from deploy/k8s/base/pvc.yaml (keep warren-data), updating the header comment; (3) rewrite the repo-cache documentation in deploy/k8s/README.md (and any RUNBOOK-K8S.md mentions) as an explicit opt-in for single-node clusters: add the PVC + env back via overlay, RWO caveat, switch to RWX before a second node; (4) close this seed. The 'no signal' observability half (surfacing an Init stall in run state/events) is NOT in scope — it stays with warren-32f8. Original issue: concurrent run pods deadlock on the RWO repo-cache PVC (Multi-Attach); second run stalls in Init with no signal.
closeReason: Made the repo-cache opt-in and default-off (operator cost rationale: GKE Filestore's 1TiB RWX minimum is not justified to share a disk of small mirrors when direct clones cost seconds against 5-20min runs, and the RWO claim deadlocks concurrent run pods via Multi-Attach). Removed WARREN_K8S_REPO_CACHE_PVC + comment block from deploy/k8s/base/deployment.yaml (replaced with a pointer comment); removed the warren-repo-cache claim from deploy/k8s/base/pvc.yaml and rewrote its header (warren-data kept); dropped the repo-cache patch from overlays/kind and updated the overlays/gke comment. Rewrote deploy/k8s/README.md as a 'Repo cache (opt-in)' section with an overlay snippet (PVC + env), RWO single-node caveat, and RWX-before-second-node guidance; updated docs/RUNBOOK-K8S.md (env table, §5.3, §7.5, storage/capability bullets) to match. Annotated docs/design/k8s-migration.md (§4.3, §6.2, R2) as historical/superseded rather than rewritten. Runtime support in src/runtime/k8s/ untouched — the direct-clone fallback and opt-in cache path remain supported for single-node clusters. bun run check:all: 12/12 gates green.

title: Run state/events never surface pod-level scheduling or volume stalls — a 17-minute FailedAttachVolume showed only as 'queued'
description: Companion to the RWO repo-cache Multi-Attach bug: while run_f9s8feqr0y9r's pod was stuck in Init:0/1 on FailedAttachVolume (2026-07-30, ~17 min), GET /runs/:id reported state 'queued' and the run's event stream carried nothing. An operator watching the UI cannot distinguish 'waiting for a worker' from 'pod scheduled but wedged on infrastructure'. The K8sProvider could watch pod events (FailedAttachVolume, FailedScheduling, ImagePullBackOff) and emit them into the run's event stream, or at minimum surface a lastPodCondition field on the run object. Found during the 2026-07-30 dogfood pipeline.
closeReason: K8s provider now surfaces pod-level stalls onto the run event stream: new PodEventWatcher (src/runtime/k8s/pod-event-watcher.ts) list-watches core v1 Warning events (type=Warning field selector), correlates involvedObject pod name → run id via the PodWatcher cache, dedupes per event uid (transition-only, no flood on a 17-min stall; relists cannot re-flood), and boot wiring (runtime-wiring + k8s-pod-warning-sink) appends a structured k8s.pod_warning run event (reason, truncated message, pod phase, timestamps) published to the live broker. Shared list-watch loop extracted to list-watch.ts; LocalProvider untouched. Tests cover transition emit, repeat dedupe, relist dedupe, healthy-startup silence, and the run-stream sink.

title: A seeds close can be silently lost when duplicate rows for one id are resolved to the open copy at merge (observed: warren-e274)
description: warren-e274 was filed on main (a9747f2c) and closed by PR #665's branch (run_702gb23bf7wk), leaving two rows for the id after merge: one open, one closed. Subsequent agent PRs (#668, #669) each resolved the duplicate by deleting the CLOSED row — so the issue read open on main after its fix merged, and the close had to be manually restored with evidence. Two layers worth fixing: (1) reap-time seeds handling should never let duplicate rows for one id reach a PR (dedupe by id keeping the newest updatedAt, which also resolves open-vs-closed correctly); (2) sd doctor / sd sync could detect duplicate ids and refuse or repair. Observed during the 2026-07-30 dogfood pipeline; this loss class is a known failure mode in the dogfood protocol.

Observed 2026-07-30 in an agent worktree while committing the warren-fe9f diff: the pre-commit hook's check:all run leaked git state beyond the documented core.bare flip — the worktree branch ref was moved onto pr.test.ts fixture commits ('base'/'pr') and the index was emptied. Repaired with 'git config core.bare false' + 'git reset --mixed'. This is the same hermeticity class warren-fa84 / warren-035c closed (GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE env leaks under the hook), but a live, more destructive variant: fixture commits landed on the REAL repo's ref, meaning the isolation is still incomplete in hook context (likely another env var — GIT_WORK_TREE?, GIT_COMMON_DIR? — or a fixture spawning git before its beforeEach env-clear). A mulch ci failure record was written in the session. Fix: make the git fixtures fully hermetic under the pre-commit hook (spawn-site env allowlist rather than per-test clearing), and consider having the hook refuse to run the git-fixture suites when sandboxed.
closeReason: Escape path closed: scripts/article-ix-gate.test.ts spawned git with inherited env (hook's GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE diverted its 'base'/'pr' fixture commits onto the invoking repo). New canonical helper src/workspace/git/test-fixture.ts (mkdtemp-only roots, -C + GIT_* severing + GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES pin, assertFixtureHermetic guard) now backs every real-git fixture site (article-ix, pr-open.context, clone-apply, worktree, materialize, k8s workspace-init); regression suite src/workspace/git/test-fixture.test.ts proves fixture commits can't move the invoking repo's ref/index under simulated hostile hook env. check:all 12/12 green (also fixed pre-existing public-projections analytics 30-day-window time bomb).

title: pg migration 0027 hard-codes public schema in cascade FKs — breaks per-test schema substrate; #651 merged over red ci-postgres
description: src/db/migrations/postgres/0027_lumpy_silvermane.sql (cascade-delete, warren-41b3, #651) re-adds the events->runs and runs->projects FKs with drizzle-kit's schema-qualified REFERENCES "public"."runs" / "public"."projects". The ci-postgres substrate (withDb, src/db/testing.ts) runs migrations in a per-test schema via search_path, so the public-qualified reference targets a nonexistent relation and every pg test after the migration fails with 'relation public.runs does not exist' (first seen 2026-07-28 19:57 run; PreviewPortAllocator (postgres) suite). PR #651's own ci-postgres check FAILED and the PR merged anyway — ci-postgres is not a required status check, so path-filtered PRs can merge red (second-order issue worth its own decision). Fix: strip the public. qualifiers so the FKs resolve via search_path like every prior migration; harmless for already-applied public-schema DBs (drizzle journals by tag, applied migrations are not re-run).
closeReason: Fixed by PR #672 (fa6d279a, merged 2026-07-30): dropped the public schema qualifier from pg migration 0027 cascade FKs; no qualified refs remain in src/db/migrations/postgres/

title: Replace UI list polling with a global lifecycle event stream
description:
The list pages (Runs.tsx, PlanRuns.tsx, ready-plans.tsx) poll their endpoints with refetchInterval: 5000, re-fetching the full ~40KB /runs payload every 5s per open tab forever. LB telemetry (2026-07-29/30 traffic spike, project warren-502318) shows this polling dominates request volume (~4.9k of 8k sampled requests hit /runs) and drove response egress from ~100MB/day to ~2GB/day.

Design (pieces mostly exist):
1. Server: boot-wired LifecycleBus subscriber (src/runs/lifecycle-bus.ts; production emits wired in 213cfddf) publishes slim notifications {runId, hook, state, ts} into a small global broker exposed via a ServerDeps seam (handlers stay thin per layer rules). New route GET /events/stream?follow=1 tails it as NDJSON, mirroring tailRunEvents/RunEventBroker in src/runs/events.ts. Route table + gen:openapi regen.
2. UI: list pages keep useQuery but drop refetchInterval: 5000; one shared stream connection per tab, debounce-invalidate ['runs']/['plan-runs'] on notification (copy the RunDetail.tsx useEventStream + invalidate-on-event pattern). Keep a slow fallback poll (30-60s) plus reconnect-with-backoff — GCLB timeoutSec 3600 cuts streams hourly (already handled for per-run streams).

Net effect: idle tab goes from ~720 polls/hr x 40KB to a held-open connection that transfers bytes only on run state changes.
closeReason: Shipped GET /events/stream?follow=1: a global LifecycleStreamBroker fed by a boot-wired LifecycleBus extension (src/runs/lifecycle-stream.ts), exposed via ServerDeps.lifecycleStream, served as slim NDJSON {runId, hook, state, ts} lines, operator-gated, added to ROUTE_TABLE with docs/openapi regenerated. UI: Runs/PlanRuns/ready-plans dropped refetchInterval 5000 for a 45s fallback poll; one shared stream connection per tab (LifecycleStreamBridge in App.tsx) debounce-invalidates ['runs']/['plan-runs']/['ready-plans'] on each notification with reconnect-with-backoff via the now-generic runEventStreamLoop. All 12 check:all gates green.

title: bridge: drop pi's remaining per-delta noise events (tool_execution_update, message_start) + purge legacy message_update rows
description:
Follow-up to commit 6ed46514 (drop message_update telemetry). Verified in the live warren-dogfood Supabase instance 2026-07-30: the fix works — message_update writes stopped at 22:16 UTC (deploy) — but ~75% of persisted rows per post-fix run are still non-durable chatter, so the UI event counter (RunDetail 'Events (N)') still jumps in large steps.

Evidence (post-fix window 22:20-00:55 UTC): tool_execution_update 1304 rows, message_start 1279, tool_execution_start/end 1360, turn_start/turn_end 1184, vs only ~1100 durable content rows (text/thinking/tool_use/tool_result). Biggest run (run_17v10tsp44mc): 2265 events, 564 durable.

Root cause: burrow's pi parser (burrow/src/runtime/parsers/pi.ts) documents pi v0.74.0's vocabulary; pi has since grown tool_execution_update (streaming partial tool output — payload carries cumulative partialResult). Unknown to the switch, it falls into the default 'unknown -> state_change' branch, so it is persisted + published. Same delta-snapshot class as message_update; the final output is already durably stored as tool_result. message_start is an empty skeleton (content: [], stopReason: pending, zeroed usage) that nothing reads.

Fix lands WARREN-SIDE (per the burrow-absorption decision, warren-c80e — do not deepen the burrow parser dependency): widen isStreamingSnapshotTelemetry in src/runs/stream/bridge.ts to a general per-delta-noise filter dropping payload type tool_execution_update, and decide on message_start / turn_start / tool_execution_start/end. MUST KEEP turn_end: usage aggregation (src/runs/usage-aggregate.ts) reads state_change turn_end (pi) and result (claude-code) for cost/token totals via listUsageEvents. The filter is provider-agnostic (bridge sits above local + k8s).

Also: one-time cleanup DELETE of the 48,707 legacy message_update rows (~115 MB, ~85% of events payload bytes) in the live instance.

Nuance for later: dropping at the bridge means the UI never sees streaming partials; if mid-run typing UX is ever wanted, the shape is publish-but-dont-persist.
closeReason: Code half done: widened isStreamingSnapshotTelemetry into isPerDeltaNoiseEvent in src/runs/stream/bridge.ts — now drops message_update (telemetry), tool_execution_update and message_start (state_change) per-delta noise; deliberately keeps turn_start / tool_execution_start|end (once-per-invocation lifecycle markers) and turn_end (HARD CONSTRAINT: src/runs/usage-aggregate.ts reads state_change turn_end for cost/token totals). Comment block updated to document the full drop/keep set. Tests extended in src/runs/stream/bridge.test.ts (tool_execution_update + message_start dropped, message_update still dropped, turn_end + lifecycle markers pass). Warrent-side only per warren-c80e; burrow parser untouched. The DB purge half (48,707 legacy message_update rows) was already done manually by the operator on 2026-07-31. bun run check:all: 12/12 gates passed.

title: K8s run pod reached terminal phase without posting finalize result — investigate in-pod finalize loss (possible #682 agent-entrypoint regression)
description:
Observed live 2026-07-30, run_pnknyar9yw3d (warren-daef attempt, $3.43 lost): agent finished its work and was ~13 min into a silent bun run check:all when watchdog.terminal_reconciled fired (idleMs=802978, providerPhase=succeeded, providerExists=true), followed by reap_failed step=finalize 'run pod reached a terminal phase without posting a finalize result; in-pod finalize could not run' — every reap step (mulch_merge, seeds_close, plans_mirror, seeds_commit, branch_push) failed and the run ended finalize_failed. The pod exited 'succeeded' without the in-pod finalize ever posting. Timing suspect: PR #682 (rule-8 deletions) touched src/runtime/k8s/agent-entrypoint.ts + pod-spec.ts and deployed shortly before. Note the NEXT k8s run (run_m6br4vntg007) DID execute in-pod finalize (its push was rejected by GitHub, a different failure), so the entrypoint isn't wholly broken — investigate the interaction of long-silent tool calls, the watchdog idle reconcile, and pod termination. Salvage (warren-cd3b, #685) reduces the blast radius but the finalize loss itself needs a root cause.

---

## Root-cause diagnosis (investigation run, 2026-08-01)

**Verdict: NOT a #682 regression.** #682's diff to agent-entrypoint.ts and pod-spec.ts is comment-only (removed two `agent.pauseTimeoutMs` cross-references); the pause-machinery deletions don't touch the K8s path. #706 postdates the run (merged 2026-07-31). The deployed build at run time was ~#682: finalize-entrypoint still had the OLD `WARREN_FINALIZE_MAX_WAIT_MS` default of 300_000 (raised to 3_000_000 by #698/warren-5ea1 the NEXT day, in direct response to this incident) and no salvage (#685 landed 3h after the run).

**Causal chain (all timestamps corroborated):**

1. 22:16:27Z — pi (stdin-held runtime) issues bash tool call 126 (`bun run check:all`, timeout 1800s). The warren-side pod-log follow (src/runtime/k8s/log-stream.ts pump over log-follow.ts) went silent here and NEVER delivered another byte. The reconnect loop only advances when the follow's `onDone` fires; a half-open HTTP stream (no bytes, no FIN, no error — a silently dropped apiserver/LB connection mid-run) blocks `openAndConsume` forever. There is no read timeout and no idle liveness probe — true at the deployed commit and STILL TRUE AT HEAD.
2. ~22:24:2xZ — check:all actually FINISHED (~8 min is a normal quiet-runner duration); pi printed tool_result 126 + its terminal envelope (agent_end), the stdin-hold close-trigger fired, pi exited 0. All of it went into the dead follow — warren never saw logical completion, so no reap intent was ever parked while the pod lived. (Consistent with 126 tool_result vs 127 tool_use, and with the absence of any stdin_hold_timeout event — the in-pod 30-min idle watchdog never fired.)
3. ~22:24:3xZ — the in-pod finalize-entrypoint started polling `GET /runs/:id/finalize-intent`. With the then-default maxWaitMs=300s and warren blind, no intent arrived; it gave up and runAgentEntrypoint returned the agent's exit code 0 → container exit 0 → pod phase **Succeeded** at ~22:29:2xZ, taking the only copy of the commits (emptyDir) with it.
4. 22:29:49.985Z — the watchdog terminal-reconcile net (warren-c433) saw the terminal pod on its first tick after phase flipped (idleMs=802978 ≈ 803s since the last bridged event) and drove reap.
5. 22:29:56.5Z — finalizeK8sRun's pod-terminal fast-fail (warren-fd08) synthesized the failed FinalizeResult ('run pod reached a terminal phase without posting...'); warren-495d flipped the would-be-succeeded outcome to failed/finalize_failed. Pre-#685 there was no salvage, so the work was unrecoverable.

**Answers to the investigation questions:**
(1) If the agent exits while a long-silent tool subprocess runs, runAgent returns on proc.exited and finalize DOES run — but the container can absolutely exit before finalize's HTTP post: when no intent is parked within maxWaitMs, pollForIntent gives up and the entrypoint exits 0. With the old 300s default this window was far SHORTER than warren's slowest detection path (watchdog grace/tick, 45-min heartbeat), guaranteeing the loss whenever the bridge was blind.
(2) Yes — the intent-null give-up path (and the no-callback-credential skip) terminates the container as success without posting finalize. No trap-ordering/backgrounding bug; the wait budget was simply too small (fixed by #698).
(3) Yes — watchdog terminal_reconciled (outcome=succeeded) routed through reap, whose pod-terminal fast-fail converted the lost finalize into finalize_failed. The 'succeeded' providerPhase was itself a lie produced by exit-0-without-finalize (see warren-4d6a).

**Why the next run worked:** the blind-follow failure is per-connection luck; run_m6br4vntg007's follow stayed healthy, warren saw its terminal envelope, parked the intent in time, and in-pod finalize ran (its push rejection is unrelated).

**Follow-ups filed:** warren-029d (P1 — log-follow liveness/read-timeout; the true root cause, still open at HEAD), warren-4d6a (P2 — entrypoint should exit non-zero when finalize never posts so pod phase can't masquerade as Succeeded). #698/warren-5ea1 already closed the too-small maxWait window; #685/warren-cd3b added salvage.
closeReason: Root cause confirmed: the warren-side K8s pod-log follow has no liveness/read timeout — a half-open HTTP stream at 22:16:27Z silently muted the event bridge for the rest of the run (log-stream.ts only reconnects on onDone; no idle probe, still true at HEAD). Warren never saw pi's agent_end after check:all finished, so no finalize intent was parked; the in-pod finalize gave up after the then-default 300s maxWait (raised to 50min by #698 the next day) and the container exited 0 → pod Succeeded, losing the only copy of the commits. The watchdog terminal-reconcile net (warren-c433) reaped at idleMs=803s and finalize's pod-terminal fast-fail (warren-fd08) produced finalize_failed. #682 exonerated (comment-only diff to those files). Follow-ups: warren-029d (P1, log-follow liveness — true root cause) and warren-4d6a (P2, exit non-zero when finalize never posts).

description: 2026-07-31 dogfood: a fresh (non-ref) dispatch of warren-d923 succeeded agent-side but reaped as finalize_failed with prUrl null; the retry with an identical prompt succeeded (run_0788cefjmpgd, PR #692). warren-b94b only covers stale host clones on REF-dispatch, so this is either a distinct finalize path bug or b94b's class is wider than documented. closeReason: Root cause: the agent process exited (code 0 → pod phase Succeeded) without warren ever observing a terminal envelope (stream severed mid-tool — no result/agent_end), so no reap intent was ever parked while the pod was alive. The in-pod finalize gave up polling after only 300s (WARREN_FINALIZE_MAX_WAIT_MS) and exited — which is what flipped the pod terminal — and warren's terminal-reconcile watchdog then reaped into a dead pod: 'terminal phase without posting a finalize result', work destroyed with the emptyDir (0.13.0 also predates warren-cd3b salvage). The 300s give-up was far shorter than warren's slowest intent-parking path (45-min heartbeat watchdog → reap), and the pod stays Running while it waits, so pod-terminal backstops could never fire — a circular deadlock guaranteeing loss. Fix: (1) in-pod finalize now waits 50 min (outlasting the 45-min heartbeat watchdog) and banks a proactive no_intent salvage bundle at the old 5-min mark while still waiting, so a slow warren finds a live pod for the full finalize and a dead warren still leaves the bundle; (2) failedFinalizeResult carries an unposted cause (timeout/pod_terminal/pod_gone) and reap maps it to a NEW failureReason finalize_unposted, distinct from finalize_failed (a posted result whose push failed — warren-b94b's class); (3) reap surfaces a pod-posted salvage from the run row (reap.workspace_salvage_recorded, salvage in reap.completed) and lets destroy proceed when the work is durable; (4) UI label + regression tests at the entrypoint/provider/reap seams.

title: Run evicted mid-flight (run_ccj2pvf767pt, warren-3995 attempt 1): $0.58 of work discarded; surface eviction cause and consider graceful drain

title: bundle-size-autoheal cannot heal: materializeProjectWorkspace/readHostGitIdentity tests fail on the autoheal runner (host git identity sensitivity)
description: 2026-07-31 dogfood: PR #690 overshot gzip budgets by ~2KB after a main merge — exactly autoheal's job — but the workflow's check:all died in check:coverage on 5 tests (materializeProjectWorkspace carve/fork, identity is null when host config empty, readHostGitIdentity both/one-half) that PASS in regular CI. Those tests read the RUNNER's host git config, so they are environment-sensitive; the autoheal runner has a different git identity state than the ci.yml runner. Make the tests hermetic (inject/stub host identity, e.g. HOME to a temp dir) so autoheal's gate matches CI. Until then autoheal silently fails closed and a human/agent must re-baseline (PR #690 needed a local worktree fix).
closeReason: Root cause: git config --get for the host identity ran with cwd = the checked-out warren repo, so a repo-LOCAL user.name/user.email (which the autoheal workflow configures to commit its re-baseline) overrode the tests' pinned GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL. Made the two isolatedEnv helpers (identity.test.ts, materialize.test.ts) fully hermetic by adding GIT_DIR pointing at an empty dir inside the temp HOME, severing repo discovery; added a regression test proving a cwd repo-local identity can't leak in. Verified both env states: tests pass with normal CI env AND with a repo-local identity configured in /workspace plus a bare HOME (autoheal-runner simulation); repo local config restored clean afterwards. bun run check:all: 12/12 gates.

title: k8s runtime: GET /runs/:id/events closes after replay instead of following a live run (observed on app.warren.run 0.13.0)
description: 2026-07-31 dogfood: two authenticated curl -N connections to /runs/run_vaj2bmmtrfqf/events (run state=running, claude-opus-5 actively emitting) each replayed persisted events (seq 1-17, then since=17 replayed 18-29) and exited cleanly in <1s instead of holding open to follow. Deployed image commit 6ed46514, version 0.13.0, WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s, no WARREN_EVENT_STREAM_* env set. Consequence: UI live-tail works only via the error/reconnect resume loop (constant reconnect churn against the connection cap from warren-25f6), and the RUNBOOK-K8S >30s Ingress stream verification (warren-63e4, BackendConfig timeoutSec=3600) cannot be performed. Determine whether the k8s event-ingestion path signals end-of-stream after each poll batch, and make the handler hold the connection and follow while the run is non-terminal.
closeReason: Root cause: GET /runs/:id/events defaulted follow=false, so any client not passing ?follow=1 got replay-then-close even on a live run (broker.close only ever fired bridge-side; nothing handler-side held the connection). Fix: (1) handler defaults follow to !isTerminalRunState(run.state) — live runs follow by default, terminal runs keep replay-then-close, explicit ?follow=0|1 still wins; (2) tailRunEvents gained a terminal backstop that polls run state (1s default), aborts the broker subscription via a linked AbortController, drains events committed-but-never-published, then closes — no dangling follow connections when no bridge remains (warren restart, finalize racing connect); (3) runtime-agnostic — both local and k8s ingest through the same bridge/broker path; (4) handler-level regression tests: live event delivery after connect on a bare request, prompt close on terminal transition, terminal replay-then-close; domain tests for backstop drain + transient probe failures; (5) RUNBOOK-K8S stream-verification note updated (bare curl now follows a live run; ?follow=0 forces replay).

title: warren run (CLI) races burrow finalize: successful run reaped as failed/crashed, PR auto-open skipped
description:
Mirrors GitHub issue #663 (https://github.com/jayminwest/warren/issues/663).

One-shot CLI (warren run) can mark a successfully completed claude-code run as failed / failure_reason: crashed, skipping PR auto-open, even though the agent exited cleanly and the branch was pushed. HTTP dispatch path (POST /runs) handles the same run correctly.

Root cause: src/cli/commands/run.ts defaultFetchRunState polls burrow status() exactly once immediately after the NDJSON stream ends; the stream's terminal result envelope can arrive a few hundred ms before burrow finalizes the run row, so the probe sees phase: running and maps it to failed. inferFailureReason then labels it crashed and pr-open is skipped. The server bridge is race-free because detectRuntimeTerminal (src/runs/stream/terminal-detect.ts) derives the outcome from the in-stream result envelope (is_error).

Suggested fix (either/both):
1. CLI path reuses in-stream terminal detection like the server bridge — result envelope's is_error sets the outcome directly, status() probe only as fallback.
2. defaultFetchRunState tolerates finalize lag: bounded retry (a few seconds) while phase is queued/running before assuming failed.

Impact: exit code 1 for successful work, PR auto-open skipped, plan-runs/seeds gates keyed on succeeded treat the run as failed. Labels on GH: priority/P1, type/bug, area/cli, area/runs, effort/small.
closeReason: Fixed CLI finalize race (mirrors GH #663): runRun now prefers the bridge's in-stream terminal detection (BridgeRunStreamResult.terminalDetected, derived via detectRuntimeTerminal on the result envelope's is_error) over the status() probe, and threads terminalDetected.failureReason (e.g. oom_killed) into reapRun instead of re-inferring 'crashed'. defaultFetchRunState (src/cli/commands/run.ts) is now a bounded-retry fallback (250ms poll, 5s budget, injectable) that rides out burrow's finalize lag while the phase is queued/running instead of mapping the first non-terminal read to failed. Tests: src/cli/commands/run.test.ts gains in-stream-outcome-wins / failureReason-passthrough / probe-fallback cases; new src/cli/commands/run.fetch-state.test.ts covers the retry paths. bun run check:all: 12/12 gates green.

title: K8s pod-log follow has no liveness/read timeout — a half-open stream silently mutes the event bridge (root cause of warren-3047)
description:
Root cause surfaced by warren-3047 (run_pnknyar9yw3d, 2026-07-30, finalize_failed, $3.43 lost).

Causal chain: 22:16:27Z the agent (pi, stdin-held) issued bash tool call 126 ('bun run check:all', timeout 1800s) and the event bridge went silent for the rest of the run. The pod itself was healthy: check:all finished (~8 min later), pi emitted its tool_result + agent_end and exited 0 — but NONE of those events reached warren. src/runtime/k8s/log-stream.ts only advances its reconnect loop when the follow's onDone fires; a half-open HTTP log-follow (no bytes, no FIN, no error — e.g. a silently dropped LB/apiserver connection mid-stream) blocks openAndConsume forever. There is no read timeout and no idle liveness probe, at the deployed commit AND still at HEAD. Warren stayed blind, never saw the terminal envelope, never parked a finalize intent; the in-pod finalize gave up (then-default WARREN_FINALIZE_MAX_WAIT_MS=300s, raised to 50 min by #698/warren-5ea1 the next day) and the container exited 0 → pod phase Succeeded with the only copy of the commits. The watchdog terminal-reconcile net (warren-c433) reaped 803s later and finalize fast-failed on pod-terminal (warren-fd08) → finalize_failed.

Fix: add a liveness guard to the K8s log follow in src/runtime/k8s/log-stream.ts / log-follow.ts: if the follow delivers no bytes for a bounded window while deps.probe() reports the pod Running, abort the connection and force a sinceTime resume; if probe reports the pod terminal, drain the tail and end the stream. This converts a permanent blind window into a bounded reconnect and lets warren observe terminal envelopes (or pod exit) even when the HTTP stream half-opens. Note the warren-4f2b pod-WATCHER already has a resync timer for the same 'silently stalled stream' shape — the log follow needs the equivalent.
closeReason: Added a liveness guard to the K8s pod-log follow: src/runtime/k8s/log-stream.ts now races each ChunkQueue pull against a per-byte-reset stall window (stallTimeoutMs dep, default DEFAULT_LOG_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS=5min, env WARREN_K8S_LOG_STREAM_STALL_MS, 0 disables, malformed values throw). On a trip the connection is aborted and the pump falls through to its existing probe: pod Running -> sinceTime resume (seq/high-water dedup keeps it lossless + dup-free), pod terminal -> drain tail + end. Extracted LogConnection/CursorState/sink types into src/runtime/k8s/log-connection.ts to stay under the file-size ratchet; src/runtime/k8s/provider.ts wires resolveLogStallTimeoutMs(env) into streamEvents. New tests in src/runtime/k8s/log-stream.stall.test.ts cover healthy-stream-no-trip (per-byte reset), half-open+Running resume without loss/dup, from-start resume, half-open+terminal drain+end, warn logging, and the env resolver. Mirrors the warren-4f2b pod-watcher resync precedent. bun run check:all: 12/12 green.

title: In-pod agent entrypoint should exit non-zero when finalize never posts — pod phase Succeeded is a lie for a lost run
description:
Residual hardening from the warren-3047 investigation (run_pnknyar9yw3d).

src/runtime/k8s/agent-entrypoint.ts runAgentEntrypoint returns the AGENT's exit code even when runFinalizeEntrypoint gave up without posting a result (no intent within maxWaitMs) — so the pod's terminal phase reads Succeeded for a run whose committed work was never pushed. Downstream this forces warren-495d's flip (succeeded → failed/finalize_failed) at reap time and made the warren-3047 incident read as 'pod succeeded' in the watchdog.terminal_reconciled event, which initially looked like a contradiction.

Proposal: when the finalize entrypoint returns false / fails to deliver the result (and a callback credential was present), exit the container non-zero so the pod phase reads Failed and status-map/watchdog classify it truthfully (terminalReason 'error' instead of a fake 'succeeded'). Keep the agent's own non-zero exit as-is. Coordinate with warren-029d (log-follow liveness) — with both fixes the warren-3047 failure shape becomes impossible to misread.
closeReason: runAgentEntrypoint now returns EXIT_FINALIZE_NOT_DELIVERED (75, EX_TEMPFAIL) when the agent exited 0 but runFinalizeEntrypoint failed to deliver with a callback credential present, so the pod phase reads Failed (status-map terminalReason 'error') instead of a lying Succeeded. Agent's own non-zero exit unchanged; no-credential path unchanged. Files: src/runtime/k8s/agent-entrypoint.ts (logic + docs), src/runtime/k8s/agent-entrypoint.test.ts (4 new tests).

title: POST /runs neither persists nor echoes ref — dispatchers cannot verify a ref-pinned dispatch took
description: Dogfood finding (2026-07-31 P1 session): POST /runs accepts ref in the body (src/server/handlers/runs/dispatch.ts reads it and threads it to spawnRun) but the run row does not persist it, so both the POST response and GET /runs/:id report ref=null even when a ref was honored. A dispatcher pinning a repair run to a PR branch (ref + targetBranch) cannot confirm from the API that the base ref took — during the session this looked like a dropped field and cost a verification round-trip into the handler source. Fix direction: persist ref on the run row (like targetBranch, warren-709e) or at minimum echo it in the dispatch response.
closeReason: ref persisted on runs row and echoed in POST /runs + projections

title: plan-run ref is not honored as PR base — chained children cannot accumulate on a non-default parent branch
description:
Restated 2026-08-16 against the post-Forge code, as the original 2026-08-11 deferral required — the Forge campaign (pl-d1c9) is done, so base-branch resolution now sits behind the Forge contract in the reap path and this is no longer deferred.

POST /plan-runs accepts `ref` and each child workspace is cut from it (src/plan-runs/dispatch.ts:60 — `ref = planRun.ref ?? project.defaultBranch`), but reap-time PR opening still hardcodes the PR base to the project default branch: src/runs/reap/pr-open.ts:121, :130, and :224 all pass `baseBranch: input.project.defaultBranch`, and src/runs/reap/run.ts:125 resolves `baseBranch` from `project.defaultBranch` for the ahead-count. The pr-open input type (pr-open.ts:65, :164) carries only `defaultBranch` — the run's ref never reaches it.

Consequences with a non-main ref: (1) every child PR targets the default branch, not the parent branch; (2) the chain stops accumulating — child N+1 clones from the stale parent branch that never received child N's merged work, so forward-chained plans break at step 2; (3) the merge gate (src/plan-runs/merge-gate.ts) checks only PR-merged, not merged-into-the-ref-the-next-child-clones-from. Originally found 2026-08-01 attempting to parallelize pl-4701 + pl-1717 on separate parent branches.

## DECISION 2026-08-16

PR base = ref. Thread the run's ref through reap so the child PR's base branch is the plan-run ref; merging the PR into the ref IS the parent-branch advance — no extra sync machinery. The merge gate's merged check then naturally means merged-into-ref. Rejected: keeping base=defaultBranch with a separate fast-forward step; dropping non-default-ref support.

Acceptance: a plan-run dispatched with ref=<branch> opens every child PR based on <branch>; after child N's PR merges, child N+1's workspace (cut from the ref) contains child N's work; a dispatch without a ref behaves exactly as today (base = defaultBranch).
closeReason: Threaded the run's frozen clone ref through reap as the PR base: run.ts resolves baseBranch = run.ref ?? project.defaultBranch (ahead-count + salvage + pipeline), pr-open.ts resolves the same base for gatherPrContext/draft/findPullRequest (head==base repair runs skip with reason branch_is_base), and the coordinator reopenPr seam in plan-run-wiring.ts uses run.ref ?? defaultBranch. Merge gate needed no change — its merged check on the PR now naturally means merged-into-ref. Tests: new src/runs/reap/pr-open.ref-base.test.ts (base resolution, exists-mode find, repair-run skip) plus a coordinator.gating.test.ts case proving a ref-carrying plan-run passes the parent-merge gate and dispatches with the ref. check:all 12/12 green.

title: Reap pr_open body can exceed GitHub's 64KB cap — 422 Validation Failed, no PR opened
description: Observed 2026-08-01 on a local (home-server) instance while live-testing pl-1c02: a run dispatched with a non-default ref against a project clone whose local main was months stale produced commitsAhead=1531, and the auto-PR body composed at reap (src/runs/reap/pr-open.ts, body built per warren-9ee3) exceeded GitHub's 65536-char limit. GitHub rejected creation with 422 'body is too long (maximum is 65536 characters)'; reap.step_failed step=pr_open, branch still pushed, run still succeeded (graceful). Fix: clamp the composed body to the API cap (truncate the commit list with an 'and N more' line), independent of the warren-8cbf base-ref fix that removes the inflated count in this scenario.

title: Workspace GC never converges: already-gone/destroyed burrows re-stranded every tick, readyz stale_burrow_workspaces permanently red
description: Observed 2026-08-01 live-testing pl-1c02 on the local (home-server) topology with a May-era warren_data volume: /readyz reported 15 stranded burrow workspaces with hint 'the fallback workspace GC reclaims these on its next sweep' — but two consecutive sweeps each logged scanned:16 stranded:15 destroyed:15 failed:0 (all workspace_gc.already_gone) and the readyz count never dropped. Root cause: findStrandedBurrows (src/runs/reap/gc.ts) derives candidates from burrowIds on terminal runs, but neither the per-reap workspace_destroy nor the GC's destroyed/already-gone outcomes clear run.burrowId or record destruction anywhere warren-side (burrow's deletedRuns/deletedEvents are burrow's own tables). So every reclaimed burrow re-strands next tick, the sweep issues a futile DELETE per burrow per 5min forever, and every terminal run joins the permanent red set once older than the 1h TTL (the fresh smoke run run_79d47dhvn075 was already the 16th scanned candidate). The readyz hint is a contract that lies, same category as pl-1c02 step 6. Fix direction: persist destruction (null burrowId or a workspace_destroyed_at stamp on the run rows, in both the reap destroy and both GC outcomes) and make the diagnostic/predicate honor it.
closeReason: GC persists destruction outcomes; findStrandedBurrows + readyz honor them; sweep converges

title: Agent-controlled event kind is trusted by terminal detection — a crafted state_change line on stdout terminalizes the run as succeeded
description: The K8s log parser validates stream (normalizeStream, src/runtime/k8s/log-parse.ts:108-112) but takes envelope.kind from the agent-owned stdout NDJSON verbatim (log-parse.ts:97), and src/db/repos/events.ts:41-55 appends it unvalidated. Terminal detection (src/runs/stream/terminal-detect.ts:40-52) reaps the run based on kind === "state_change" + stream === "system" + payload.type — and "system" is an accepted stream value an agent can emit. So an agent that prints {"kind":"state_change","stream":"system","payload":{"type":"agent_end"}} can terminalize its own run as succeeded, short-circuiting real outcome detection. Reap failure-reason inference (src/runs/reap/state.ts) also branches on agent-supplied kind values. Fix direction: distinguish warren-originated system events from runtime-forwarded transcript events at the parse layer (provenance tag, not kind string), or restrict terminal detection to events warren itself synthesizes. Related earlier parsing work: warren-2687, warren-36c0. Found during ontology/validation-gap audit 2026-08-02.
closeReason: Tagged stream events with parse-boundary provenance (warren-6646). Added EVENT_ORIGINS/EventOrigin to src/core/wire.ts (single source of truth) and NormalizedEvent.origin in src/runtime/contract.ts. src/runtime/k8s/log-parse.ts now classifies every pod-log line: only a line carrying the marker warren's in-pod emitter stamps (src/runtime/k8s/agent-io.ts formatEventLine) is origin 'warren'; an unattributed line is origin 'agent' and its self-declared stream 'system' is downgraded to 'stdout', so no consumer keyed on state_change+system (terminal detect, usage-aggregate, reap/provider-error) can read a terminal envelope off it. src/runs/stream/terminal-detect.ts adds a second, domain-side lock: detectRuntimeTerminal + isPiAgentEnd refuse origin==='agent'. LocalProvider (src/runtime/local/stream.ts) stamps 'warren' (host-side burrow classifies the transcript itself), and an absent tag stays trusted so burrow RunEvents/test sources are unchanged. Tests: src/runtime/k8s/log-parse.provenance.test.ts (forged state_change/system line does not terminalize; emitter envelopes still do) plus provenance-gate cases in src/runs/stream/terminal-detect.test.ts and log-stream.test.ts. Residual, documented in-code: the pod is one trust domain, so an agent deliberately writing a marker-bearing line at the entrypoint's stdout fd is still indistinguishable in-band; closing that needs UID separation between entrypoint and agent (filed separately). check:all 12/12 green.

title: targetBranch on POST /runs is an unvalidated push target — direct push to default branch bypasses PR review and the Article IX gate
description: A dispatch-capable caller can set targetBranch to the default branch (e.g. main) and the agent workspace is pushed straight there at finalize: src/runtime/k8s/finalize-collect.ts:211-214 builds refspec HEAD:<branch> from InPodFinalizeIntent.branch with no ref-grammar or policy check. composeRunBranch (src/runs/branch.ts:77-80) short-circuits prefix composition on any non-empty targetBranch, and the handler (src/server/handlers/runs/dispatch.ts:112) only checks typeof string. Contrast RunBranchPrefixSchema (src/warren-config/schema.ts:102-108) which does enforce a kebab-case grammar for the config-supplied prefix. Consequence: no PR is created, so the Article IX auto-merge gate (a PR-time check) never runs — protected paths can be modified on the default branch by any dispatch-capability token. Fix direction: validate targetBranch against a ref grammar at dispatch, and refuse (or require an explicit allow-knob for) targetBranch equal to project.defaultBranch. Found during ontology/validation-gap audit 2026-08-02.
closeReason: Validated targetBranch at the domain seam: new src/runs/target-branch.ts (git ref grammar + refusal of the project default branch, no opt-in knob), enforced in spawnRun (src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts) before any side effect, with tests in src/runs/target-branch.test.ts and src/runs/spawn/target-branch.test.ts. Repair runs targeting an existing PR head branch are unaffected.

title: POST /runs/:id/steer casts arbitrary priority string past INBOX_PRIORITIES — unknown value persists and makes the inbox sort comparator return NaN
description: src/server/handlers/runs/pause-resume.ts:54-56 does optionalString(body, "priority") as MessagePriority — typeof check only, no membership check against INBOX_PRIORITIES (src/core/wire.ts:75). The drizzle enum column (src/db/schema/sqlite.ts:395, postgres.ts:262) is TS-only narrowing; the repo has zero SQL CHECK constraints, so e.g. {"priority":"CRITICAL"} persists. Downstream, src/db/repos/run-inbox.ts:144-147 computes PRIORITY_RANK[b.priority] - PRIORITY_RANK[a.priority]; an unknown key yields undefined -> NaN, the comparator returns NaN, and Array.sort ordering for the claimed batch becomes implementation-defined — steering delivery order silently corrupts from a one-line curl. Fix: validate membership at the handler (enum already exists in wire.ts; zod is already a dependency) and 400 on unknown values. Same hardening applies to the unchecked metadata cast at src/server/handlers/runs/dispatch.ts:138. Found during ontology/validation-gap audit 2026-08-02.
closeReason: Validated steer priority against INBOX_PRIORITIES at the handler boundary (400 on unknown) via new src/server/handlers/body-fields.ts (optionalEnum/optionalObject); pause-resume.ts drops the MessagePriority cast; dispatch.ts metadata is shape-checked instead of cast; run-inbox.ts comparator ranks unknown priorities deterministically last so it stays total; tests in runs.pause-resume.test.ts, runs.dispatch.test.ts, run-inbox.test.ts

title: finalize-wire stage validator hand-lists six of seven FinalizeStage values (missing seed_reset); runtime contract.ts vocabulary is outside check:wire-types scope
description:
REMAINING SCOPE (re-scoped 2026-08-02): the finalize-wire half of this issue is DONE — validateStages in src/runtime/k8s/finalize-wire.ts no longer hand-lists stages; it derives membership from isFinalizeStage / FINALIZE_PIPELINE_STAGES in src/runtime/finalize-stages.ts (which includes seed_reset). Fixed by warren-357c / PR #746. Do not redo.

What remains is the structural half: src/runtime/contract.ts maintains a parallel wire vocabulary that check:wire-types cannot see. Verified sites on main:
- src/runtime/contract.ts:131 — RunPhase duplicates RUN_STATES (src/core/wire.ts).
- src/runtime/contract.ts:177 — MessagePriority duplicates INBOX_PRIORITIES.
- src/runtime/contract.ts:192 — inline inbox-state union duplicating INBOX_STATES.
- src/runtime/k8s/log-parse.ts:12 — NORMALIZED_STREAMS duplicates EVENT_STREAMS.
- scripts/check-wire-types.ts scopes only src/core/wire.ts canonical names with an empty ALLOW list, so none of the above is guarded.

Fix direction: unify. Make contract.ts and log-parse.ts derive from / re-export src/core/wire.ts rather than declaring parallel copies (convention: define once in wire.ts, re-export outward). Any genuinely deliberate local copy goes in check-wire-types.ts's ALLOW list with a why comment. Also consider widening DOMAIN_STEMS so these names are actually guarded going forward. Related: warren-b229, warren-d371, warren-357c.
closeReason: Unified the runtime seam onto the canonical wire vocabulary (src/core/wire.ts): src/runtime/contract.ts now derives RunPhase from RunState, MessagePriority from InboxPriority, Message.state from InboxState, and NormalizedEvent.stream from EventStream; src/runtime/k8s/log-parse.ts and src/runtime/local/stream.ts drop their private NORMALIZED_STREAMS copies for EVENT_STREAMS. Added src/runtime/contract.test.ts pinning the derivations at type + value level, and documented the guard's name-based blind spot in scripts/check-wire-types.ts (ALLOW stays empty; DOMAIN_STEMS needed no widening since every canonical export already carries a stem). Trimmed contract.ts prose to stay under check:size and ratcheted its budget 512 -> 510. The seed_reset / finalize-wire validateStages half was already fixed on main by warren-357c / PR #746 and was not redone. bun run check:all: 12/12 green.

title: plan_run_children and run_previews have no transition tables — any writer can move a child merged->pending or a preview torn-down->live
description: Runs and plan-run parents both have real legal-transition tables (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS, src/db/repos/runs.ts:38-50 and src/db/repos/plan-runs.ts:34-46) enforced with StateTransitionError -> 409.
