Tables enumerated from the live writers (src/plan-runs/coordinator.ts, src/plan-runs/in-flight.ts, src/preview/launch/orchestrate.ts, src/preview/port-allocator.ts, src/preview/teardown.ts). Tests: src/db/repos/plan-runs.test.ts, new src/db/repos/runs.preview-transitions.test.ts; fixtures that jumped states now walk the legal path via a new Harness.seedChildState helper.

title: .warren/config.yaml fails open — one unknown key silently drops the admission cap, quality gate, resource limits, and cost caps for every dispatch
description: DefaultsConfigSchema is .strict() (src/warren-config/schema.ts:368), so a single typo (e.g. maxConcurrentRun missing the s) fails the whole document. loadWarrenConfig (src/warren-config/load.ts:5-7) then yields defaults: null plus an errors[] entry, and consumers proceed on built-in defaults: src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts:221-223 reads projectDefaults?.admission?.maxConcurrentRuns and simply omits the cap. Every guardrail the file carries — admission cap, qualityGate, resource limits, cost caps — silently disappears at once. The error surfaces only in readyz (src/diagnostics/checks-config.ts:73), the trigger tick log, and the UI; no dispatch is refused. Fix direction: a project with a present-but-unparseable .warren/config.yaml should refuse dispatch (or at minimum refuse to drop admission/cost guardrails) rather than degrade silently — parse errors in a guardrail file should fail closed. Found during ontology/validation-gap audit 2026-08-02.
closeReason: Fail-closed guardrail config at dispatch. Added WarrenConfigInvalidError (src/warren-config/errors.ts, exported via index.ts, mapped to 422 in src/server/errors.ts). readProjectDefaults in src/runs/spawn/agent-cache.ts now calls the new assertGuardrailConfigUsable(), which throws when the loader reports a parse/schema error against a guardrail-bearing file (.warren/config.yaml or legacy defaults.json); triggers.yaml and pr-template.md stay non-blocking. Refusal fires before repos.runs.create so no orphan run. Kept whole-document .strict() rather than per-section salvage: per-section validation would still silently drop the exact knob the operator typo'd. Loader header contract in load.ts and docs/design/warren-config.md updated. New tests src/runs/spawn/guardrail-config.test.ts drive the real loader + real cache: unknown key -> refused with no RunSpec, bad YAML -> refused, valid config -> maxProjectConcurrency + WARREN_QUALITY_GATE enforced, no .warren/ -> unchanged, broken triggers.yaml -> still dispatches.

title: Agent runtime id is never validated against KNOWN_RUNTIME_IDS — an unknown runtime dies inside burrow at dispatch instead of 4xx at registration
description: KNOWN_RUNTIME_IDS = ["claude-code","sapling","pi"] is declared and zod-enforced at src/warren-config/schema.ts:226-229 — but only for the .warren/config.yaml interactive-runtime override. description:

DECISION 2026-08-04: deferred entirely past the 0.14.x polish pass, together with warren-8dbb. The UID split risks the single-uid assumptions on /workspace, HOME, the bun global store, and git config (see warren-fd08 fragility notes in Dockerfile.agent). Revisit after the Forge campaign with live-pod validation budgeted.

Follow-up to warren-6646. The provenance tag now strips system authority from any pod-log line warren's in-pod emitter did not author, but the marker itself is in-band: the agent shares the pod's UID/namespace, so a deliberate write at /proc/1/fd/1 can reproduce a marker-bearing envelope. Closing that residual needs an out-of-band attestation (an entrypoint-generated nonce registered with warren before the agent spawns) or, cheaper, running the agent under a different UID than the entrypoint (setpriv/su in the agent container) so the entrypoint's stdout fd is not writable by the agent. See src/runtime/k8s/log-parse.ts + src/runtime/k8s/agent-io.ts.
closeReason: Implemented the in-pod entrypoint/agent uid split. The agent container's entrypoint (pid 1, uid 1000) now setpriv-drops the agent process to WARREN_POD_AGENT_UID=1001 (gid 1000, clear-groups, no_new_privs, emptied inh/ambient/bounding cap sets) via src/runtime/k8s/agent-uid-drop.ts, so a forged write at /proc/1/fd/1 from the agent fails EACCES and the warren-6646 provenance marker is unforgeable from the agent side. Pod spec adds caps [SETUID, SETGID, KILL] for the entrypoint only + stamps WARREN_AGENT_RUN_AS_* env; the entrypoint preflights the drop (setpriv ... -- true) and fails the run legibly when ambient caps never arrive; WARREN_K8S_AGENT_UID_DROP=0 restores the legacy shape. Workspace writability preserved via fsGroup + umask 002 in workspace-init and the entrypoint; git safe.directory '*' is uid-agnostic. Dockerfile.agent ships util-linux (setpriv). DockerProvider unchanged (no in-pod entrypoint). Tests: agent-uid-drop.test.ts, agent-entrypoint.uid-drop.test.ts, pod-spec.uid-drop.test.ts; check:all 12/12 green. Live-pod validation REMAINS A RELEASE GATE — exact operator commands documented in docs/RUNBOOK-K8S.md §4.2 (marker-forge write must EACCES while clone/bun/git-commit still work as uid 1001).

title: Path traversal via percent-decoded route params: POST /runs/:id/salvage writes outside the salvage dir
description:
matchRoute percent-decodes every :param, but ([^/]+) only constrains the RAW pathname and URL.pathname preserves %2F. POST /runs/..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpwn/salvage therefore decoded to id='../../etc/pwn', which the salvage handler joined straight onto salvageDir - an arbitrary file write of up to 32MiB of caller-supplied bytes for any bearer holding the 'dispatch' capability (short of 'admin'). Verified end-to-end: the unpatched server wrote /tmp/pwned.bundle from a request whose salvage dir was a mkdtemp under /tmp.

Same decode also threw URIError out of matchRoute on a malformed escape (e.g. /runs/%ZZ/cancel). handleRequest calls matchRoute OUTSIDE its try/catch, so the connection died with ECONNRESET instead of returning warren's error envelope.

Fixed two layers: (1) router refuses a param that decodes to a path separator or NUL, and refuses a malformed escape, in both matchRoute and pathExists so a refused param is a 404 not a 405; (2) new salvageBundlePath() resolver validates the run id and asserts containment under the salvage dir, shared by the HTTP intake and the reap-side writer.

Also closed the sibling gap this audit surfaced: /runs/:id/salvage was missing from RUN_CALLBACK_ROUTE_PATTERNS, so every in-pod salvage POST (which carries the run-scoped token from warren-57fd) was 403'd and the pod's only recoverable copy of the run's commits died with the emptyDir.

title: Path-mode previews share warren's browser origin, so agent-authored preview code can read the operator token
description:
WARREN_PREVIEW_MODE=path is the default and serves each run's preview app at https://<warren-host>/p/<run-id>/ - the same browser origin as the warren UI, which keeps the operator bearer token in localStorage. The preview app is code an agent wrote, so any script it loads can read that token and drive the control plane as the operator. The proxy already strips Authorization and Cookie before forwarding upstream, so only the in-browser direction is open. Realistic path: a prompt-injected agent on a repo whose issue or PR text an attacker can influence, plus an operator who opens the preview.

Documented as a known V1 limitation in SECURITY.md with the operational mitigation (WARREN_PREVIEW_MODE=subdomain gives each preview its own origin). Not fixable with a response header: the sandbox CSP directive that would give the preview an opaque origin also makes the browser treat the preview's own sub-resource requests as cross-site, which blocks the SameSite=Lax preview cookie those requests need.

Candidate real fixes: (a) move the UI's operator credential off localStorage onto an HttpOnly cookie the preview origin cannot read; (b) serve path-mode previews from a distinct origin warren owns; (c) pair a sandbox CSP with SameSite=None on the preview cookie and re-derive the CSRF posture.
closeReason: Fixed in 07c34e89: path-mode previews now serve from a dedicated listener on WARREN_PREVIEW_PORT (default bind port + 1) — own browser origin, so preview code cannot read the operator token; warren origin 308-redirects /p/ paths; unix transport keeps legacy mounting with a boot warning

title: The no_intent salvage POST can land after the heartbeat watchdog terminalizes the run, and gets 401
description:
The run-scope gate (server.ts runActivityCheck) refuses a run-scoped token once the run row is terminal. That is at odds with the salvage intake, which exists precisely for the case where warren has lost track of the run - and the intake handler is explicitly written to tolerate a gone run row.

Concrete window, verified against the defaults: pollForIntent waits maxWaitMs = WARREN_FINALIZE_MAX_WAIT_MS, default 3_000_000ms (50 min). The heartbeat watchdog force-fails a silent run at DEFAULT_WATCHDOG_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_700_000ms (45 min). A pod waiting on an intent that never arrives is silent for the whole wait, so the watchdog terminalizes the row at 45 min and the terminal no_intent salvage POST at 50 min hits a terminal run -> 401 run_token_expired for all five attempts.

Not as bad as it looks: the warren-5ea1 early salvage fires at earlySalvageMs (default 5 min), well inside the budget, so a bundle is already banked. What is lost is the final, most complete capture.

Two paths that are NOT affected, checked explicitly: (1) push_failed salvage POSTs BEFORE finalize-result, so reap is still awaiting and the run is non-terminal; (2) the terminal-reconcile net (watchdog-reconcile.ts) only fires when the pod is terminal-or-gone, so it never races a live finalizing pod.

Candidate fixes: (a) exempt the salvage route from the liveness half of the run-scope gate, accepting a bounded write primitive (one file, one path pinned to the token's own run id, <=32MiB, idempotent) in exchange for durability; (b) default WARREN_FINALIZE_MAX_WAIT_MS below the heartbeat budget - smaller change but couples two independently tunable knobs.
closeReason: finalize max-wait default lowered below the watchdog budget (variant b); cross-budget test guards the ordering

title: Salvage intake has no rate limit or per-run quota on the pod's write path
description:
Follow-up to PR #772, which added /runs/:id/salvage to RUN_CALLBACK_ROUTE_PATTERNS (the route was previously 403'd for the run-scoped token every pod carries, so the pod's last recoverable copy of a run's commits died with the emptyDir).

The fix is correct and was the documented intent of warren-cd3b, but it opens a write path from the untrusted side: the agent shares the pod's UID/namespace (see warren-cb93), so an attacker-influenced agent that reads WARREN_API_TOKEN can POST to its own run's salvage intake. The write is bounded per request (one file, id pinned to the token's own run, <=32MiB, refused once the run is terminal) but there is no rate limit and no per-run quota. storeBundle (src/server/handlers/runs/salvage.ts) stages each POST as <bundlePath>.tmp-<uuid> before the rename, so N concurrent POSTs stage N tmp files of up to 32MiB each on the control-plane volume before any of them collapse onto the single final path.

Directions to evaluate: a per-run in-flight cap on the salvage route (one concurrent intake per run id); a per-run POST count/byte budget for the run's lifetime; or reusing whatever rate-limit seam the event-stream per-client cap (warren-25f6) established. Also worth confirming the tmp files are unlinked on a failed write rather than left behind.

Evidence: PR #772 review, src/server/handlers/runs/salvage.ts storeBundle, src/runs/spawn/run-token.ts RUN_CALLBACK_ROUTE_PATTERNS.
closeReason: salvage uploads capped to one in flight per run via the shared per-key limiter; tmp files cleaned in try/finally; lifetime byte budget skipped by decision

title: SDK getProject calls GET /projects/:id, which the route table does not register
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Step 1 of plan pl-882c.

Parent seed: warren-d089 — Agent-facing CLI + npm publish (ROADMAP Now item, 0.14 plan)
Plan template: feature
Plan approach: Forward-chained in three waves. Wave 1 (steps 1-8) is single-source consolidation that the CLI then stands on: fix the live drift bugs, move the response envelopes into src/core/wire.ts so check:wire-types guards them for free, build the…

Run `sd plan show pl-882c` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).

Spotted while reviewing PR #772; unrelated to that PR.

src/client/client.ts:133 getProject() issues GET /projects/${encodeURIComponent(projectId)}, but ROUTE_TABLE in src/server/handlers/index.ts only registers DELETE /projects/:id (line 268). There is no GET for a single project, so every getProject() call lands on the pathExists 405 branch (methodNotAllowed) rather than returning the row.

Two candidate resolutions, and the choice is a design call: (a) add GET /projects/:id with policy readPublic, projected the same way listProjectsHandler projects each row, which makes the SDK method work and closes the surface gap; or (b) delete getProject() from the SDK if the single-project fetch is not a surface warren wants, since consumers can filter GET /projects.

Whichever way it goes, this is the kind of drift the single-source-of-truth rule in AGENTS.md exists to prevent: the SDK is supposed to be a consumer of the HTTP route, not a declarer of routes that do not exist. Worth asking whether a guard can assert that every path the SDK constructs resolves to a ROUTE_TABLE entry, the way check:agents asserts AGENTS.md references resolve.
closeReason: Registered GET /projects/:id (policy readPublic) as a thin handler over a new getProject domain fn in src/projects/manage.ts; bare-row body matches SDK getProject. Projection reuses projectProject so spectators get PUBLIC_PROJECT_FIELDS only. Files: src/projects/{manage.ts,index.ts,get-project.test.ts}, src/server/handlers/{projects.ts,index.ts,index.test.ts,projects.get.test.ts}, regenerated docs/http-api.md + docs/openapi.yaml.

title: Agent name schema admits names the router now refuses (z.string().min(1) vs the kebab grammar every consumer assumes)
description:
Spotted while reviewing PR #772. That PR makes matchRoute refuse a route param whose percent-decoded value carries a path separator or NUL, which is correct — no legitimate caller sends one.

The one place warren's own schema is looser than that rule: the seed-file agent schema types name as z.string().min(1) (src/registry/schema.ts:35, src/registry/builtins/seed-file.ts:28), so an operator using WARREN_SEED_AGENTS_FILE can register an agent named 'foo/bar'. GET /agents/foo%2Fbar would have matched before #772 and 404s after it. Purely hypothetical today — all eight BUILTIN_AGENTS are simple kebab names and the canopy library tier is gone — but the schema is the only thing that makes it expressible.

Every other consumer already constrains the same value: trigger role must match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/ (src/warren-config/schema.ts:90). Tightening the registry name field to that same grammar makes the vocabulary agree across the config schema, the registry, and the router, and turns a silent 404 into a boot-time validation error with a useful message.
closeReason: registry name fields now enforce the kebab grammar shared with RoleNameSchema

title: CLI: bun auto-loads cwd .env, stale WARREN_API_TOKEN silently overrides client config and stdin token
description: The published CLI is raw bun-shebang TypeScript, so bun auto-loads .env from the invoking cwd. Consider: warn when the token source is an auto-loaded .env, or have login prefer stdin over env when stdin is piped, or document the footgun in prime/doctor hint.

title: Auto-retry infra-lost runs (burrow_run_lost): one re-dispatch as a new run linked via retryOf, cumulative spend cap
description:
null

## DECISION 2026-08-16 (design resolved — implementation-ready)

- Retry is a NEW run id linked to the original via a `retryOf` field. No attempt counter on the run row, no row migration beyond the link field.
- One automatic retry per infra-lost run, then terminal.
- Spend is cumulative: the retry inherits the original cap and the first attempt's spend counts against it — no fresh budget.
- Plan-run children reuse the warren-6de9 coordinator retry shape.
- Sequencing: dispatch AFTER warren-6de9 merges so this reuses its proven shape (dep edge added).

title: warren CLI silently absorbs stale credentials from cwd .env (bun auto-load) — login/doctor report invalid bearer token with no source hint
description:
Observed dogfooding 2026-08-04: the globally-installed warren CLI (bun-shebang) run from a repo root picks up that repo's .env via Bun's automatic .env loading. A stale WARREN_API_TOKEN there outranks both the token piped to 'warren login' on stdin (env > stdin precedence) and the persisted ~/.warren/client.json (env > file), so every command fails with '[unauthorized] invalid bearer token' even immediately after a successful 'warren login --token ...' (flag > env is the only escape). The operator gets no hint the credential came from ./.env rather than their config. Original diagnosis (String(Uint8Array) mangling in readTokenFromStdin) was WRONG — stdin path verified fine once the env var was cleared. Candidate fixes: (a) 'warren doctor' / auth-failure hints should name the resolved credential SOURCE (flag/env/.env-file/config-file); (b) document the bun .env auto-load footgun in the CLI env contract; (c) consider bunfig/--env-file=off for the CLI entrypoint if feasible. Repro: echo $GOOD_TOKEN | warren login --url <live> from a repo whose .env holds a stale WARREN_API_TOKEN.

CLOSED 2026-08-16 as duplicate of warren-8807 — same defect (bun cwd .env auto-load outranking client.json/stdin, no source hint), one fix covers both. Filed on GitHub as #898 under warren-8807.

title: K8s reap intent never issued after stdin_hold_timeout: run stuck running, pod polls finalize-intent forever
description:
Observed live 2026-08-06 on run_5p7nfj1bsn5m (plan-run plnr_45cpxtrd2k5k child 1, sapling). Sequence: agent settled 23:00Z -> stdin_hold_timeout 23:30Z (idleMs 1800000) -> pod polls GET /runs/:id/finalize-intent every ~2s, always 200 with no intent, indefinitely. reap.workspace_salvaged fired at 23:35 trigger=no_intent with nothing captured. Run row stayed running until pod deletion flipped it failed/burrow_run_lost. Cost of the hang: 30min hold + ~25min stuck + $1.76.

CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (session investigation 2026-08-06): structural deadlock in the stdin-hold path, systematic for every stdin-held (pi) K8s run that idles. The reap intent is written ONLY by the reap pipeline (src/runtime/k8s/finalize.ts:258 via src/runs/reap/pipeline.ts:215), and reap triggers ONLY on a terminal envelope: payload.type result|agent_end on the kind=state_change/stream=system carrier (src/runs/stream/terminal-detect.ts:53-63, src/core/event-envelope.ts:98-105), a terminal provider.status() phase, cancel, or the watchdog. When the idle watchdog (src/runtime/k8s/agent-stdin-hold.ts:203-216) closes stdin and kills pi, pi exits WITHOUT emitting agent_end -> no terminal envelope ever reaches the bridge; the pod then sits Running inside pollForIntent (src/runtime/k8s/finalize-entrypoint.ts:228-255, 40min ceiling) so provider.status() keeps reading running and the run-state poller never terminalizes either. stdin_hold_timeout itself is read by NOTHING in the control plane.

FIX SKETCH (spiked locally this session, reverted intentionally, gates were passing at revert): (1) in src/runtime/k8s/agent-entrypoint.ts runAgent, track whether any parsed RuntimeEvent was a terminal envelope; after agent exit, if none was seen, emitSystem a synthesized state_change {type: agent_end, synthesized: true, reason: agent_exit_without_terminal_envelope, exitCode, stopReason: error + errorMessage when exitCode != 0} — passes provenance (origin marker via agent-io formatEventLine) and detectRuntimeTerminal with no control-plane change. (2) agent-stdin-hold.ts onTimeout: closeStdinOnce() needs .catch (EPIPE from a dead child inside the timeout handler is a fatal unhandled rejection in the pod; the sibling in stop() already catches). (3) log-stream.ts pullNext: the orphaned queue.pull() chain needs a rejection handler. (4) make the hardcoded 15s STDIN_HOLD_KILL_GRACE_MS an env knob (WARREN_AGENT_STDIN_KILL_GRACE_MS) for testability. Watch check:size on agent-entrypoint.test.ts (near 500-line budget; split new tests into a sibling file).

RELATED FINDINGS not fixed here, see also warren-6016: run-state-poller maps exists:false to null (transient) so a vanished pod never terminalizes via the poller (src/runs/stream/run-state-poller.ts:44); poller aborted mid-sleep can miss the final probe (run-state-poller.ts:107 + bridge.ts:366); silent cold-resume line drop at log-connection.ts:116 and null-stamp anchor at :132-140; cancel leaves the row running through the 30s pod grace (src/runs/cancel.ts:190-206).
closeReason: Shipped the four-part fix: (1) runAgent tracks terminal envelopes via isTerminalEnvelope/extractAgentEventEnvelope and synthesizes a state_change agent_end (synthesized: true, reason agent_exit_without_terminal_envelope, exitCode, stopReason error + errorMessage on non-zero exit) post-exit when none was seen — passes provenance + detectRuntimeTerminal with no control-plane change; (2) closeStdinOnce() in the watchdog onTimeout now catches EPIPE rejections; (3) log-stream pullNext's orphaned queue.pull() chain resolves LOG_STALL on rejection instead of an unhandled rejection; (4) WARREN_AGENT_STDIN_KILL_GRACE_MS env knob replaces the hardcoded 15s grace. New tests in agent-entrypoint.synthesized-terminal.test.ts (agent-entrypoint.test.ts was near the size budget). bun run check:all 12/12 green.

title: K8s salvage window has no git credential: rescue push always skipped, uncommitted work unrecoverable
description: Companion to warren-9a4a, observed on run_5p7nfj1bsn5m. reap.workspace_salvaged notes: 'rescue push skipped: no git credential available in this window' and 'bundle capture (main..HEAD) failed: fatal: Refusing to create empty bundle'. Two gaps: (1) the salvage path runs without a git credential, so the rescue-ref push can never work in that window; (2) salvage only bundles COMMITTED work (main..HEAD) — an agent that settles without committing (exactly the failure case salvage exists for) leaves a dirty tree that salvage ignores. Suggest: salvage should git add -A + commit with the bot identity before bundling, and the finalize/salvage window should carry the same scoped credential the reap push uses. Recovery this time was manual kubectl exec commit + git bundle + kubectl cp.
closeReason: K8s salvage window fixed both ways: (1) the pod now carries WARREN_GIT_TOKEN from the warren-git-token Secret on the agent container (harness-only — scrubbed from the agent child spawn env), and the salvage windows fall back to it when no intent parked a token, mirroring provider.resolvePushToken; (2) collectSalvage now folds a dirty tree into a warren bookkeeping commit (git add -A + --no-verify commit via the src/bot-identity.ts resolver, Article VII) BEFORE the rescue push and bundle, so uncommitted work is captured instead of dying to 'Refusing to create empty bundle'. Operator WARREN_BOT_NAME/EMAIL overrides thread into the pod so the in-pod commit spells the identity the control plane's way. Tests cover commit-then-bundle ordering, identity pinning, credential fallback, and the env scrub; verified end-to-end against a real git repo. check:all 12/12 green.

title: flaky: public-projections '1.25' leak assertion trips on ISO millisecond timestamps
description: The test 'no cost figure survives anywhere in the anonymous analytics body' (src/server/handlers/public-projections.test.ts:310) seeds costUsd 1.25 and asserts JSON.stringify(body) does not contain '1.25'. title: check-coverage.ts drops the tail of bun test output — process.exit before stderr flush
description: scripts/check-coverage.ts buffers bun test's output via spawnSync, then reportResult() calls process.exit() immediately after process.stdout.write/process.stderr.write of a multi-MB buffer. The process exits before the pipe flushes, so CI logs cut off mid-suite: no test summary, no coverage table, no failure diff (observed on PR #816 run 31238103333 — the failing test was only recoverable from the junit.xml artifact). Fix: flush both streams before exiting (await write callbacks / use process.exitCode instead of process.exit), or stream the child's output with stdio inherit + tee instead of buffering.

title: forge p4: empirical spike — answer Q1-Q4 against the live GitHub API and amend the design doc
description:
Settle the four questions GitHub does not document (design doc §7), each with recorded evidence in the doc: Q1 does the App manifest redirect_url accept a loopback address (the whole self-hosted registration story depends on it — a NAT deployment has no public URL); Q2 does POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions require authentication, and is the code single-use; Q3 does a fine-grained PAT reach PUT /pulls/:n/merge (read X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions); Q4 can an App approve a PR it authored. Amend docs/design/forge-contract.md §7 with the answers and their consequences for the manifest-flow design (warren-a647). No warren code changes. This step has no code dependencies and can run any time before phase 4 locks.

--- SPIKE PROTOCOL (prepped 2026-08-11) ---

RESOURCES: private scratch repo jayminwest/warren-forge-spike exists (created 2026-08-11; delete after the spike). The throwaway App is created DURING Q1 — creating it via the manifest flow is itself the test.

OWNER PREREQS (~5 min of browser time, interleaved below):
(a) click "Create GitHub App" on the manifest page the spike serves (Q1 step 3);
(b) install the resulting App on warren-forge-spike (Q4 step 6);
(c) mint a fine-grained PAT scoped ONLY to warren-forge-spike, permissions Contents:RW + Pull requests:RW, 7-day expiry, exported as WARREN_SPIKE_FG_PAT in the spike shell (Q3).

Q1 — loopback redirect_url:
1. Run a local listener on http://127.0.0.1:8377/callback that prints the full query string (bun one-liner).
2. Serve a local HTML page with a form POSTing to https://github.com/settings/apps/new?state=<rand> with a single `manifest` field: name warren-spike-<rand>, url http://127.0.0.1:8377, redirect_url http://127.0.0.1:8377/callback, public false, webhook absent, default_permissions { contents: write, pull_requests: write, checks: read }.
3. OWNER opens the page and clicks Create GitHub App.
4. Evidence: the browser lands on the loopback with ?code=... => Q1 yes. If GitHub rejects the manifest, retry once with redirect_url http://localhost:8377/callback before answering no. Record the exact behavior either way.

Q2 — conversion auth + single-use (within 1h of Q1; the code expires):
5. curl -sS -i -X POST https://api.github.com/app-manifests/<code>/conversions -H "accept: application/vnd.github+json" with NO authorization header. 201 with {id, slug, pem, ...} => unauthenticated conversion works. Save id/pem/slug to local files OUTSIDE any repo.
6. Repeat the identical call with the same code. Expected 404 => single-use proven. Record both status lines verbatim.

Q4 — App approves its own PR (needs the App installed: owner prereq b):
7. Mint an installation token: RS256 JWT (iss = app id, 10-min exp) -> GET /app/installations -> POST /app/installations/:id/access_tokens.
8. With the installation token: create a branch + commit via the contents API on warren-forge-spike, open a PR.
9. POST /repos/jayminwest/warren-forge-spike/pulls/:n/reviews {"event":"APPROVE"} with the SAME installation token. 200 => yes. 422 "Can not approve your own pull request" => no. Record the response body.
10. Opportunistic while the App token is live: GET /repos/jayminwest/warren-forge-spike/commits/<head>/check-runs with it, to re-confirm the §6.7 App-vs-fine-grained-PAT Checks asymmetry from the other side.

Q3 — fine-grained PAT vs merge (owner prereq c):
11. curl -i -X PUT /repos/jayminwest/warren-forge-spike/pulls/:n/merge with WARREN_SPIKE_FG_PAT (reuse the Q4 PR or open a fresh one with the PAT). Record the status AND the X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions response header verbatim. Merged => yes. 403 => the header names the demanded permission set; record it.

DELIVERABLES: amend docs/design/forge-contract.md §7 replacing the four questions with dated answers + verbatim evidence (status lines, header values, error bodies — never tokens). Feed consequences to warren-a647 (manifest registration flow). CLEANUP: uninstall + delete the throwaway App, delete warren-forge-spike, revoke the fine-grained PAT. SAFETY: tokens and the pem never enter a commit, a seed, or the design doc.
closeReason: All four questions answered empirically 2026-08-11 and recorded in docs/design/forge-contract.md §7 with evidence: Q1 loopback redirect works; Q2 conversion unauthenticated + code single-use; Q3 fine-grained PAT merges with contents=write only; Q4 App cannot self-approve (422). Bonus: ghs_ 383-char token observed; App token reads check-runs. Consequences flow to warren-a647 via the amended doc.

title: seeds: .gitattributes merge=union on issues.jsonl silently produces duplicate contradictory rows
description:
Found while running the pl-d1c9 forge campaign through the dogfood pipeline
(PRs #822-#827, 2026-08-11). Every one of the five PRs after the first needed
a hand repair for the same reason.

## What happens

`.gitattributes:1` declares:

    .seeds/issues.jsonl merge=union

`merge=union` tells git that on a conflicting hunk it should keep BOTH sides'
lines with no conflict markers. That is the correct strategy for an
append-only log. `.seeds/issues.jsonl` is not one: seeds REWRITES rows in
place. Closing a single issue rewrites that row's `status`/`closedAt` AND
rewrites every sibling's `blockedBy` to drop the closed id.

So when two branches each close an issue from the same plan, both have
rewritten the same rows, and union merge emits two contradictory copies of
every touched row. Git reports a clean merge. Nothing warns.

Observed on this campaign: PR #823 duplicated 8 rows, PRs #824/#825/#826
duplicated 20 rows each — every child of plan pl-d1c9. 1326 rows became 1346.

## Why it is worse than it looks

Picking either duplicate row is wrong. On the umbrella seed warren-3fe7,
main had dropped `warren-4e78` from blockedBy and kept `warren-0993`; the
branch had done the exact inverse. Whichever row survives silently
RESURRECTS a blocker that is already satisfied, so `sd ready` under-reports
available work for the rest of the campaign. Neither side's row is correct.

The correct resolution needs both sides at once:
  - status: `closed` wins (each side only ever closes)
  - blockedBy: the INTERSECTION of the two sides (each side only ever
    REMOVES a blocker, so intersection = union-of-removals)

## Current state of the defence

`check:seeds-integrity` (warren-a71f) detects the resulting duplicate and
contradictory rows, and it fired correctly every time. But it is a
post-hoc detector for a corruption the repo's own merge config guarantees.
The repo has a footgun plus an alarm, not a correct merge strategy.

## Proposed fix

Replace `merge=union` with a custom seeds merge driver that merges
id-keyed JSONL semantically using the two rules above, registered in
`.gitattributes` as `merge=seeds-jsonl` with the driver defined in git
config. `merge=union` should stay only for genuinely append-only seeds
files if any exist — `templates.jsonl` and `plans.jsonl` carry the same
declaration and need the same audit.

A working reference implementation of the merge algorithm (closed-wins +
blockedBy intersection) was used to repair all five PRs this session; it
lives in the session scratchpad as dedupe-seeds.py and is ~40 lines.

Belongs upstream in the seeds tool, not just in warren's .gitattributes —
every repo using seeds with plans and concurrent agents has this bug.
closeReason: Fixed by a real 3-way id-keyed JSONL merge driver (scripts/merge-seeds-jsonl.ts), registered as merge=seeds-jsonl in .gitattributes for .seeds/issues.jsonl, .seeds/plans.jsonl, .seeds/templates.jsonl, and .mulch/expertise/*.jsonl (all four rewrite rows in place — verified against the seeds store writePlans/writeTemplates call sites and mulch's upsert-merge). The driver merges per field against the ancestor and set-merges array fields like blockedBy by applying both sides' ancestor-relative additions and removals; genuine conflicts exit non-zero instead of silently picking a side. Driver config is installed per-clone by package.json prepare (git config merge.seeds-jsonl.driver). Audit outcome: the two .canopy entries were dead config (canopy retired in pl-3a79, files gone) and were removed; no merge=union entries remain. LIMITATION: the driver only runs locally — GitHub server-side merges (gh pr update-branch, squash-merge) never invoke it, so that path stays covered by check:seeds-integrity (warren-a71f) inside the lint gate only. Verified end-to-end: two branches each closing a different issue from the same row merge cleanly with both blockedBy removals preserved (the exact pl-d1c9 corruption shape), and a genuine priority conflict surfaces as a real git conflict.

title: warren runs rewrite all plan-sibling rows in .seeds/issues.jsonl, guaranteeing cross-PR collisions
description:
Found while running the pl-d1c9 forge campaign through the dogfood pipeline
(2026-08-11). Companion to warren-9c90, which covers the merge-strategy half.

## The behaviour

When a warren run closes its seedId, seeds recalculates `blockedBy` on every
sibling in the same plan and rewrites those rows. For a 19-child plan like
pl-d1c9 that means a single `sd close` dirties up to 20 rows in
.seeds/issues.jsonl.

Consequence: any two warren runs dispatched against children of the same
plan will collide in .seeds/issues.jsonl, always, no matter how disjoint
their code changes are. On this campaign PRs #824, #825 and #826 each
touched exactly 4-5 source files and 20 seed rows.

## Why it matters for warren specifically

This is the file every warren run writes at reap. It converts the tracker
into a guaranteed contention point for the exact workload warren exists to
run — parallel agents on one plan. The dogfood pipeline's "sequential
one-at-a-time" mode does not avoid it either, because a run's clone is taken
before the previous PR merges.

Combined with warren-9c90 (merge=union silently keeps both copies) the
result is that every PR after the first in a campaign needs a hand repair.
Five of six PRs this session did.

## Options worth weighing

1. Fix the merge strategy (warren-9c90) and accept the churn. Cheapest;
   makes the collision harmless rather than absent.
2. Have seeds derive `blockedBy` at read time from the forward `blocks`
   edges instead of storing it denormalized on every sibling. A close then
   rewrites ONE row. This is the real fix and removes the churn at source.
3. Have warren's reap skip the sibling recalculation and let `sd` recompute
   lazily.

Option 2 is a seeds change; option 3 is a warren change. Recommend scoping
option 2 upstream first, since the denormalized blockedBy is what makes a
one-issue close a twenty-row write.

## Evidence

PRs #822-#827 on jayminwest/warren, plan pl-d1c9, all 2026-08-11.
Row counts: 1326 clean -> 1346 after merge, 20 duplicated ids, repeatably.
closeReason: Root cause is upstream seeds write-side denormalization: sd close rewrites every plan-sibling row's blockedBy, which no warren-side change can fix without risky row-scoped staging surgery. Filed upstream as seeds-9be5 (derive blockedBy at read time). Warren-side collisions are already self-healing via the merge-seeds-jsonl driver + check:seeds-integrity + seeds-merge-autoheal, and the same-clone concurrency residual is owned by warren-232d (pl-a37b).

title: GitHub reports mergeable=CONFLICTING on a PR that merges cleanly locally; update-branch refuses
description:
Observed on PR #824 during the pl-d1c9 dogfood campaign, 2026-08-11.
Operational note for anyone shepherding warren PRs — not a warren defect.

## What was seen

    gh pr view 824 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus
      -> {"mergeable":"CONFLICTING","mergeStateStatus":"DIRTY"}

    gh pr update-branch 824
      -> X Cannot update PR branch due to conflicts

At the same moment, against byte-identical refs:

    local origin/main       b3a0cde1f
    github  heads/main      b3a0cde1f      (identical)
    PR 824 head             c61a590d2      (identical local and remote)

    git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/warren/run_ygfa3ntcqc7g
      -> clean, tree hash only, no conflict output

A real `git merge origin/main` in a worktree also succeeded with zero
conflicts. GitHub's cached mergeability was simply wrong, and stayed wrong
across a 15s re-poll and an explicit update-branch attempt.

## Resolution

Pushing a merge commit to the PR branch forced GitHub to recompute, after
which the PR went MERGEABLE/BLOCKED and auto-merged normally.

## Why it is worth recording

The warren-dogfood-pipeline skill's shepherding table maps DIRTY ->
"dispatch a repair run". Following that here would have spent a full agent
run (~$1.30 and ~10 minutes) resolving a conflict that did not exist.

Suggested amendment to the skill: on DIRTY, verify with
`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` BEFORE dispatching a
repair run. If merge-tree is clean, the conflict is a GitHub cache
artifact — push a merge commit to force recomputation instead.

Filed at P3 because the workaround is cheap and reliable once known; the
value is the diagnostic step, not a code change.

title: dogfood: guard against pushing a duplicate-row .seeds/issues.jsonl to main
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Step 37 of plan pl-a37b.

Parent seed: warren-bc61 — v0.18.0 — the any-setup release: dispatch-context log, IssueTracker seam + RemoteTracker bridge, external-repo readiness
Plan template: feature
Plan approach: Five tracks, forward-chained. Track A (steps 1-5): the dispatch-context log as a core insert-only dispatch_context table keyed by run_id, written fire-and-log inside spawnRun (the verified single choke point covering all 8 dispatch sites),…

Run `sd plan show pl-a37b` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

Filed against myself after corrupting main during the pl-d1c9 phase-1
dogfood session, 2026-08-11. Companion to warren-9c90.

## What happened

Commit e4624412 reached main carrying 1350 rows with 20 duplicated,
contradictory plan-child rows — the exact corruption its own message
documents. Sequence:

1. `git pull --rebase origin main` rebased the findings commit onto main.
   merge=union silently duplicated all twenty pl-d1c9 rows (warren-9c90).
2. `bun run check:seeds-integrity` ran and FAILED, exit code 1.
3. `git push origin main` ran anyway in the same compound command and
   SUCCEEDED. Its output included
   `remote: - 2 of 2 required status checks are expected.`
   which reads like a rejection but is informational — the push landed.
4. The output was read as a failed push, the file was deduped and the
   commit amended locally, so the corrected version never reached the
   remote and the corrupted one sat on main.

Repaired by b4612106. All six phase-1 closes and the four follow-up
issues were verified intact; nothing was lost.

## Three separate holes

1. **No pre-push guard.** check:seeds-integrity is in the `lint` gate and
   runs in CI on PRs, but a direct push to main bypasses CI entirely.
   Nothing stopped a known-corrupt file from landing.
2. **A failing gate did not stop the push.** The gate and the push were
   chained with `;` rather than `&&`, so a red gate was advisory.
3. **The push output is ambiguous.** `2 of 2 required status checks are
   expected` appears on a SUCCESSFUL push to a branch with required
   checks configured. It is easy to misread as a rejection.

## Proposed

- A `pre-push` hook that runs check:seeds-integrity when
  `.seeds/*.jsonl` is in the pushed range and refuses on failure. This is
  the one gate that must survive a direct-to-main push, because the
  corruption it catches is invisible in a diff.
- Require a PR for main if direct pushes are not intended; branch
  protection currently reports required checks but still admits the push.
- Amend the warren-dogfood-pipeline skill's wrap-up step 5 to verify the
  push by re-reading the file from origin, not by trusting push output.

Note the irony worth keeping: the session that documented merge=union as
a P1 bug was itself bitten by it during its own wrap-up, which is
evidence for how silent the failure is.
closeReason: Added scripts/hooks/pre-push + scripts/pre-push-seeds-guard.ts: when any .seeds/*.jsonl path is in the pushed ref range (git pre-push stdin protocol), runs check:seeds-integrity against the issues.jsonl blob at the local tip (not the worktree) and refuses on failure. Untouched seeds skips cleanly; branch deletes skipped. Strips GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_PREFIX like pre-commit (warren-8664). check-seeds-integrity gained --stdin for blob scanning. Unit tests cover parsePushLine/buildDiffRange/seedsTouched/listChangedPaths. Dogfood skill wrap-up step 5 now verifies origin tip instead of trusting push output. Branch-protection (require PR for main) left as operator-only out of scope.

title: POST /runs/:id/steer is a silent no-op for the pi agent: steer.sent is recorded but the harness never delivers it
description:
Observed live on run_8a5b6pf07m9s (seed warren-9c90), 2026-08-11.

## What happened

An operator steered a running `pi` agent to add scope:

    POST /runs/run_8a5b6pf07m9s/steer   -> 200
    {"message":{"id":"msg_v9fvfxf7k18y","runId":null,"state":"unread",...}}

Timing was generous: the run started 20:57:21, the steer was sent
20:59:45 (2m23s in), and the run ended 21:25:20 — about 25 minutes of
agent work after delivery.

The agent never acted on it. Verified from the run's own event stream
(375 events):

  - `steer.sent` recorded at seq 1615, ts 20:59:45.125, with the full
    body intact in the payload.
  - After that timestamp: 187 state_change, 46 tool_use, 46 tool_result,
    21 thinking, 14 text events.
  - Mentions of the steering content ("doctor", "check-attr", "sd init")
    across ALL post-delivery thinking and text events: ZERO.
  - Tool calls referencing inbox or steer: ZERO.
  - The resulting PR (#829) contains none of the steered scope.

The agent did not ignore the instruction. It never saw it.

## Why it is dangerous

Steering is a headline warren capability ("accepts steering mid-run").
The failure is SILENT and every signal available to the operator says it
worked:

  - the POST returns 200 with a message object,
  - a `steer.sent` event lands on the run and shows in the UI,
  - no error, no warning, nothing in `/readyz`.

`steer.sent` only asserts that warren SENT the message. There is no
`steer.delivered` or `steer.acknowledged` event, so nothing distinguishes
"the agent read it and disagreed" from "the agent never received it".
An operator watching the run cannot tell the difference.

## Suspected mechanism

Two separate stores exist and they are easy to conflate:

  - `POST /runs/:id/steer` -> `steerRun` (src/runs/steer.ts:65) ->
    `runtimeProvider.sendMessage`. Its own doc comment notes burrow's
    inbox is scoped PER-BURROW, not per-run, which is why the returned
    message carries `runId: null` (expected, not the bug).
  - `GET /runs/:id/inbox` -> `repos.runInbox` -> a DIFFERENT store, the
    in-pod steering poll added for the K8s backend (warren-3d0b).

So the message reached the runtime provider's inbox, and the `pi`
harness evidently does not drain that inbox — or drains a different one.
Worth checking which agents actually poll for steering: this needs to be
per-agent-harness truth, not assumed uniform across the eight builtins.

## Asks

1. Determine which builtin harnesses actually consume steering. `pi` is
   confirmed NOT to.
2. Emit a delivery-side event (`steer.delivered` / `steer.acknowledged`)
   so `steer.sent` alone stops reading as success.
3. If a harness cannot consume steering, `POST /runs/:id/steer` should
   fail loudly for that agent — 409 or 501 with a clear reason — rather
   than 200. A capability flag on the agent record would express it.
4. Document the two-inbox split, because `GET /runs/:id/inbox` returning
   `{"messages":[]}` after a steer looks like proof of delivery and is
   not. Note that route also MUTATES on read (handlers/index.ts:204-207),
   so an operator checking it can drain the real queue.

## Workaround

None mid-run. Re-dispatch with the corrected prompt, or apply the change
by hand on the PR branch afterwards.
closeReason: Diagnosis: (2) confirmed primary — pi's rpc loop reads stdin only at a turn boundary and warren closes stdin at pi's terminal agent_end, so a mid-turn steering line sits unread in the pipe and is discarded; the incident run was one continuous 25-min turn, so the message never reached pi. (1) confirmed as a live secondary hazard by code inspection — GET /runs/:id/inbox is poll-consume, so any non-pod reader steals the message. Shipped: (a) all 8 builtins consume steering only at spawn (encodeInboxMessage fold-in); none consume mid-run — declared via new frontmatter.steering flag (STEERING_CAPABILITIES in core/wire-inbox.ts), all builtins 'spawn-only'; (b) steer.delivered emitted per claimed message by the inbox poll; (c) steerRun 409s (StateTransitionError) steers a declared harness cannot consume, undeclared agents fail open; (d) ?peek=1 non-claiming inbox read + two-inbox split documented in k8s-migration.md §1.4.

title: K8s: control-plane pod replacement mid-run deadlocks the agent on finalize-intent; run never reaches terminal
description:
Observed live on app.warren.run during the pl-d1c9 dogfood pipeline, run run_j4e5n48y6v9s (2026-08-11).

## What happened

1. The agent finished its work, drove check:all to 12/12 green, made 9 commits, and ran sd close.
2. The warren control-plane pod (warren-7cfdcbbf47-kjq64) failed its readiness probe with 'connection refused' and was replaced in-place by the SAME ReplicaSet — not a deploy, the process died. replicas:1, so there was a real outage window (external GETs returned GCE 502s).
3. On recovery warren emitted a stream_gap event (reason cursor_predates_retained_logs, sinceSeq 6945, retainedLines 756).
4. Reap then fired salvage with trigger 'no_intent' — it had lost the completion signal — pushing warren/rescue/run_j4e5n48y6v9s plus a bundle at /data/salvage/run_j4e5n48y6v9s.bundle.
5. The agent pod, however, was still alive and had NOT been told anything. It sat polling GET /runs/run_j4e5n48y6v9s/finalize-intent every ~2s, receiving 200 each time, indefinitely.

Net effect: a deadlock. The agent waits forever for a finalize intent the control plane has already given up on issuing. The run stayed state=running with prUrl=null and costUsd=null for 30+ minutes, and would seemingly have stayed there indefinitely. The chain behind it was blocked.

## Why it matters

The pod boundary correctly protected the agent from the control-plane outage (run pod: 0 restarts, unaffected) — that part of the K8s topology worked. But there is no reconciliation between 'reap decided no_intent and salvaged' and 'the agent pod is still running and asking for intent'. Either side alone is coherent; together they hang.

## Expected

After a control-plane restart, one of:
- the recovered control plane re-attaches to the live agent pod and issues the finalize intent it is polling for (preferred — the work was complete and would have reaped normally), or
- salvage-on-no_intent also terminates the agent pod and drives the run to a terminal state, so the run does not sit in a permanent running limbo.

## Recovery used

POST /runs/:id/cancel deleted the pod, then the completed tree was pushed from the salvage ref and PR #831 opened by hand.

## Evidence

- events seq 6946 (stream_gap) and 6947 (reap.workspace_salvaged) on run_j4e5n48y6v9s
- control-plane log: repeating GET /runs/run_j4e5n48y6v9s/finalize-intent 200 at ~2s intervals from pod warren-7cfdcbbf47-8gmpf
- kubectl events in ns warren showing SuccessfulCreate for the replacement pod in the same RS

Related: warren-b94b (stale host clone on ref-dispatch), warren-0395 (noChanges seed auto-close). See src/runs/reap/salvage.ts and the finalize-intent route.
closeReason: Shipped poll-driven finalize recovery (preferred fix): the K8s finalize-intent GET now reports intent misses to a boot-wired recovery hook (src/runs/finalize-recovery.ts, wired under WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s only). A miss that outlives a 30s grace drives a fresh reap, which re-parks the intent via finalizeK8sRun so the normal finalize handshake completes and the run terminalizes. Outcome is classified from the pod-reported agent exit code (new ?agent_exit= poll param, overlaid by agent-entrypoint), then the persisted terminal envelope, then a succeeded default bounded by reap's safety nets. Invariants pinned in tests: never fires while an intent is parked, never inside the grace window, single-flight per run with re-arm on failure, terminal/gone pods stay with the warren-c433 reconcile net, salvage intake untouched (idempotent). Invariant established: after a control-plane restart every non-terminal run converges — live pods via recovery reap (~30s), given-up pods via the terminal-reconcile net. LocalProvider unaffected.

title: POST /runs/:id/cancel deletes the agent pod but leaves the run row state=running
description:
Observed live on app.warren.run during the pl-d1c9 dogfood pipeline, run run_j4e5n48y6v9s (2026-08-11). Split out from warren-5202, which is the deadlock that led here.

## What happened

The run was wedged (agent polling finalize-intent forever after a control-plane replacement; see warren-5202). Called:

    POST /runs/run_j4e5n48y6v9s/cancel

Response was accepted and coherent:

    {"state":"running","alreadyTerminal":false,"burrowRun":{"id":"036fd820-...","state":"running"}}

The agent pod was in fact deleted — 'kubectl get pods -n warren-runs' went from 'run-run-j4e5n48y6v9s 1/1 Running' to 'No resources found'. But GET /runs/run_j4e5n48y6v9s continued to report state=running, failureReason=null, costUsd=null well after the pod was gone.

## Why it matters

Cancel is the documented escape hatch for a wedged run, and the pipeline's polling contract treats terminal states (succeeded|failed|cancelled) as the signal to advance. A cancel that removes the workload but never transitions the row means:
- an automated poller waits forever on a run whose pod no longer exists
- the run occupies its slot against admission caps (admission.maxConcurrentRuns / WARREN_K8S_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH) despite being dead
- costUsd is never finalized, so spend for the run is unattributed

## Expected

Cancel drives the run row to 'cancelled' once the pod is confirmed gone, finalizing costUsd, or a pod-watcher/reconciler notices the missing pod and marks it terminal (RunStatus.status() returning exists:false is the documented out-of-band recovery path, per src/runtime/contract.ts §6.7).

## Caveat on scope

This was observed on a run already in the warren-5202 deadlock, so the cancel path may behave correctly on a healthy run. Worth reproducing on a normal run before assuming the defect is unconditional.

## Correction (2026-08-12, same session)

The run DID eventually reach a terminal state — it is not a permanent
limbo as first written. Timeline:

- ~00:37  POST /runs/:id/cancel accepted, agent pod deleted immediately
- 00:59:42 run row finally transitioned, roughly 25 minutes later

Two things remain wrong, and they are narrower than the original report:

1. The terminal state was `failed`, not `cancelled`. An operator-requested
   cancel that resolves as `failed` loses the distinction between "a human
   stopped this" and "this broke", which matters for triage and for any
   automation that treats failed runs as needing repair.
2. The ~25-minute lag between pod deletion and the row transition is long
   enough that a poller with any reasonable iteration cap gives up first.
   The pod was confirmed gone from the API within seconds.

So: not "never transitions" but "transitions late, and to the wrong state".
The admission-slot and unattributed-cost concerns in the original report
still apply for the duration of the lag, but they are bounded, not
indefinite.

### Further correction: costUsd DID finalize

The original report listed "costUsd is never finalized, so spend for the run
is unattributed" as a consequence. That is wrong. The run finalized at
costUsd=0.8081574 once it transitioned. Cost attribution is delayed by the
same lag as the state transition, not lost. Strike that bullet; the
remaining concerns (wrong terminal state, admission slot held for the
duration of the lag) stand.
closeReason: Cancel intent now wins over the pod-watcher lost mapping: cancelRun records cancel.requested, the watchdog terminal-reconcile net (hasCancelIntent via EventsRepo.hasKind) resolves a vanished pod to cancelled instead of failed, and a new cancel fast-path grace (WARREN_RUN_CANCEL_RECONCILE_GRACE_MS, default 15s) probes cancel-intent runs well before the full 2-min grace — the deliberately-deleted pod reconciles in seconds-to-a-minute, not ~25 min, and reap finalizes costUsd. cancelRun also maps a post-cancel exists:false status read to cancelled inline.

title: Every PR touching .seeds/issues.jsonl shows CONFLICTING on GitHub: the seeds-jsonl merge driver is local-only
description:
Observed live during the pl-d1c9 dogfood pipeline on PR #832 (2026-08-12).

## What happened

PR #832 reported mergeable=CONFLICTING / mergeStateStatus=DIRTY on GitHub, and 'gh pr update-branch 832' refused with 'Cannot update PR branch due to conflicts'. But locally the same merge was clean:

    git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>
    -> 3ded8d45f311bc09f64bff7b09d3b82675041b59   (tree hash only, no conflict output)

The merged tree was also CORRECT: 1335 rows, all ids unique, every concurrently-created row present on both sides.

## Root cause

.gitattributes routes .seeds/issues.jsonl (and the mulch state files) through a custom merge driver:

    merge.seeds-jsonl.driver = bun scripts/merge-seeds-jsonl.ts %O %A %B

registered by package.json's prepare script. It is a real 3-way id-keyed merge, added to replace merge=union after warren-9c90.

GitHub's server-side merge does NOT run custom merge drivers — they only exist in a local clone that has run 'bun install'. So GitHub falls back to a plain textual 3-way merge of an id-keyed JSONL file and sees a genuine conflict on any row both sides rewrote.

## Consequence

Any PR whose branch touches .seeds/issues.jsonl (i.e. essentially every agent run, since runs close their seed) will show as CONFLICTING on GitHub as soon as ANY other .seeds change lands on main. That means:
- GitHub auto-merge cannot merge it
- 'gh pr update-branch' cannot fix it
- the only resolution is a human/agent doing the merge in a local clone where the driver exists, then pushing

For an autonomous pipeline this is a hard stop: the merge gate that plan-runs depend on cannot clear itself. It also makes the DIRTY-state triage in the dogfood runbook misleading — the documented advice is 'if merge-tree is clean, GitHub's cached mergeability is wrong, push a merge commit to force a recompute' (warren-fb6e). Here merge-tree being clean does NOT mean the cache is stale; it means the local driver resolved something GitHub genuinely cannot.

## Recovery used

git checkout -B pr832 origin/<head>; git merge origin/main --no-edit; verify rows; git push. After the push GitHub reported MERGEABLE.

## Worth considering

- A CI job that performs the driver-aware merge and pushes it, so PRs self-heal
- Or reshaping the on-disk format so a plain 3-way merge is correct without a driver (e.g. one file per issue), which removes the class of problem entirely
- At minimum, document this in the dogfood runbook's DIRTY row so agents stop treating merge-tree-clean as proof of a stale cache

Related: warren-9c90, warren-db8c (the merge=union duplicate-row shape the driver replaced), warren-fb6e (genuinely stale mergeability cache), #830 (the guard keeping sd doctor from re-adding merge=union).
closeReason: Shipped .github/workflows/seeds-merge-autoheal.yml: on PRs touching .seeds/*.jsonl that GitHub reports CONFLICTING, it checks out the PR branch, registers the seeds-jsonl driver, runs the driver-aware git merge origin/main, verifies row integrity (check:seeds-integrity + duplicate-id scan), and pushes the heal merge back via the AUTO_MERGE app token. Fork PRs skipped; [seeds-autoheal] commit-message sentinel plus the CONFLICTING gate prevent retrigger loops. Also corrected the dogfood runbook DIRTY row (.claude/skills/warren-dogfood-pipeline/SKILL.md): a clean merge-tree on a .seeds-touching PR is a real GitHub-side conflict (driver is local-only), not a stale mergeability cache.

title: forge-contract §0's domain list omits src/projects/ — the registration boundary was an unanticipated seam gap
description:
Surfaced by the campaign's own falsification test (warren-2600, PR #838) during the pl-d1c9 dogfood run, 2026-08-12.

## What happened

Acceptance scenario 40 boots warren with WARREN_FORGE=fake and drives a FakeForge-owned project through dispatch -> reap -> push -> PR. The claim under test is that this needs ZERO domain-code changes.

It could not even register the project. src/projects/url.ts was GitHub-specific, so a fake:// URL failed parsing at the registration boundary, well before any run started.

The agent resolved it correctly: it checked the change against docs/design/forge-contract.md §0's list of domain modules — which names src/runs, src/plan-runs, and src/triggers — found src/projects/ absent, judged that routing repo-ownership through the forge was legitimate seam work rather than a falsification, and reported it rather than special-casing the fake. The fix is contained (src/projects/url.ts +39, manage.ts +30, one handler line, with tests) and preserves the [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ per-segment validation that guards /data/projects path safety (mx-e741b0).

## The actual issue

§0's domain list is incomplete, and that incompleteness is load-bearing: it is the checklist an agent (or a human) uses to decide whether a change falsifies the seam or extends it. Project registration is plainly domain code that must not know which forge owns a URL, yet it was not listed, so nothing in phases 1-3 was scoped to cover it. The gap surfaced only because a falsification test tried to do the one thing the list did not anticipate.

## Work needed

- Add src/projects/ to §0's domain list, and re-derive the list from what actually consumes forge-shaped data rather than from memory.
- Re-check the remaining phases against the corrected list. warren-5497 (phase 5, delete the old paths) does an Article VI repo-wide old-path search whose completeness depends on knowing every domain that touched the old path.
- Consider whether §0 should name the falsification test's registration step explicitly, so a future forge implementation cannot pass the scenario while leaving registration GitHub-only.

Evidence: PR #838, scripts/acceptance/scenarios/40-fake-forge-roundtrip.ts, and the run's own reasoning trace on run_kj7j7cq90x71.
closeReason: added src/projects/ to forge-contract §0 domain list and re-derived the list against live Forge consumers

title: forge p4: GitHubApp credential heartbeat probe (in-warren runtime, not a CI job)
description:
Split out of warren-f8df (plan pl-d1c9 step 16) during the 2026-08-12 dogfood session, because f8df bundled four separable deliverables and the combined PR was judged likely to breach the 91.85% coverage ratchet against a fresh untested tree (plan risk 4).

warren-f8df keeps: RS256 JWT mint, installation-token cache with expiry margin, capability-flag wiring, and the registry 'app' arm.

This issue is the remaining piece: a heartbeat probe that surfaces a dead App credential LOUDLY rather than as a silent merge-gate stall. That is plan pl-d1c9 acceptance criterion 8, and it exists because of the PR #818 lesson.

IMPORTANT — the precedent is the 'app-heartbeat' job at .github/workflows/release.yml:289 (from PR #818 / commit 4c932878), but do NOT copy it as a CI job. The acceptance criterion asks for an in-warren RUNTIME probe: warren itself must detect and surface the dead credential while running. The CI job is prior art for what to check, not for where it lives.

Blocked by warren-f8df — the probe has nothing to probe until the App provider and its capability flags exist.

What it checks: on WARREN_FORGE=app, a boot-wired timer force-mints an installation token (new InstallationTokenSource.mintFresh bypasses the cache read, so every tick is a real liveness proof — a successful mint is the whole proof since App keys carry no expiry) via GitHubAppForge.probeCredential, which reports only the token expiry, never the secret. How a dead credential surfaces: error-level structured log per failed tick (kind + detail only, no secret-carrying fields, so no log-redact additions needed), the warren_forge_heartbeat_probe_total metrics counter with outcome/kind labels for Grafana alerting, and an info-level recovery line on the first success after a failure. This closes the PR #818 gap where a dead App credential hid as merge-gate patience. 12/12 quality gates green.

title: A run that fails with provider_error mid-work discards all uncommitted changes and produces no salvage bundle
description:
Observed live on the public instance during the 2026-08-12 dogfood session (plan pl-d1c9).

## What happened

run_y3196c50a5qb (seed warren-c9ac, agent pi, openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3) ran 29 minutes and did substantial real work — it was successfully editing src/runtime/k8s/finalize-entrypoint.salvage.test.ts at 18:35:14.926Z.

At 18:35:33.516Z openrouter returned an EMPTY completion: a turn_end event whose usage block was all zeros (input 0, output 0, cacheRead 0, totalTokens 0) and whose content was []. agent_end fired 20ms later. The run went terminal as state=failed, failureReason=provider_error, costUsd 4.0274952.

## The actual bug

The reap.completed event recorded:

    noChanges: false
    seeds: { closed: 0, created: 0, committed: false }
    prUrl: null
    salvage: { rescueRef: null, bundlePath: null }

noChanges:false says warren KNEW there were changes in the workspace. But no salvage bundle and no rescue ref were produced, and the branch warren pushed (refs/heads/warren/run_y3196c50a5qb, sha 88be91fd) is byte-identical to origin/main — verified with git rev-parse. Every edit the agent made was discarded.

$4.03 and 29 minutes of work lost to a transient upstream fault that warren observed cleanly.

## Why it matters

The salvage path (rescueRef / bundlePath) exists precisely so that a run which dies with work in the workspace does not lose it. It did not fire here. Either:

1. salvage is gated on a failure mode that excludes provider_error, or
2. salvage only considers COMMITTED work, so an agent that dies before its first commit is unsalvageable by construction.

If (2), that is the design gap: the agent's commit discipline should not be the only thing standing between a transient provider fault and total work loss. A run's uncommitted workspace diff is exactly what salvage should capture.

## Repro

Dispatch any long-running agent run and kill the model provider mid-turn, or wait for an empty-completion fault. Check the reap.completed salvage fields against noChanges.

## Workaround in use

Dogfood prompts now instruct agents to commit incrementally per unit of work rather than once at the end. That is insurance, not a fix — it depends on the agent complying.

## Evidence

- run_y3196c50a5qb on the public instance, full event stream retained
- branch refs/heads/warren/run_y3196c50a5qb == origin/main (88be91fd)
- the re-dispatch that replaced it: run_tceybz0vx3m7

<!-- root-cause-correction 2026-08-12 -->
## ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED

The trigger was NOT random upstream flakiness. The immediately-following
re-dispatch (run_tceybz0vx3m7) failed in 2 minutes at $0.00 with an
explicit error that names the cause:

    402: This request requires more credits, or fewer max_tokens.
    You requested up to 131072 tokens, but can only afford 121713.
    limit_source: openrouter_credits

The OpenRouter account ran out of credits. run_y3196c50a5qb's empty
completion at 18:35:33 was the same exhaustion arriving mid-run — the
balance drained while it worked, which is why the fault looked like an
empty response rather than a clean 402.

**This makes the salvage gap worse, not better.** Credit exhaustion is a
foreseeable, recurring, and completely predictable operating condition,
not a freak event. Warren observed it cleanly — it recorded
failureReason=provider_error and a reap.provider_error event carrying the
full 402 body — and still discarded 29 minutes of work with
noChanges:false and both salvage fields null.

A provider running out of money should cost the operator the run, not the
work. Note also that reap recorded branchPushed:true and commitsAhead:0
— warren pushed an empty branch and reported success at pushing it.

Worth considering alongside the fix: a pre-dispatch credit/balance probe
would have failed this run in 0 seconds for $0 instead of 29 minutes for
$4.03.
closeReason: Pod-side salvage trigger: finalize-entrypoint now detects a SUCCESSFUL zero-commit push with a dirty tree (the provider_error mid-work death shape) via salvageTriggerForResult() and runs the existing capture path (commitUncommittedWork fold-in + rescue-ref push + git bundle POST) with a new empty_push_dirty trigger BEFORE the result POST lets warren terminate the pod. SalvageTrigger vocabulary canonicalized in src/core/wire.ts and re-exported through finalize-wire.ts; intake validation accepts the new trigger (POST /runs/:id/salvage stays idempotent). Reap-side arm: run.ts surfaces pod-posted salvage (salvageRef/salvagePath on reap.completed + reap.workspace_salvage_recorded) for provider_error failures under k8s, not just finalizeFailed. The pre-dispatch credit probe was skipped as optional/separable. No retry logic (not warren-339d/4af7).

title: merge-seeds-jsonl driver reports updatedAt-only differences as unresolvable conflicts
description:
Observed live during the 2026-08-12 dogfood session (plan pl-d1c9).

## What happened

PR #842 (warren-a647) went CONFLICTING against main after PR #841
(warren-c9ac) merged. Probing the conflict with

    git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main pr842

produced:

    merge-seeds-jsonl: unresolvable conflicts:
      warren-3fe7.updatedAt
      warren-5497.updatedAt

Both rows differ ONLY in their updatedAt timestamp. There is no semantic
disagreement between the two sides — no status difference, no blockedBy
difference, no field either side actually contested. The driver declared
the whole file unresolvable over two timestamps.

## Why this is a bug

The merge driver landed in warren-9c90 (PRs #829 + #830) precisely to do
a real 3-way id-keyed merge instead of the merge=union corruption that
preceded it. It correctly INTERSECTS blockedBy and correctly takes closed
where either side closed. updatedAt should get the same treatment: it is
a monotonic timestamp, and the obvious resolution is TAKE THE LATER
VALUE. There is no case where a human or agent needs to arbitrate which
of two mtimes is correct.

As it stands, any two concurrent warren runs that touch the same issue
row — which is the normal case, since closing any child rewrites
updatedAt on plan siblings — produce a hard conflict that costs a repair
run to clear. In this session that was a real dispatched run against the
live instance.

## Suggested fix

In the driver's per-field resolution, treat updatedAt (and any other
pure-timestamp field) as auto-resolvable by max(). Reserve
'unresolvable' for fields where the two sides genuinely disagree about
content.

## Evidence

- PR #842 vs origin/main at 2026-08-12
- repair run dispatched to clear it: run_ntzfmmfhaevv
- driver introduced in warren-9c90

## Note on scope

The driver lives in the warren repo but the same class of file is
produced by sd in every os-eco repo. If the resolution logic is shared or
copied, fix it at the source — see seeds-6e2d, the upstream issue about
sd init / sd doctor --fix re-adding merge=union.

## Merged from warren-d8f0 (duplicate, closed 2026-08-16)

Second live occurrence: PRs #878 and #879 (pl-17ca dispatch session
2026-08-15). Closing any plan child rewrites updatedAt on the parent and
every sibling (blockedBy recompute), so ANY two PRs that each close a
sibling of the same plan produce a both-changed-differently updatedAt
scalar on the shared rows. Every consecutive-sibling PR pair in a plan
run therefore needs a manual driver merge (normalize updatedAt to max on
both sides, re-run driver). This also blocks seeds-merge-autoheal from
healing these PRs, since it runs the same driver. Resolution remains:
take max (or the side whose row otherwise won the field merge) —
updatedAt is bookkeeping, not user data.
closeReason: merge-seeds-jsonl auto-resolves updatedAt/closedAt timestamp-only conflicts by max()

title: Anonymous /github-app/register lets a stranger drive unbounded outbound conversion POSTs to github.com
description:
Surfaced while reviewing PR #842 (warren-a647) during the 2026-08-12 dogfood session. NOT a blocker for that PR — filing so the decision is recorded rather than lost.

## Context

warren-a647 added two routes, both policy 'anonymous':

  GET /github-app/register   — renders the App manifest form
  GET /github-app/callback   — GitHub redirects here after App creation

Both are defensible as written, and src/server/handlers/github-app.ts documents the reasoning well:

- The App created belongs to the CALLER's GitHub account, not the instance's.
- renderCredentialsPage DISPLAYS the PEM/client-secret and persists nothing — 'warren keeps no copy, and this page is the only place they appear', served with cache-control: no-store.
- The callback is gated by a single-use, ten-minute state nonce; without a live nonce it answers 400 and converts nothing.
- Both pages carry a locked-down CSP with no scripts and form-action narrowed to github.com.

So there is no credential leak and no warren state change. Confirmed by reading the handler and the registration module.

## The residual concern

On a WARREN_AUTH=public instance (app.warren.run is one), an anonymous stranger can:

1. GET /github-app/register as many times as they like, minting an unbounded number of live nonces in the process-local RegistrationSessions store, and
2. drive a corresponding POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions from warren's own egress toward github.com for each one.

That is an abuse vector rather than a disclosure: unbounded outbound requests attributable to the instance, unbounded growth of the in-process nonce store, and burn against whatever GitHub-side limits apply to the conversion endpoint. It also expands the 'anonymous' policy class from two routes (/healthz, /version) to four, and the route table's own doc says default-deny is the rule and 'there is nowhere to declare open'.

## Options

1. Cap the nonce store (bounded size + eviction) and rate-limit both routes per-IP. Cheapest, keeps the browser-navigation UX that motivated 'anonymous'.
2. Move GET /github-app/register to readOperator and have the operator open it from an authenticated UI surface that hands the browser a pre-signed one-shot link. Keeps the callback anonymous (it must be — no bearer rides a GitHub redirect).
3. Gate both routes off unless WARREN_FORGE is being configured, i.e. do not expose the registration flow at all on an instance already running with credentials.
4. Accept as-is and document it.

Recommend (1) plus (3): a bounded store with rate limiting, and no registration surface at all on an instance that already has a working forge credential.

## Evidence

- PR #842, src/server/handlers/github-app.ts, src/forge/github-app/registration.ts
- src/server/handlers/route-table.ts — the anonymous policy entries
- scenario 39 caught the route's bare 400 but does not assert anything about repeat-call cost

## DECIDED design (2026-08-13 investigation, prompted by the operator confirming incognito access on app.warren.run)

Live-instance context at decision time: app.warren.run runs WARREN_AUTH=public
(eight-repo allowlist) AND WARREN_FORGE=app with credentials configured — the
registration flow has already served its one purpose there and is pure surface.
Verified: RegistrationSessions sweeps expired nonces on begin()/consume() but
has NO size cap, so memory grows with flood rate inside the 10-minute TTL
window; each live nonce enables one outbound conversion POST from the
instance's egress.

Adopt options (3) + (1) from the list above, refined:

1. **Existence gate (the real fix).** Boot-resolved, logged at startup.
   Explicit `WARREN_GITHUB_APP_REGISTRATION=on|off` wins; the default derives
   fail-safe: OFF when `WARREN_AUTH=public`, OFF when `WARREN_FORGE=app` is
   already configured, ON only for a private instance without App credentials
   (the first-boot case the flow exists for). Gated-off routes answer 404 —
   not 401/403, preserving the public-mode invariant scenario 39 guards. On
   the live instance both default conditions trigger, so the surface
   disappears with zero operator action.
2. **Abuse bounds when the flow IS on.** Cap the pending-nonce store
   (evict-oldest or refuse past ~32 entries). The callback converts nothing
   without a live nonce, so the cap transitively bounds outbound conversions
   to store-size per 10-minute window — one change closes both the memory
   and the egress vector.
3. **Future-proofing.** The `setup_url` return route proposed in warren-54c7
   (`/github-app/installed`) must ride the same gate, or the anonymous class
   grows again.

Non-goals, confirmed during investigation: there is no credential disclosure
(a visitor's App is their own; warren's credentials never pass these routes)
and no warren state change beyond the nonce store. Interim exposure on the
live instance is accepted — no in-app kill switch exists today and the
Cloudflare DNS is DNS-only (no WAF path rules) — because severity is bounded.
closeReason: Shipped the DECIDED design: (1) existence gate resolveGitHubAppRegistrationGate in src/server/github-app-gate.ts — explicit WARREN_GITHUB_APP_REGISTRATION=on|off wins (unknown value fails boot), default OFF under WARREN_AUTH=public, OFF under WARREN_FORGE=app, ON only for private first-boot; resolved once at boot + logged; gated-off /github-app/* routes answer 404 via buildApiRoutes prefix wrap (future /github-app/installed inherits it). (2) RegistrationSessions capped at REGISTRATION_STATE_MAX_PENDING=32 with evict-oldest, bounding outbound conversions per TTL window. Scenario 39 opts the surface back on explicitly; RUNBOOK-K8S §2.6/§3 document the knob. 12/12 gates green.

title: Code comments cite forge-contract.md §4.2, a section that does not exist
description:
Doc-hygiene defect noticed during the 2026-08-12 dogfood session (plan pl-d1c9).

docs/design/forge-contract.md has '## 4. The load-bearing decision: credentials are minted, never held' (line 321) and '### 4.1 The run that outlives its token' (line 375). There is NO §4.2. A reader following a §4.2 pointer lands nowhere.

Several comments about per-spawn credential minting cite 'forge-contract.md §4.2' anyway. The intended target is §4 (the mint-per-operation decision) in every case.

Known sites at the close of the session (verify against HEAD before fixing):

  src/runs/reap/clone-apply.ts:193
  src/runs/reap/finalize-intent.ts:24
  src/runs/reap/run.ts:238
  src/runs/reap/salvage.ts:40
  src/runtime/contract.ts:329       ('contract §4.2')
  src/server/handlers/plan-runs.ts  (in the comment PR #844 rewrote)

## Important: do NOT blanket-replace §4.2 across the repo

Most §4.2 references in src/runtime/k8s/ point at docs/design/k8s-migration.md §4.2, which DOES exist and is correct — pod-spec.ts, workspace-init.ts, seed-configmap.ts, agent-entrypoint.ts and friends. Only the ones naming forge-contract.md (or bare 'contract §4.2' inside forge-credential comments) are wrong.

## How it spread

The pointer was wrong in three files at the start of the session. warren-f8df's run fixed those three. warren-4e1c's run independently introduced four new ones in the reap pipeline, and warren-5497's run copied the spelling again. Each agent read a neighbouring comment and matched it. A wrong citation propagates by imitation, so fixing it once is worth more than the two-line diff suggests.

## Alternative fix worth considering

Rather than editing six call sites, add a §4.2 heading to forge-contract.md covering the mint helper itself (mintGitCredentialSecret and its call-site contract). Every existing pointer would then resolve, and the section is arguably missing anyway — §4 states the decision and §4.1 covers the long-run case, but nothing documents the helper the whole codebase calls.

title: K8s App-mode soak: prove a >1-hour run finalizes without a 401 (pl-d1c9 criterion 7)
description:
The one pl-d1c9 acceptance criterion never verified end-to-end: a K8s run under WARREN_FORGE=app that outlives its hourly installation token must still complete the finalize push and PR open. The unit layer is covered (installation-token cache margin, resolveK8sPushToken preferring the per-spawn mint and failing closed, POST /runs/:id/git-credential callback, salvage path), but no live run has spanned a real token expiry.

Shape: a manually-dispatched (workflow_dispatch) soak workflow or documented operator runbook step — NOT per-PR or nightly, since it costs >1h wall clock plus real App credentials. GitHub's 1-hour installation-token TTL is not configurable, so the wall-clock hour cannot be compressed against the real API.

Recipe: K8s deployment with WARREN_FORGE=app (RUNBOOK-K8S §2.6), dispatch a run whose prompt makes the agent outlast the mint (~70 min: wait, then make a trivial commit). Assert (1) finalize push succeeds without a 401, (2) the PR opens, (3) the pod spec never references the static warren-git-token Secret. Depends practically on the live gke-live deployment switching to App mode, or a dedicated test cluster + sacrificial App installation.

See docs/design/forge-contract.md §4.1 (the three token windows) and warren-c9ac (which closed the control-plane-side fallback).

title: GitHub App registration pages don't match the warren UI styling
