title: Provider credentials are hardcoded per-topology; introduce a provider→env registry in core
description:
Found during a 2026-08-13 self-hosting session on the `local` topology (docker compose, published ghcr image v0.14.1).

## The defect

Provider credential plumbing is hardcoded independently in each topology, so the two support DISJOINT provider sets.

**k8s** — src/runtime/k8s/pod-env.ts:286-308 is two hand-written blocks:

    if (spec.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY === undefined) { ...anthropicSecret... }
    if (spec.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY === undefined) { ...openrouterSecret... }

That is the entire provider surface. No generic mechanism. A third provider needs a warren code change, a new Secret, and a new config field.

**local** — burrow's PI_PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS (src/runtime/pi.ts) carries openai, google, groq, mistral, deepseek, zai. No openrouter. piEnvPassthrough() hits its "unknown providers contribute nothing" branch and returns only the anthropic base triple, so OPENROUTER_API_KEY never reaches the sandbox.

## Resulting support matrix

| topology | providers |
|---|---|
| local  | anthropic, openai, google, groq, mistral, deepseek, zai |
| k8s    | anthropic, openrouter |

Overlap is anthropic ONLY. OpenRouter runs only on k8s. groq/mistral/deepseek/zai/openai/google run only on local. Neither is a superset. Nothing surfaces this: `provider` is a free-form string that reaches pi's --provider flag on both paths, so dispatch accepts a provider the topology cannot authenticate, and the run dies at auth inside the sandbox.

Verified against the container's burrow 0.3.15 AND burrow origin/main (same version, both files unchanged upstream) — not a stale-checkout artifact.

## Proposed fix

A provider -> env-key registry in src/core/, following the src/core/wire.ts single-source-of-truth pattern. RuntimeProvider becomes responsible only for DELIVERING an opaque set of key/value pairs it does not interpret: LocalProvider stuffs them into the sandbox env, K8sProvider maps them to secretKeyRefs. Neither knows what "openrouter" means.

## Notes

- Relates to warren-bad5 — the registry is what makes its dispatch-time modelOverride/provider validation possible.
- The local half cannot fully land while burrow owns the env allowlist. Either it needs a burrow release plus the double pin bump (Dockerfile + package.json), or it waits for warren-c80e step 5 (warren owns bwrap profile generation).
- .env.example documents no OPENROUTER_API_KEY; fold that in.
closeReason: Built src/core/providers.ts: a frozen provider→env-key registry (anthropic, openrouter, openai, google, groq, mistral, deepseek, zai — the union of both topologies' sets) following the wire.ts pattern (src/core imports nothing; define once, re-export outward). K8sProvider now maps EVERY registry provider's canonical env key to an optional secretKeyRef generically (warren-<provider>-key/api-key, overridable per provider via WARREN_K8S_<PROVIDER>_SECRET_NAME/_KEY) — the two hand-written anthropic/openrouter blocks in pod-env.ts are gone; unknown providers contribute nothing rather than erroring. LocalProvider folds collectProviderEnv(serverEnv) into the sandbox env opaquely (domain env wins); burrow's env allowlist still gates delivery — that half is the filed burrow-side follow-up, untouched per scope. warren-bad5's dispatch validation now normalizes provider names through the registry, so casing variants of known providers hit the same mismatch checks. OPENROUTER_API_KEY folded into .env.example. Also fixed a pre-existing nondeterministic-readdir flake in scripts/check-layers.ts scan ordering that was red in this environment. Tests: registry shape, k8s generic mapping (anthropic/openrouter/groq + overrides), unknown-provider behavior, local delivery, casing-variant rejection. bun run check:all: 12/12.

title: docker-compose.yml hardcodes host ports 8080/8081 with no env indirection
description:
Found during a 2026-08-13 self-hosting session following the README compose quickstart verbatim.

## Problem

docker-compose.yml publishes literal host ports:

    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
      - "8081:8081"

A host that already has 8080 in use cannot resolve this without editing a tracked file or adding an untracked docker-compose.override.yml. WARREN_BIND_PORT does not help — it moves the CONTAINER-INTERNAL bind, not the host publish, so it cannot resolve a host-side collision.

On the test box 8080 was held by an unrelated service (squaremap). 

## Why it cost real time

The failure was silent. `docker compose up -d` reported success and `docker compose ps` reported `0.0.0.0:8080-8081->8080-8081/tcp`, while requests to localhost:8080 were answered by the OTHER service. Warren looked broken — 404 on /healthz, /version, and /agents — while being perfectly healthy inside the container (`docker compose exec warren curl localhost:8080/version` returned {"version":"0.14.1"} throughout).

The silent-bind part is colima-specific (its SSH port-forwarder fails to bind without surfacing an error; Docker Desktop hard-fails with "port is already allocated"), so that half is not warren's bug. But the missing knob is: with an env-indirected port this would have been a one-line .env fix instead of a tracked-file edit plus a diagnosis detour.

## Fix

    ports:
      - "${WARREN_HOST_PORT:-8080}:8080"
      - "${WARREN_HOST_PREVIEW_PORT:-8081}:8081"

and document both in .env.example next to the existing WARREN_BIND_PORT / WARREN_PREVIEW_PORT entries, making the host-vs-container distinction explicit since that is the confusing part.
closeReason: compose host ports env-parameterized with defaults; documented in .env.example

title: seeds-merge-autoheal did not fire for conflicted PR #859 — no workflow run for the branch
description: Observed live 2026-08-14: PR #859 (warren/run_092t8hvar3pn) sat DIRTY with a seeds-only conflict; gh run list showed no seeds-merge-autoheal run for that branch (last run was for the previous branch at 16:22). Manual driver-aware merge was required. Determine why the trigger did not fire (event type, concurrency group, or path filter) — and note the heal would also have hit warren-5f0d's updatedAt false positive.
closeReason: Root cause: the workflow triggered only on pull_request events (opened/synchronize/reopened/ready_for_review) with a .seeds/*.jsonl paths filter, but the CONFLICTING state it heals is created by a push to main (another PR's .seeds change merging). No pull_request event fires on the still-open victim PR when main moves, so no run was ever scheduled for warren/run_092t8hvar3pn — it only healed if the agent happened to push again. Fix: added a push-to-main trigger (paths: .seeds/*.jsonl) with a scan job that finds open, same-repo, CONFLICTING PRs touching .seeds/*.jsonl, and a serial (max-parallel: 1) heal-scan matrix job reusing the same driver-aware merge + integrity check + app-token push. Kept the pull_request trigger, the [seeds-autoheal] loop-guard sentinel (checked in heal-scan too), the fork skip, and added a global non-cancelling concurrency group so a main-push scan can never race a PR-event heal. Note: the heal path re-runs check:seeds-integrity, which is also where warren-5f0d's updatedAt false positive would surface; fixing that stays scoped to warren-5f0d.

title: CLI: 'warren login' stdin token flow is documented but unimplemented; missing-token error misdiagnosed
description:
AGENTS.md ('Agent session bootstrap') documents: echo "$WARREN_API_TOKEN" | warren login --url ... as THE history-safe credential flow, but warren login (0.15.0) supports only --token and env WARREN_API_TOKEN; piped stdin is silently ignored. With no token delivered, login surfaces the SERVER 401 message '[unauthorized] invalid bearer token' (exit 4) instead of a client-side 'no token provided (use --token or WARREN_API_TOKEN)', sending the operator to debug token validity instead of token delivery. Fix: implement reading the token from piped stdin when no --token/env is given (keeping the docs' security rationale), and emit a client-side usage error when no credential source yields a token.

CLOSED 2026-08-16 as already-fixed BEFORE filing: stdin token read exists (src/cli/commands/bootstrap.ts:55-62, consumed at login.ts:83-93 with flag>env>stdin precedence) and a missing token is a client-side exit-2 usage error before any server call (login.ts:50-55). Both shipped in 26056fe4 (PR #783, 2026-08-04), 11 days before this row was filed. Minor residual nit (not this row's claim): bare 'warren login' on a TTY ignores an existing client.json token (login.ts:48/56).
closeReason: Already implemented in PR #783 (commit 26056fe4, shipped in v0.15.0): warren login reads the piped stdin token (readTokenFromStdin in src/cli/commands/login.ts) and prints the client-side 'no token supplied' error with exit 2; the reported 401 was a stale WARREN_API_TOKEN from bun cwd .env auto-load outranking stdin per documented precedence (that footgun is tracked separately in warren-8807/warren-2ceb)

title: merge-seeds-jsonl: resolve both-changed updatedAt conflicts (take max) instead of failing
description: Observed live on PRs #878 and #879 (pl-17ca dispatch session 2026-08-15): closing any plan child rewrites updatedAt on the parent and every sibling (blockedBy recompute), so ANY two PRs that each close a sibling of the same plan produce a both-changed-differently updatedAt scalar on the shared rows — which scripts/merge-seeds-jsonl.ts treats as an unresolvable conflict. Every consecutive-sibling PR pair in a plan run therefore needs a manual driver merge (normalize updatedAt to max on both sides, re-run driver). updatedAt is a bookkeeping timestamp, not user data: the driver should resolve both-changed updatedAt by taking the max (or the side whose row otherwise won the field merge). Also blocks seeds-merge-autoheal from healing these PRs, since it runs the same driver.
closeReason: Duplicate of warren-5f0d (same fix: merge-seeds-jsonl resolves both-changed updatedAt by taking max); the pl-17ca PR #878/#879 observation and autoheal-blocking detail were merged into warren-5f0d's description

title: Fresh-install token bootstrap: mint+persist bearer token when WARREN_API_TOKEN unset
description:
When WARREN_AUTH=token and WARREN_API_TOKEN is unset, mint a random bearer token on first boot, persist it under WARREN_DATA_DIR, and print it exactly once to the boot logs so a fresh-install operator never hand-mints a credential.

Acceptance:
- First boot (no WARREN_API_TOKEN, no persisted token): mints a cryptographically random token, persists it under WARREN_DATA_DIR with 0600 permissions, prints it once to the boot logs.
- Subsequent boots reuse the persisted token (no re-mint, no re-print).
- An explicitly set WARREN_API_TOKEN always wins over the persisted one.
- 401 semantics unchanged: a stale or malformed token still rejects (warren-851b posture). Auth is not weakened in any mode.

File set: src/server/auth.ts, src/server/main/index.ts (boot wiring), src/server/main/preview-wiring.ts (derives from the same token), src/cli/commands/serve.ts, plus tests beside each file. docs/http-api.md untouched (no route change). Do not touch src/runtime/k8s/, schema/migration files, src/registry/builtins/, .warren/triggers.yaml, or docs/CONSTITUTION.md.

Conventions: kebab-case filenames, strict TS, verb-led test names with no "should".

title: Tripwire: core never reads an extension endpoint — decide the verdict ingest surface when the first join consumer is seeded
description: Architectural tripwire recorded from owner conversation 2026-08-16 (amendment appended to docs/design/corpus-flywheel.md). Rule: no core code (UI included) ever reads from an extension endpoint — a core reader pointed at an optional extension is the forbidden middle state (neither clean kernel nor integrated feature, invisible to check:layers because it is HTTP, not an import). Tension to resolve: corpus-flywheel.md §1 says warren computes the join trajectory x outcome x verdict, but verdicts live in the judge extension's own store — both cannot stay true. When the first join consumer becomes a seed (review queue ranked by verdict, router, or the dispatch-context log), decide AS ONE CUT: either promote a verdict/annotation ingest surface into core (core owns the fact table + POST endpoint under the locked §12.3 shape; judge becomes a pluggable producer; absent judge = empty table) or execute the §12.1 in-core move (note key-custody cost: warren pod holds an LLM credential and spends on interpretation). Current leaning per the flywheel framing: ingest-surface promotion, matching §4 (core provides small dispatch surfaces, extensions interpret) and open question 1. Until then the judge stays export-only and consumption stays outside core.

Observed 2026-08-16 during the wave-1 dogfood session, AFTER warren-c84c's push-to-main trigger merged (#925): PR #928 (branch warren/run_qe9t2xabkt95, .seeds + .mulch touching) opened DIRTY/CONFLICTING, but no seeds-merge-autoheal run fired for that branch — gh run list showed only main-push and earlier-branch runs. Hypothesis: on pull_request opened, GitHub often reports mergeable=UNKNOWN while the merge commit is computed; the workflow's not-CONFLICTING early-exit then treats the PR as healthy and never rechecks. The push-to-main trigger (c84c) covers later main movement but not a PR that is born conflicted. Fix candidates: retry/poll mergeability for up to ~60s on the opened event before deciding, or re-trigger via a delayed check. Manual driver-aware merge healed #928 (recorded pattern per warren-b34b).
closeReason: Root cause: the push-triggered scan job filtered mergeable == "CONFLICTING" with a single un-polled `gh pr list`, so PRs whose mergeability was still UNKNOWN (the normal state seconds after a main .seeds push flips them) were silently dropped and nothing ever rechecked them. The original UNKNOWN-hypothesis for the opened-event heal is SUPERSEDED: the pull_request heal job already polled UNKNOWN mergeability 6x10s (shipped in PR #845, predating the misses), so that was not the miss. Fix: the scan job now enumerates every open same-repo PR, pre-filters on touched .seeds/*.jsonl files, then polls each candidate mergeability until it resolves (bounded 6x10s, matching the heal job) before deciding. Validation: cannot trigger live GitHub events from the sandbox; the next dogfood wave is the real test.

title: README quickstart on macOS: docker-CLI bind mount silently breaks dispatch ($(command -v docker) not in Docker Desktop shared paths -> /usr/bin/docker mounts as empty dir; image ships no CLI fallback); /srv/warren lands in the VM not the host
description: Verified 2026-08-18 walking the README quickstart verbatim on a macOS host (Docker Desktop, virtiofs). Boot succeeds end-to-end on ghcr 0.17.0: token minted+persisted, healthz/readyz green, UI 200, 401 without bearer. But (1) -v "$(command -v docker)":/usr/bin/docker:ro mounts /opt/homebrew/bin/docker, which is outside Docker Desktop's default shared paths, so the engine creates an empty DIRECTORY at /usr/bin/docker; the image has no docker CLI of its own, so DockerProvider's spawn seam (WARREN_DOCKER_BIN default 'docker') gets 'Permission denied' and every dispatch would fail after a clean-looking boot. (2) -v /srv/warren:/srv/warren resolves inside the Desktop VM, not the macOS host — data invisible on host, lost on VM reset. Fix options: docs note for macOS (install a static linux docker CLI into the data dir + WARREN_DOCKER_BIN, or bake the CLI into the image), and a readyz/doctor check that execs $WARREN_DOCKER_BIN --version so the failure surfaces at boot, not first dispatch. Also observed: a stale local :latest (0.13.1 pre-pl-3007) crash-loops demanding BURROW_API_TOKEN with vocabulary 0.17.0 removed — quickstart may deserve an explicit 'docker pull' line or pinned tag.

closeReason: Seatbelt profile now grants read on the host bun install root ($BUN_INSTALL or ~/.bun) via resolveHostBunInstall in src/sandbox/seatbelt.ts; resolveToolchainPaths also mounts that root + install/global/node_modules for bwrap parity. title: provider-retry classifier ignores the structured httpStatus captured on reap.provider_error — a 5xx without a literal status token in the prose fails closed as unknown
description: Split from warren-a553 (closed born-dead). classifyProviderError (src/runs/retry/provider-retry.ts:153-158) is regex-over-prose only: lastProviderErrorMessage (provider-retry.ts:324-334) reads payload.message and ignores the structured httpStatus that warren-4001's enrichment (src/runs/reap/provider-error.ts:89-96) puts on the same reap.provider_error event. enrichProviderError appends 'status=NNN' into the message only when the base message is opaque (OPAQUE_MESSAGE, provider-error.ts:110), so a non-opaque provider message lacking a literal 5xx token classifies unknown and fails closed despite a known 502 one field over. Fix: thread httpStatus out of the event payload and short-circuit >=500 -> transient, 400-499 -> durable, before the regex fallback. This is the plausible explanation for the 2026-08-17 observation that motivated warren-a553.

title: RemoteTracker bridge: warren-tracker/v1 wire protocol + in-core bridge to an external container (extension holds its own credential)
description: Build RemoteTracker: implementation #2 of IssueTracker and the last tracker core adds (2026-08-04 decision). warren-tracker/v1 is a versioned JSON-over-HTTP wire protocol to an external container: endpoints covering the base contract (get issue, list statuses, close — idempotent), capability discovery (GET /capabilities returns the flag set + protocol version), and the optional plan/metadata/scheduled surfaces; an error taxonomy mapping onto IssueNotFoundError/TrackerError; version negotiated explicitly, mismatch fails loud at boot, not per-call. Config: per-project tracker endpoint + optional bearer resolved from .warren/config.yaml (tracker: {url, tokenEnv}) — the credential is read from the operator's environment, warren never persists it (the extension holds its own tracker token; old blocker B1 dissolves). Caching and backoff live in the bridge per the B3/B4 re-derivation: a small TTL cache on reads (the ready-plans N+1 rides this) and honest 429/5xx backoff. The sandbox stays network:none-compatible: agents never call the tracker; only warren's control plane does, and any future agent-side tracker access proxies through warren (B6). Packaging and handshake conventions consume extensions/audit-log/FRICTION.md. The wire contract is documented in docs/design/issue-tracker.md (warren-240e) and marked experimental until a foreign implementation survives it unchanged. Unit tests against an in-process fake server; the published conformance suite is warren-53ea.

title: base-commit pinning: baseCommit dispatch field split from ref, branch-or-SHA validation at the HTTP boundary, PR base stays branch-shaped
description: Base-commit pinning: the one core feature between today's code and historical issue replay (corpus-flywheel sections 4 and 6). runs.ref carries two meanings today — workspace cut point AND PR base — and a SHA ref breaks the reap: src/runs/reap/run.ts:132 sets baseBranch = run.ref ?? defaultBranch, and a 40-hex PR base is a GitHub 422 that burns pr_open's 3 retries on every replay run. The split: (1) new optional baseCommit on POST /runs (+ CLI --base-commit, SDK field), persisted as a runs column (migration both dialects). (2) Workspace cut resolution becomes baseCommit ?? ref ?? defaultBranch (src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts:249-280) — materialization already handles SHAs on both providers (src/runtime/k8s/workspace-init.ts:220-239 has the detached-checkout fallback; git worktree add accepts any commit-ish). (3) PR base resolution stays branch-shaped: run.ref ?? defaultBranch, never baseCommit. (4) Validate at the HTTP boundary: ref must pass isValidBranchRef (reuse src/runs/target-branch.ts) or be rejected; a 40-hex value in ref is rejected with a pointer to baseCommit; baseCommit must be exactly 40-hex. Regression bar: byte-identical semantics for existing branch refs — pr-fixer and conflict-repair ref-dispatches must not change. (5) src/runs/reap/clone-apply.ts pushCloneDeltasToOrigin guards against a SHA ref (skip with a logged reason). SDK/UI types re-export; gen:docs/gen:openapi/gen:cli-ref committed. Tests: SHA dispatch materializes at the commit and opens its PR against a branch base; branch-ref goldens unchanged.
closeReason: Shipped the baseCommit/ref split: new optional baseCommit on POST /runs + spawnRun (runs.base_commit column, migrations 0051 sqlite / 0046 pg), HTTP-boundary validation (ref must be branch-shaped — a 40-hex ref is a 400 pointing at baseCommit; baseCommit must be exactly 40-hex), workspace cut resolution baseCommit ?? ref ?? continuation base, PR base resolution untouched (run.ref ?? defaultBranch stays byte-identical for branch refs), pushCloneDeltasToOrigin skips SHA refs with a logged reason, infra-lost retry carries baseCommit forward, SDK/CLI (--base-commit)/UI types updated, goldens + cli-reference regenerated. check:all 12/12 green.

title: per-project host-clone serialization + detached-HEAD-safe materialization (materialize 'main' fallback, migration-preflight skip, clone-apply ref guard)
description: Make the shared host clone safe under concurrent dispatch — the replay workload is per-run distinct base commits. (1) Per-project serialization: an in-process keyed mutex around the refreshProjectClone → readProjectDefaults → worktree-materialization critical section (src/projects/refresh.ts:95-183, src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts:134-138, the LocalProvider materialization) so two dispatches on one project cannot interleave checkout --force / reset --hard with reads. In-process is sufficient: one warren process owns the clone. (2) Detached-HEAD-safe materialization: for a baseCommit dispatch (warren-aaf7), do not mutate the host-clone HEAD at all — fetch the object (git fetch origin <sha>, falling back to a full fetch where the server lacks allowReachableSHA1InWant) and git worktree add -b <runBranch> <ws> <sha> directly; the shared clone's checked-out branch never moves. (3) Sweep the audit's small wrongs: src/workspace/materialize.ts:234 hard-codes 'main' as the fallback base (wrong for master/develop repos — thread the project default); migration-preflight (src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts:288-317) skips baseCommit dispatches (it fires on every non-default ref today and its heal path would commit onto a detached HEAD); document the k8s repo-cache refspec limit (ensureMirror fetches only heads/tags, so non-branch-reachable SHAs fall through to a direct clone — accepted). Tests: interleaved dispatches with different refs leave the clone consistent; a master-default project materializes correctly. This also closes the residual same-clone concern from warren-f6b5.
closeReason: Shipped per-project host-clone serialization (withProjectCloneLock around the spawnRun dispatch critical section, proven by interleaved-dispatch tests), detached-HEAD-safe baseCommit materialization (fetch-only refreshProjectClone.fetchCommit leg: sha fetch with full-fetch fallback + object verify, HEAD never moves; worktree cut at the SHA), migration-preflight skip for baseCommit dispatches, the materialize 'main' hard-code replaced with an explicit baseBranch requirement (master-default test), and the k8s repo-cache refspec limit documented in RUNBOOK-K8S.md. check:all 12/12 green.

title: provider-retry classifier reads structured signals: httpStatus/upstreamBody before message, retryOf lineage on the retry run
description: warren-a553 was closed born-dead (PR #935 shipped run-level provider retry), but the 2026-08-18 investigation found the live residual: maybeRetryProviderError (src/runs/retry/provider-retry.ts:213-243) classifies from lastProviderErrorMessage(events) — payload.message only. warren-4001 enriched reap.provider_error payloads with structured provider/model/httpStatus/upstreamBody (src/runs/reap/provider-error.ts:75-95), and pi frequently emits the opaque literal 'Provider returned error' (OPAQUE_MESSAGE, provider-error.ts:110) → matches no TRANSIENT/DURABLE pattern → 'unknown' → fails closed → no retry, precisely on the flaky-provider runs the retry exists for. Fix: read the full payload; classify on httpStatus first (5xx/529/408 transient; 4xx durable, keeping the existing DURABLE_PATTERNS semantics incl. 429-as-durable), then upstreamBody text, then message; unknown still fails closed. Also align lineage with the retryOf convention: the provider retry sets parentRunId + cloneKind='replicate' and no retry_of today — additionally set retryOf: run.id on the spawn call (provider-retry.ts:~275) so retry projections and the dispatch-context log (warren-d6ca) see all retries uniformly. The single-retry bound stays event-marker-based (spawn.provider_retry) — must not double-retry when both markers exist. Tests in provider-retry.test.ts: opaque message + httpStatus 529 retries; 401 with 5xx-looking body text does not; retryOf lands on the successor run. The pi-side opaque-body fix remains upstream (warren-962f, out of plan).
closeReason: upstreamBody classification tier added between httpStatus and prose message (classifyProviderError 3rd param, provider-retry.ts); retry spawn now sets retryOf: run.id. 23 tests pass in provider-retry.test.ts incl. opaque+529 retry, 401+5xx-body no-retry, retryOf assertion; check:all 12/12 green.

title: seeds-merge-autoheal: no heal fired for any of 7 dogfood PRs opened CONFLICTING on 2026-08-19 — fresh evidence for warren-c97b
description: During the pl-a37b Track D dogfood session (2026-08-19), every warren-authored PR that outlived a prior merge opened or went CONFLICTING/DIRTY on GitHub because of .seeds/issues.jsonl: PRs #988, #992, #997, #999, #1000, #1001, #1002. closeReason: Root cause confirmed: the 7 dogfood PRs (#988/#992/#997/#999/#1000/#1001/#1002) outlived a prior .seeds merge, so they went CONFLICTING via a push to main — no pull_request synchronize fired on them. The push-triggered scan job DID fire (runs appeared on main) but filtered on a single un-polled `gh pr list` for mergeable == "CONFLICTING"; at scan time GitHub still reported UNKNOWN for exactly those PRs, so they were silently dropped and never rechecked. Fix: the scan job now lists every open same-repo PR, pre-filters on .seeds/*.jsonl touched files, and polls each candidate mergeability until resolved (bounded 6x10s, matching the heal job). Supersedes warren-c97b. Validation: next dogfood wave is the real test.

title: check:size merge-union overshoot: two green PRs can union a file over its ratchet; autoheal only covers bundle-size
description: Observed three times in the pl-a37b Phase B dogfood session (PRs #1007, #1009, #1011): src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts sat exactly at its 500-line budget, each in-flight PR added lines to it, and every driver-aware update-branch merge pushed the union to 501-502 — failing check:size in CI even though both sides were individually green. title: provider-retry auto-retry drops providerOverride/modelOverride — retry runs on the agent-default model
description:

title: Implement durable Warren dispatch and restart reconciliation
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Step 7 of plan pl-91b6.

Parent seed: warren-cdbb — OpenClaw upstream-contribution controller V0
Run `sd plan show pl-91b6` for the full plan context, dependency graph, risks, and acceptance criteria.
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

## Scope and acceptance

Implement the durable dispatch/reconciliation state machine that converts one admitted work item into a Warren run without duplicate paid work. In one transaction reserve the full run cap and persist a deterministic dispatch action plus exact request digest before calling Warren. Send the stable idempotency key; on a confirmed response persist the run id and reconcile by authoritative GET reads until terminal. If the POST outcome is ambiguous and no known run id exists, enter `dispatch_uncertain` and create an attention item instead of retrying. On restart, expire leases, reconstruct reservations, resume known-run reads, settle actual cost when terminal, and leave unknown cost conservatively reserved. Terminal success records the pushed branch/ref required for later dry-run PR intent; failure records structured outcome without advancing. Acceptance: fake-server tests prove normal dispatch, concurrent tick exclusion, accepted-response-loss, restart with known run, restart with unknown run, terminal settlement, unknown-cost reservation, and no second POST for an uncertain action.
closeReason: Implemented durable intent-before-I/O Warren dispatch and restart reconciliation without duplicate POSTs

description:

## Scope and acceptance

Implement the V0 cross-fork PR intent builder and journaler. Given an approved OpenClaw profile plus a succeeded Warren run against the `warren-run-bot` fork, derive an exact upstream request targeting `openclaw/openclaw` default branch with head `<fork-owner>:<run-branch>`. Compose a repository-specific title/body containing the linked issue, AI-assisted disclosure, problem/solution/user impact, validation evidence placeholders or collected facts, Warren run reference, and maintainer-editability/operator-review notes required by policy. Persist the rendered request digest as a planned dry-run action and emit it through machine-readable CLI data; never call a GitHub mutation. Implement read-only reconciliation for an already-known upstream PR identity using GitHub participating notifications as wake-ups and authoritative PR/review/comment/check reads as truth. Normalize issue comments, submitted reviews/requested changes, code review comments, check rollups, author association, timestamps, and node ids into durable source events; deduplicate by repository plus event kind plus node id and tolerate reordered pages. ## Scope and acceptance

Compose the V0 operator CLI and one deterministic reconciliation tick from the approved lower-level modules. Commands must include manifest validate/import, digest approval, one-shot dry-run tick, campaign/work-item status, action journal, and attention listing/acknowledgment, with NDJSON default and optional human-readable output. Tick ordering is lease -> validate/admit -> reserve/journal -> Warren dispatch or reconcile -> render dry-run PR intent -> read-only GitHub reconcile -> settle/report; every stage is restart-safe and bounded. Configuration comes from explicit environment/file paths, never ambient repo imports; secrets are accepted only from named environment variables and redacted from errors/output. The CLI must have no command that posts a PR/comment or discovers GKE secrets. title: Provision the K8s repo-cache mirror PVC so openclaw run pods stop re-cloning 2.9GB per dispatch
description: The campaign-controller's openclaw runs (prj_5ek8btnfvkjc, warren-run-bot/openclaw fork, ~2.9GB) pay a full network clone in every run pod's workspace-init because the optional git-mirror repo-cache PVC is not provisioned in the warren-502318 cluster. Hard numbers 2026-08-26: attempts 1 (run_frqh8bc3qm6n) and 2 (run_ee5z5arpefg5) each sat ~20min in Init:0/1 re-downloading 2.9GB before the agent started. Owner call: this is a confirmed payer for workspace/container caching per docs/design/resumable-agent-environments.md — the repo-cache mirror PVC is the V0 slice (workspace-init already supports mirror reuse: clone --mirror once, fetch after); the resumable-environments record owns the full warm-start direction. Mind the RWO Multi-Attach history (warren-554f).
closeReason: Provisioned the repo-cache mirror PVC in the warren-502318 cluster and verified the fix live. warren-repo-cache is RWX (standard-rwx / Filestore Basic HDD, 1Ti tier minimum) in warren-runs — RWX because run pods schedule across nodes, so the warren-554f RWO Multi-Attach deadlock rules out the single-node recipe. Created imperatively (like the Secrets); a one-off Job pre-warmed the openclaw mirror (2.8G at sha256(gitUrl).git). Env wired three ways so it survives everything: live (kubectl set env + rollout), deploy pipeline (deploy-gke.yml renders WARREN_K8S_REPO_CACHE_PVC from the repo variable of the same name, commit de5d422d), and the local gitignored gke-live overlay. Verified with a capped openclaw run (run_5a0a1csmdnvw): workspace-init logged 'updating repo-cache mirror' + 'materialized from repo-cache mirror', Init 22s vs the ~20min re-clones in run_frqh8bc3qm6n/run_ee5z5arpefg5. Docs updated (deploy/k8s README multi-node RWX section, RUNBOOK-K8S §5.3 + env table).

title: warren up: runtime autodetect (darwin sandbox-exec / linux bwrap / docker fallback), data dir + boot defaults, automatic operator-token client login
description:
END STATE: `warren up` is the one command that takes a fresh machine from installed-CLI to a running warren instance with the operator already logged in, choosing the runtime so the user never reads the bwrap/docker/k8s table.

New CLI command `up` (src/cli/commands/up.ts, registered in src/cli/main.ts) that:

1. Detects the runtime: darwin -> LocalProvider (sandbox-exec); linux with bwrap on PATH -> LocalProvider (bwrap); otherwise, if a docker daemon is reachable, print the compose guidance and exit 0 (this step does NOT implement a docker orchestration path); otherwise exit non-zero naming what is missing. Print one sentence stating the choice.
2. Defaults WARREN_DATA_DIR to ~/.warren/data (created 0700) when unset; leaves an explicit env value alone.
3. Boots the server in-process exactly as `warren serve` does (reuse runServe/bootServer — no duplicate boot path; spawnRun-style single-implementation rule applies).
4. After boot, reads the minted-or-persisted operator token from the token boot result and writes base URL + token to the client config (~/.warren/client.json, mode 0600) the same way `warren login` does — reuse the login persistence function, do not re-implement it. The user never greps a log for mintedOperatorToken.
5. Prints the URL and stays in the foreground; SIGINT/SIGTERM shuts down cleanly (same semantics as serve).

Scope guard: no interactive prompts in this step (that is the credential-wizard child), no browser opening (that is the auth-handoff child). Non-interactive flags must keep working for scripts: `warren up --no-open` reserved but inert here.

VERIFY: on macOS, `warren up` from a checkout boots, writes client config, and `warren projects` works immediately with no env vars set. Unit tests cover runtime detection matrix + token persistence. gen:cli-ref regenerated. bun run check:all passes.
closeReason: warren up implemented: runtime autodetect (sandbox-exec/bwrap/docker heuristic), ~/.warren/data default 0700, boot via runServe with onBooted hook, operator token auto-persisted to client.json 0600; smoke-tested end-to-end mint path; check:all 12/12 green.

title: One-time browser auth handoff: single-use setup code minted at boot, /setup redemption route logs the browser into the UI, warren up auto-opens it
description:
END STATE: the browser lands in the warren UI already authenticated — the operator token never passes through human hands on the happy path.

Mechanism (one-time setup code, so the long-lived token never sits in browser history):

1. Server: when booting via `warren up` (opt-in boot flag, e.g. BootServerOptions.setupHandoff), mint a single-use, short-TTL (10 min) setup code bound to the operator token. Storage in-memory is fine (same posture as the github-app state nonces). No code is minted on ordinary `warren serve` boots.
2. New route GET /setup?code=<code> in ROUTE_TABLE: consumes the code (single-use), and serves a tiny page that stores the operator token where the UI login expects it (same localStorage key the login page writes), then redirects to /. An invalid/expired/spent code renders a 400 page pointing at the UI login. The route is anonymous by necessity — model it on the /github-app nonce policy so the public-instance leak guard (scenario 39) stays green.
3. CLI: `warren up` opens the browser at http://<host>:<port>/setup?code=... using open(1)/xdg-open, suppressed by --no-open and when stdout is not a TTY.
4. Wire surface: gen:docs / gen:openapi regenerated for the new route; check:client-contract stays green (the UI does not call /setup via the API client — it is a navigation target).

Security notes for the PR: single-use + TTL + loopback-by-default; document in SECURITY.md that /setup exists only on setup-handoff boots and never on WARREN_AUTH=public instances (refuse to arm the handoff under public auth).

VERIFY: `warren up` on a fresh data dir opens a browser tab that is logged in; a second GET of the same code 400s; acceptance:public unaffected. bun run check:all passes.
closeReason: Merged: single-use 10-min setup code armed only by warren up boots, GET /setup redemption route stores the operator token in the SPA's warren.apiToken key and redirects, warren up auto-opens the URL (open/xdg-open, TTY-gated, --no-open suppresses); refused under WARREN_AUTH=public; scenario 39 extended and green; check:all 12/12.

title: Credential wizard in warren up: Claude subscription via claude setup-token or pasted API key, GitHub token via gh detection or paste, persisted 0600 under ~/.warren
description:
END STATE: `warren up` on a machine with no credentials walks the user to a working credential set without ever mentioning .env, PAT scopes, or machine accounts. Spike-proven basis (2026-08-27): a run authenticated ONLY by CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (Claude Max) succeeded end-to-end on the macOS local runtime (run_zqf52t76x4m3).

Wizard behavior (runs inside `warren up` before boot, only when a needed credential is absent from env AND from the persisted store; every prompt skippable, fully bypassed by --non-interactive):

1. Model credential: offer (a) 'Use your Claude subscription' — if the `claude` CLI is on PATH, shell out to `claude setup-token` and capture the sk-ant-oat token; otherwise print the one-line install hint and accept a pasted token; or (b) paste an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. State plainly that subscription auth serves only the claude-code harness; other providers still need API keys.
2. GitHub credential: offer (a) detected `gh auth token` (show the account name, ask to use it), or (b) paste a token. Frame this as temporary bootstrap — the GitHub App flow (separate child) is the durable path; the wizard must still work with neither by skipping.
3. Persistence: write accepted values to a warren-owned env file under ~/.warren (e.g. ~/.warren/env, mode 0600, created 0700 dir). `warren up` (and only up — serve is unchanged) loads this file into the boot env with real env vars taking precedence. Never write ANTHROPIC/GitHub credentials into client.json (decision D5 keeps that file to base URL + token).
4. Git author identity: when unset, default WARREN_GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL from the GitHub token's login (`<login>` / `<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com` via one /user call) instead of demanding a machine account; print what was chosen and how to override.

VERIFY: unit tests for precedence (env > stored > prompt), 0600 modes, and non-interactive bypass; manual: fresh HOME + wizard -> dispatched run succeeds. bun run check:all passes.
closeReason: Credential wizard in warren up: claude setup-token / pasted token / API key, gh detection + paste, ~/.warren/env 0600 store, env>stored>prompt precedence, non-interactive bypass; 12/12 gates green

title: Sandbox git preflight: verify the resolved git executes inside the sandbox profile at project-add and doctor --local; clear error instead of dropped_commit
description:
END STATE: a git binary that cannot execute inside the sandbox is caught at project-add or doctor time with an error naming the binary and the fix — never discovered post-hoc as a dropped_commit run failure.

Spike evidence (2026-08-27, macOS): sandbox toolchain resolution follows the server PATH (src/sandbox/resolve + env.ts PATH-prepend); a nix-store git resolved first, its dylibs were outside the sandbox profile's readable paths, every git call inside the run died with a dyld "Library not loaded" error, the agent completed anyway, and the run reaped failed/dropped_commit ($0.16 spent to discover a config problem).

Deliver:

1. An in-sandbox toolchain probe: run `git --version` (and the resolved agent harness binary with --version) inside the composed sandbox profile — the same mounts/PATH a real run gets. Implement once in src/sandbox/ and call it from (a) `warren doctor --local` as a named check, and (b) project registration or first dispatch on the LocalProvider path (cheap, cached per boot).
2. On probe failure: a structured error naming the resolved binary path, the underlying exec/dyld error, and the recovery hint ("this git cannot run inside the sandbox; install a system git (/usr/bin/git on macOS) or adjust PATH before booting warren").
3. macOS resilience: when the PATH-resolved git fails the probe but /usr/bin/git passes, prefer /usr/bin/git for the sandbox toolchain and log the substitution — a fresh Mac with nix/homebrew-exotic git must not be broken by default.
4. Do not change reap semantics: dropped_commit stays for genuinely dropped commits; this issue is about failing earlier.

VERIFY: unit tests with a stub binary that fails exec; doctor --local on this repo's dev machine (nix git) reports the failure + substitution; a real dispatch on macOS then succeeds (spike run 2 pattern). bun run check:all passes.

title: Console shell: make the topbar span full width on desktop and mobile (w-full on console-topbar.tsx:119 header, fix console-shell.tsx:54 row-flex wrapper and :39-51 nested-header mobile arm, align topbar gutter px-3.5 md:px-6 to the Direction C page grid)
description:
Symptom: the topbar/header stops roughly mid-viewport on every page (border-b terminates mid-page; RUNTIME/IDENTITY bunch up next to BURN instead of right-aligning). Global, but the origin is the shell.

Root cause: src/ui/src/components/console/console-shell.tsx:54 wraps <ConsoleTopbar> in `<div className="hidden md:flex">` — a ROW-flex wrapper. The topbar's <header> (console-topbar.tsx:119) has no w-full/flex-1 and flex-basis:auto, so as a row-flex item it sizes to max-content (the width of the HEALTH/RUNNING/QUEUE/BURN/RUNTIME/IDENTITY figures). The internal `<span className="flex-1" />` spacer at console-topbar.tsx:132 contributes ZERO intrinsic width (flex-basis:0%), so it cannot widen the header. The mobile arm has the same defect: console-shell.tsx:39-51 nests ConsoleTopbar's <header> inside another flex-row <header> (also nested landmark elements + doubled border-b). Present since the shell landed in 8a60b103 (#1074); the `shrink-0` on the topbar header shows it was authored expecting a column parent.

Fix:
1. console-topbar.tsx:119 — add `w-full` (or `min-w-0 flex-1`) to the header classes. This fixes BOTH the desktop wrapper and the mobile nesting.
2. Optionally console-shell.tsx:54 — `hidden md:flex` -> `hidden md:block` (desktop-only fix; keep the header change regardless).
3. Clean the mobile arm's nested <header>-inside-<header> (console-shell.tsx:39-51): avoid double landmarks/stacked border-b.
4. Gutter alignment: topbar uses px-4 sm:px-[22px] while Direction C pages self-pad px-3.5 md:px-6 (operations.tsx:66, runs.tsx:218). Align the topbar to px-3.5 md:px-6 so figures sit flush with page content.

Verify at md+ and mobile widths; no max-w-* constraints exist elsewhere (index.css has no header/main rules).
closeReason: Topbar header now w-full/min-w-0/flex-1, shell wrappers use md:block + de-nested mobile header, gutter aligned px-3.5 md:px-6; build:ui and check:all (12/12) green.

title: Live durations: add a shared useNow(intervalMs) hook, make 'now' a required arg in runs/runs-format.ts:19 and plan-runs/walk-state.ts:47, and thread a 1s tick through runs-table/runs-cards and plan-runs walk-row/walk-cards (port the operations.tsx:31-39 pattern; tick only while a visible row is non-terminal)
description:
Symptom: the /runs Duration column for live runs never updates without a refresh; /operations durations tick every second. /plan-runs Elapsed has the same freeze (desktop table + mobile cards).

Root cause: the list pages re-render only on their react-query refetch (refetchInterval: 45_000 at runs.tsx:145-151 and plan-runs.tsx:63 / walk-row.tsx:27 / walk-cards.tsx:43; the lifecycle-stream invalidation in hooks/use-lifecycle-stream-invalidation.ts:52-56 only fires on state-change events, and a run that stays `running` emits none). Duration math evaluates Date.now() at render time:
- src/ui/src/pages/runs/runs-format.ts:19 — formatDuration(row, now = Date.now()) with the default-param footgun; called with no `now` from runs/runs-table.tsx:197 and runs/runs-cards.tsx:63.
- src/ui/src/pages/plan-runs/walk-state.ts:47-54 — planRunElapsed uses new Date() internally; called from walk-row.tsx:88 and walk-cards.tsx:61.
The working pattern is operations.tsx:31-39: NOW_TICK_MS=1000, const [now,setNow]=useState(()=>Date.now()) + setInterval effect, `now` threaded as a prop, and the pure helpers REQUIRE now (operations/operations.helpers.ts:41 phaseElapsedMs(run, now)).

Fix:
1. Extract a shared hooks/use-now.ts (useNow(intervalMs), interval cleaned up on unmount). Consider having operations.tsx adopt it too.
2. runs.tsx: tick 1s only while at least one visible row is non-terminal (avoid pointless 1Hz re-render of terminal-only lists); thread `now` through RunsTable (runs-table.tsx:233-277 -> RunsTableRow :138 -> :197) and RunsCardList (runs-cards.tsx:63).
3. plan-runs: same for walk-row.tsx / walk-cards.tsx.
4. Make `now` a REQUIRED parameter in runs-format.ts:19 and walk-state.ts:47 so no call site can silently freeze again.
Run-detail pages already poll at 3-5s and are acceptable — out of scope.
closeReason: Shared useNow hook (src/ui/src/hooks/use-now.ts) with required-now formatDuration/planRunElapsed; 1s tick threaded through runs/plan-runs tables+cards gated on non-terminal rows; operations.tsx migrated; build:ui and check:all 12/12 green.

title: Run detail event stream: truncate + widen the kind column (event-tail.tsx:53 add truncate + title tooltip, widen w-[108px] to fit common reap.* kinds) and derive the coupled ml-[117px] payload offset (:62) from the column widths
description:
Symptom: on /runs/:id, long event kinds like reap.workspace_destroyed paint over the summary text in their event-stream row.

Root cause: src/ui/src/pages/run-detail/event-tail.tsx:53-55 renders the kind cell as `w-[108px] shrink-0 font-mono text-[9px]` with NO truncate/overflow-hidden. Event kinds are single dot-separated tokens with zero line-break opportunities, so the text renders at full intrinsic width and overflows the 108px box horizontally onto the sibling summary span (which is min-w-0 flex-1 at :56 and stays anchored — pure paint-over). At 9px mono (~5.4px/char) the cell fits ~20 chars; ~16 server-emittable kinds exceed that, worst offenders: reap.workspace_destroy_record_failed (36 chars), trigger.cleared_extension_failed (32), reap.pr_annotate_preview_skipped (32), reap.clone_deltas_push_skipped (30), reap.workspace_destroy_skipped (30), reap.workspace_salvage_failed / reap.workspace_destroy_failed (29), watchdog.terminal_reconciled (28), reap.workspace_destroyed (24), waiting_for_parent_merge (24), etc. The Event explorer already renders this column correctly: event-explorer.tsx:379-381 uses `truncate`.

Fix:
1. event-tail.tsx:53 — add `truncate` and `title={eventKindLabel(event)}` so the full kind is readable on hover.
2. Widen w-[108px] to ~w-[150px]-w-[168px] so common reap.* kinds fit unelided (36-char kinds still need truncate).
3. Coupled magic number: event-tail.tsx:62 hardcodes `ml-[117px]` on the expanded payload <pre> (= 42 seq + 7 gap + 68 clock). Derive/comment it from the column widths, and update it consistently with any width change.
4. Note: eventKindLabel (run-detail/event-summary.ts:58-61) can emit space-containing labels ("extension error", "compaction ▶") that currently wrap to two lines in the same cell — truncate makes these single-line too, which is the desired consistency.
No component tests exist for this tree; pure class edit.
closeReason: Kind column now truncate + title tooltip, widened to derived KIND_W=168 via style; payload offset derived from column constants replacing ml-[117px]; build:ui and check:all (12/12) green.

title: Run detail layout: let the event stream fill the column to the bottom of the sidebar (event-tail.tsx:122 add flex-1, :185 replace h-[520px] with min-h-0 flex-1 + min-h floor) and cap PromptPanel (side-panels.tsx:152 max-h + overflow-auto) so the sidebar cannot run the row height away
description:
Symptom: on /runs/:id the event stream box ends well above the bottom, leaving a large dead area beneath it, while the steer box (last sidebar panel) sits far below the stream's bottom edge.

Layout map: console-shell.tsx:58 <main> is the scroll container. Page root run-detail/index.tsx:316 is flex min-h-full flex-col with pb-12. The two-column row at :337 is `flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-3 xl:flex-row`: left column :338 (`flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col`) holds only <EventTail>; right <aside> :346 (`w-full shrink-0 xl:w-[326px]`) stacks RuntimePanel, BudgetPanel, optional PreviewPanel, RunDefinitionPanel, PromptPanel (UNBOUNDED height — side-panels.tsx:152 has no max-h), and SteerForm — every panel shrink-0, no overflow on the aside, so the sidebar sets the row height.

Root cause (two defects in event-tail.tsx): (a) :185 scroll body is hardcoded `h-[520px] overflow-auto`; (b) :122 the <section> has min-h-0 but NO flex-1, so it never claims the row height the left column receives. Card height is a constant ~561px; dead space = sidebarHeight − 561px, and it also grows with viewport height. The nested fixed-height scroll region inside the page scroll container is why the log feels tiny.

Fix (Option A — stream fills to the bottom of the steer box):
1. event-tail.tsx:122 — add flex-1 (keep min-h-0).
2. event-tail.tsx:185 — replace h-[520px] with `min-h-0 flex-1`, plus a min-h-[320px] floor for short viewports.
3. side-panels.tsx:152 — cap PromptPanel with max-h + overflow-auto so a huge prompt cannot run the row height away.
4. Consider `min-h-0 overflow-y-auto` on the aside (index.tsx:346) so an extreme sidebar scrolls independently.
5. Design call: index.tsx:316 min-h-full + pb-12 leaves the stretched card 48px above the viewport bottom — keep or trim deliberately.
Depends on the kind-column issue (same file) landing first.
closeReason: event-tail.tsx section gets flex-1 and the scroll body min-h-[320px] flex-1 replacing h-[520px]; PromptPanel capped with max-h-[240px] overflow-auto; build:ui and check:all (12/12) green

title: Telemetry bars: extract a shared MeterBar primitive with a flex-1 min-w-0 track (percentage resolves against the track, drop shrink-0 from the mark) and adopt it at all four overflow sites — loop-tab.tsx:84-107, behavior-tab.tsx:99-113 ('Where runs die'), behavior-tab.tsx:21-38 (difficulty row), judge-tab.tsx:161-178 — plus fix the loop-tab.tsx:148 min-w column floor at 90D
description:
Symptom: every /telemetry tab shows horizontal bars extending past the right page edge, producing document-level horizontal scroll. Note: recharts and components/ui/chart.tsx NO LONGER EXIST — warren-7197 (commit 654804d1) rebuilt all tabs with hand-rolled div/SVG marks.

Root cause: each bar mark is a percentage-width div that is a SIBLING of fixed-width label/value elements in the same flex row, and carries shrink-0. A CSS % width resolves against the WHOLE row content box, not leftover space — so the widest bar (always exactly 100%, widths normalized to max) equals the panel width, plus label + gaps + number on top (~150-190px overflow). shrink-0 forbids flexbox from correcting it. Overflow escapes TelemetryPanel (overflow visible) to the document (main is overflow-y-auto only). The shell/panel min-w-0 wiring is fine and NOT at fault.

All four sites (widths all computed as `${Math.max(4, Math.round((v/max)*100))}%`):
1. src/ui/src/pages/telemetry/loop-tab.tsx:84-107 — StageRow ("Where the time goes"): w-24 shrink-0 label :90, bar shrink-0 + style width :98/:105.
2. src/ui/src/pages/telemetry/behavior-tab.tsx:99-113 — FailureCauseRow ("Where runs die"): w-32 shrink-0 label :102, bar :106-107.
3. behavior-tab.tsx:21-38 — DifficultyRow bar :31-32 inside a td flex row :29; % resolves against the cell and overflows into FAIL SHARE.
4. src/ui/src/pages/telemetry/judge-tab.tsx:161-178 — failing-classes bar: w-36 shrink-0 label :166, bar :170-171.
Secondary: loop-tab.tsx:148 renders N columns min-w-[3px] flex-1 with gap-1 — at 90D a hard ~625px floor flex-1 cannot shrink below.

Fix: extract ONE shared MeterBar primitive (e.g. in telemetry/telemetry-panel.tsx or a new telemetry/meter-bar.tsx — no shared bar primitive exists today): fixed label + `flex-1 min-w-0` TRACK div, with the percentage width applied to the mark INSIDE the track; drop shrink-0 from the mark. title: Judge export proxy: add an operator-gated warren route (route-table.ts, ahead of the SPA catch-all) that reverse-proxies the judge /verdicts.jsonl export using a server-held base URL + JUDGE_EXPORT_TOKEN from env, so the browser stays same-origin under connect-src 'self' and the extension token never reaches the client; regenerate gen:docs + gen:openapi
description:
Context: the /telemetry judge tab probes the judge extension by fetching `${VITE_JUDGE_BASE_URL ?? ""}/verdicts.jsonl` (src/ui/src/pages/telemetry/judge-verdicts.ts:63,:74). With the default "" that is a same-origin request to warren, which does not serve/proxy /verdicts.jsonl — the SPA catch-all (src/server/ui.ts:71-79, deliberately last in the chain per src/server/server.ts:161) answers 200 + index.html, which the client misreads as "not deployed". A cross-origin base URL cannot work either: warren serves CSP connect-src 'self' on every response (src/server/response.ts:22-23), the judge (extensions/judge/src/server.ts) emits no CORS headers, and its bearer credential JUDGE_EXPORT_TOKEN (server.ts:83-90, distinct from warren's token, secret in deploy/k8s/extensions/judge/secrets.yaml:29) must never reach the browser. VITE_JUDGE_BASE_URL is set nowhere in the repo (Dockerfile builds the UI bare). The judge is a separate process/Service: Bun.serve on JUDGE_EXPORT_PORT 8080 (server.ts:180), ClusterIP judge.warren.svc.cluster.local:8080, no ingress path. extensions/audit-log/FRICTION.md:180-195 records the missing scoped-credential mechanism.

Fix — warren-side reverse proxy (keeps the extensions seam intact):
1. New operator-gated GET route in src/server/handlers/route-table.ts (any concrete path, e.g. /extensions/judge/verdicts.jsonl) registered ahead of the UI catch-all, proxying to a server-held judge base URL with Authorization from a server-held token; both from env (e.g. WARREN_JUDGE_BASE_URL / WARREN_JUDGE_EXPORT_TOKEN). Unconfigured -> a distinct honest status (e.g. 404/501 envelope the client can classify as "absent"), never the SPA fallback. Pass through limit/afterId query params and the X-Verdicts-Max-Id header (server.ts:103).
2. Respect handler-layer seams: no src/db/schema imports; go through boot-wired deps. Mind check:layers — api.github.com-style host literals are forge-only, but the judge URL is env-config, fine.
3. Regenerate gen:docs + gen:openapi and commit; add tests for configured/unconfigured/upstream-401/upstream-down paths.
Forward-blocks the judge client fix and the k8s deploy wiring.
closeReason: GET /extensions/judge/verdicts.jsonl proxy added (judge-proxy.ts + route-table entry, 12/12 gates green, gen:docs/openapi regenerated)

title: Judge tab client: point judge-verdicts.ts at the warren proxy path, classify honestly — empty NDJSON page = available with zero rows (:103), HTML/wrong content-type = misconfigured instead of swallowed parse failures (:92-101), distinct AbsentPanel copy per state (judge-tab.tsx:32-35) — and add the first tests for summarizeJudgeVerdicts/fetchJudgeVerdicts
description:
Symptom: /telemetry judge tab prints "The judge extension is not deployed against this instance." while the judge IS deployed. Even after the warren-side proxy exists, the client has three honesty defects to fix (src/ui/src/pages/telemetry/judge-verdicts.ts + judge-tab.tsx):

Empty page misclassified: judge-verdicts.ts:103 maps rows.length===0 to {available:false, reason:"error"} — but a healthy judge with zero verdicts legitimately returns an empty NDJSON body (extensions/judge/src/server.ts:98-99) plus the X-Verdicts-Max-Id high-water header (:103). title: profile: versioned agentGuidance block injected into every dispatch prompt (minimal-diff, no new public config surface, no fail-closed validation on previously-valid config, cite existing mechanisms)
description: The live campaign prompt covered process discipline (commit cadence, scoped validation, forbidden paths) but no design norms, and the agent on openclaw#131131 claimed a new public config surface with fail-closed validation and missed an existing fallback mechanism — exactly what upstream review then blocked. Add an agentGuidance block to the repository-policy profile: an ordered list of norm strings, versioned and covered by the policy digest so approval binds it. The dispatcher appends it to every dispatched prompt (initial and follow-up runs) under a clearly delimited section. Seed the default profile with repo-agnostic norms: smallest possible diff; never introduce or reserve new public config/API surface without maintainer direction; never add fail-closed validation over previously-accepted input; search for and cite existing mechanisms addressing the same failure in the final summary; state unprovable claims as known gaps rather than omitting them. Acceptance: prompt composition test proves the block renders for both initial and follow-up dispatches; digest test proves editing guidance changes the policy digest; no norm text lives in controller source, only in profile data.
closeReason: Added a versioned agentGuidance block to the repository-policy schema (optional, validated when present, covered by the policy digest) plus renderAgentGuidance/composeDispatchPrompt; the tick dispatch path now composes manifest.prompt with the profile's guidance for initial and follow-up dispatches. Openclaw profile seeded with the five ClawSweeper norms. title: profile+manifest: evidence tiers — declare local-provable vs external-proof-required per issue; render the known-gap / operator-proof slot in the PR body
description: Upstream reviewers distinguish evidence that local test harnesses can produce from proof that needs a real external system (openclaw#131131 was blocked pending a real-provider trace no network-restricted run pod can ever produce). Make this a first-class classification: the repository profile declares the evidence tiers it recognizes (e.g. local-provable, external-proof-required) and the manifest tags each issue with a tier at selection time. The intender renders tier-appropriate body content via the body contract from the PR-body-contract step: local-provable issues render evidence as today; external-proof-required issues additionally render a declared known-gap section naming exactly what proof is outstanding and that an operator will attach it. Admission may warn (not fail) when a campaign is majority external-proof-required, so issue selection is steered toward provable work. Acceptance: manifest schema accepts and digests the per-issue tier; body golden shows the known-gap slot; untagged issues default to local-provable with unchanged rendering.
closeReason: Implemented: profiles declare recognized evidence tiers (openclaw + default contracts now v2 with optional knownGap section), manifests accept digest-bound per-issue issueEvidenceTiers, admission warns on majority external-proof-required and refuses unrecognized tiers, and the intender renders the declared known-gap slot (proof named + operator attaches) with a new golden fixture while untagged issues render byte-identical. title: reconcile: review-feedback classifier — normalize upstream events into actionable categories via profile-declared bot grammar (untrusted-input discipline)
description: Reconcile currently stores raw deduplicated GitHub events and opens coarse attention items (maintainer_comment, failing_checks). The response loop needs normalized, actionable feedback. Add a classifier stage after event ingestion that folds events into a per-work-item feedback model with categories: failing_check (name, conclusion, url), changes_requested, review_bot_findings (structured: finding title, file, line, priority), maintainer_question, re_review_available, pr_merged, pr_closed. Recognition rules are profile data, not code: the profile declares known bot logins, durable-comment marker patterns, finding-line grammars, and the commands that trigger re-review. Untrusted-input discipline is absolute: classified output carries only structured extracted fields (check names, file paths, finding titles, priorities) each stamped untrusted-provenance; raw comment bodies are never passed onward as instructions, and no comment can name or trigger a controller action directly. Classified feedback rows are durable, deduplicated by source event node id, and are the sole input to the follow-up coordinator. Acceptance: fixture tests classify a real captured review-bot comment and a plain maintainer comment correctly under two different profiles; a comment containing imperative instructions produces only inert structured fields.
closeReason: Review-feedback classifier landed in extensions/campaign-controller: profile-declared bot grammar (src/reconcile/bot-grammar.ts, fail-closed validation), classifier (src/reconcile/classifier.ts) producing failing_check / changes_requested / review_bot_findings / maintainer_question / re_review_available / pr_merged / pr_closed with per-field untrusted provenance, durable dedupe by source event node id via new review_feedback table (migration 002), wired into UpstreamPrReconciler (feedbackCreated). Acceptance fixtures: captured review-bot comment and maintainer comment classify correctly under two profiles; imperative-instruction comment yields only inert structured fields. Extension bun test 326 pass; repo check:all 12/12 gates green.

title: warren core: dispatch a run onto an existing branch — run checks out and pushes back to a named head branch instead of composing warren/run_<id>
description: Warren core: every run composes a fresh workspace branch warren/run_<id>; there is no way to dispatch a run that continues an existing PR head branch, which blocks any follow-up push to a live PR. Add an opt-in dispatch field (e.g. existingBranch) threaded through POST /runs, the SDK, and warren run: when set, workspace composition checks out that branch from the configured remote instead of cutting a new one, the agent works on it, and reap pushes back to the same branch (no new branch, no new PR). Wire vocabulary additions go in src/core/wire.ts per convention. Guard rails: the field requires the branch to exist on the push remote; refuse when it does not (fail closed, actionable error); default behavior with the field absent is byte-identical to today — this must be provably opt-in since workspace composition is shared by all providers. Cover LocalProvider and K8sProvider paths (K8s repo-cache clone must fetch the branch). Acceptance: unit tests for compose+reap on an existing branch; an acceptance scenario dispatches run B onto run A's branch and asserts both commit sets land on one branch; ROUTE_TABLE/openapi/cli-ref regenerated.
closeReason: Implemented via salvaged branch warren/rescue/run_p3d78v30s1n9, imported scoped (20 files) and verified: existingBranch dispatch field wired through POST /runs, SDK, and warren run CLI; validateExistingBranchShape + fail-closed assertBranchOnRemote (git ls-remote) in src/runs/target-branch.ts; detached worktree checkout in src/workspace/materialize.ts + git/worktree.ts; LocalProvider teardown preserves the branch; K8s repo-cache mirror fetches +refs/heads/* so cloneBaseAndCarve checks out the existing branch. Opt-in provably: absent field takes the untouched carve path (unit tests src/runs/spawn/existing-branch.test.ts, target-branch.existing.test.ts, engine.existing-branch.test.ts). Acceptance scenario 44 dispatches runs A+B onto one shared branch and asserts both commit sets land on it plus a fail-closed 400 for a missing branch (fixed its push-target and stub-knob bugs). docs/cli-reference.md regenerated; check:all 12/12 gates green.

title: mutations phase 3: individually policy-gated updatePullRequest / postComment / updateBranch / followUpPush flags, transport methods, and journaled intents
description: The mutation vocabulary (src/mutations.ts) froze all flags false in V0; Phase 2 enabled exactly createPullRequest behind policy plus fresh approval. Phase 3 extends the same pattern to the response loop: updatePullRequest (PATCH body/title), postComment, updateBranch (update-branch API merge), and followUpPush (permission for follow-up runs to push to an existing PR head branch — fork-side, but policy-gated the same way). Each flag is individually enabled in the repository policy, default false, covered by the policy digest so enabling any one requires fresh owner approval. The GitHub transport gains exactly the corresponding methods, constructed only when the flag is enabled — the enforced-by-absence property holds per mutation, proven by a test that a disabled flag leaves no method to call. Every mutation execution follows the journal contract: intent journaled planned with a canonical request digest before any I/O, then executing/succeeded/uncertain/failure transitions identical to pr_execute. Acceptance: schema tests for the new flags and digest coverage; transport tests proving per-flag absence; journal round-trip test per mutation type.
closeReason: Phase-3 mutation vocabulary shipped in extensions/campaign-controller: updatePullRequest/postComment/updateBranch/followUpPush added to EXECUTABLE_MUTATION_FLAGS and followUpPush to MUTATION_FLAGS (src/mutations.ts); requireMutations now admits each executable flag individually with digest coverage (src/repository-policy.ts, digest changes per flag proven in tests); per-mutation gated transports in src/github/pr-mutations.ts (BunFetchGithubPrUpdater/BunFetchGithubCommentPoster/BunFetchGithubBranchUpdater/GitPushFollowUpPusher) with enforced-by-absence tests — a dry-run policy constructs no transport and each flag constructs only its own; journaled intents in src/pr-execute/mutation-journal.ts with planned-before-I/O, canonical request digest, and pr_execute-identical transitions, proven by round-trip tests per mutation type (pr_update, pr_comment, pr_update_branch, follow_up_push). 335 extension tests green, root check:all 12/12.

title: follow-up run coordinator: classified feedback -> journaled follow-up intent -> warren run on the existing PR branch -> reconcile the push, under budget caps
description: The controller opens a PR and then only observes. Close the loop: a follow-up coordinator consumes classified feedback rows (from the review-feedback classifier) for a work item with an open PR and, when policy enables followUpPush, journals a follow-up intent — a composed prompt containing the original issue context, the structured findings (untrusted-provenance fields only), the profile agentGuidance block, and the instruction to extend the existing branch — then dispatches a warren run with existingBranch set to the PR head branch, correlates the run, and reconciles the resulting push. Budget: follow-up runs draw from the same campaign caps via the existing reservation ledger, plus a new per-work-item iteration cap (policy field, e.g. maxFollowUpsPerPr, default small) so a chatty reviewer cannot ping-pong the budget away; hitting the cap opens an attention item instead of dispatching. Idempotence: one active follow-up per work item; re-ticks resume, never duplicate. Repeat-finding detection: if the newest findings equal the set already responded to, stop and open attention rather than looping. Acceptance: fake-warren/fake-GitHub test drives feedback -> journaled intent -> dispatched run -> push observed -> feedback marked addressed; iteration-cap and repeat-finding stops proven.
closeReason: Shipped in PR #1169 (merged): follow-up run coordinator src/follow-up/coordinator.ts + tests; close was lost at reap

title: mutation: updatePullRequest body refresh — re-render the body contract with new evidence and response summary after a follow-up lands
description: Review bots commonly re-review when the PR body changes (openclaw asks for exactly that once evidence is added), and follow-up pushes make the original body stale. When policy enables updatePullRequest, the controller re-renders the body via the profile body contract after a follow-up run lands or an operator attaches external proof: refreshed evidence lines from the follow-up run, a response-summary section listing each addressed finding (structured titles only), and the known-gap slot updated or cleared per the evidence-tier step. The PATCH request is journaled planned with its digest before I/O like every mutation, and the rendered body must stay deterministic for goldens. Never edit any body region the contract does not own — render the whole body from controller-owned state, treating the controller as the single writer of its own PRs; if a reconcile detects the live body diverged from the last rendered state (someone hand-edited), open an attention item and refuse to clobber without an operator flag. Acceptance: golden for the refreshed body; divergence-refusal test; journal round-trip; e2e shows body update following a completed follow-up run.
closeReason: Implemented the updatePullRequest body-refresh mutation in extensions/campaign-controller: responseSummary section key added to the PR-body contract vocabulary (default contract bumped to v3, optional section, goldens for prior profiles unchanged); renderRefreshedPrBody re-renders the whole body from controller-owned facts with follow-up evidence, structured response-summary titles, cleared known-gap slot, and a follow-up run reference (golden fixture src/pr-intent/__golden__/default-pr-body-refresh.json pins determinism); renderAndJournalBodyRefresh journals the PATCH intent planned with its canonical digest before any I/O under a body-digest action key with already_journaled/already_settled re-drive standing; divergence gate compares the live body (now carried on the narrowed PR snapshot) against the last rendered state, raising pr_body_diverged attention once and refusing to clobber without operatorOverride; execution settles through the shared mutation journal (succeeded/uncertain/permanent_failure, never re-sent). Tests: unit suite (golden, divergence-refusal incl. deduped attention, journal round-trip, settle discipline) plus e2e vertical slice driving the real BunFetchGithubPrUpdater transport against FakeGithubServer following a settled followUpPush + succeeded run. Extension bun test 418 pass; repo check:all 12/12 gates passed.

title: mutation: postComment — finding-response replies and profile-declared re-review commands, never echoing untrusted comment content
description: Some review protocols need a comment, not a body edit: acknowledging findings with what changed, or issuing the re-review command the profile grammar declares (e.g. a bot-mention command with write-access rules). When policy enables postComment, the controller journals and posts comments composed exclusively from controller-owned state: finding titles being addressed, run references, evidence lines. Hard rules: never echo raw upstream comment content (untrusted); never post more than one comment per follow-up cycle per work item (no bot chatter); comment templates live in the profile as data with named placeholders; posting a re-review command only happens when the profile declares the grammar and the preceding body-update or push actually occurred. Rate discipline: a per-day per-campaign comment cap in policy, exceeded -> attention item. Acceptance: template rendering tests under two profiles; the one-comment-per-cycle invariant proven; a grammar-less profile posts nothing; journal round-trip test.
closeReason: postComment mutation shipped in extensions/campaign-controller: profile-declared commentTemplates block (policy schema, digest-covered, fail-closed placeholders), pr-execute/post-comment.ts composing only from structured classifier fields + profile templates, deterministic one-comment-per-cycle action keys, per-day per-campaign cap raising comment_rate_capped attention, execution through the shared journalMutationIntent/executeJournaledMutation contract. Tests prove two-profile template rendering, the one-per-cycle invariant, crash mid-POST uncertainty, grammar-less profile posting nothing, and the journal round-trip. Extension suite 421 pass; repo check:all 12/12 gates green.

title: branch freshness: detect behind-base/conflicted PRs on reconcile; journaled updateBranch when clean, conflict-repair follow-up run when not
description: A draft PR that sits through review iterations goes stale against base: behind-base or conflicted merge state blocks CI and merging. On reconcile, read the PR mergeable/behind state. When behind and clean and policy enables updateBranch, journal and execute the update-branch API call (upstream merges base into the head branch). When conflicted, updateBranch cannot help: dispatch a conflict-repair follow-up run through the follow-up coordinator with a prompt instructing merge-conflict resolution on the existing branch (warren core existing-branch dispatch makes this possible), under the same iteration caps. Both paths are journaled; both are idempotent across ticks (a pending update or active repair run suppresses re-trigger). Acceptance: fake-GitHub tests for the clean path (update-branch called once, journaled) and the conflicted path (follow-up dispatched, no update-branch call); behind+disabled-policy opens an attention item instead.
closeReason: Branch freshness on reconcile: classifyBranchFreshness (mergeable_state dirty/behind), journaled-before-I/O policy-gated updateBranch via shared mutation journal when behind+clean, conflict-repair follow_up_run dispatch when conflicted, attention item when policy blocks, idempotent suppression on re-ticks. 13 new tests + coordinator unit tests; 12/12 gates green.

title: attention hygiene: auto-resolve failing_checks on green, resolve superseded-manifest items on approval, dedupe review-bot placeholder noise
description: Attention is the operator's queue, and it already accumulates noise: two failing_checks items for a check that later passed are still open, six superseded_by_new_manifest_version rows sit unresolved from one day of manifest churn, and review-bot placeholder comments (review started markers) each opened a maintainer_comment item. Add resolution rules to reconcile: (1) a failing_checks item auto-resolves when a later observation shows the same check name passing on the same PR (match on the stored check name + PR, stamp resolved_at with the resolving event key in detail_json); (2) superseded_by_new_manifest_version items auto-resolve when the superseding manifest version is approved; (3) comments the profile grammar classifies as bot placeholders or durable-comment edits never open attention at all — only classified actionable categories do (depends conceptually on the classifier landing first, but implementable against raw grammar if sequenced earlier). Resolution is monotonic and journal-free (attention is derived state, not a mutation). Acceptance: replay test over the captured openclaw#131131 event sequence yields zero stale attention rows at the end; each rule has a focused unit test.
closeReason: Implemented all three attention-hygiene rules in extensions/campaign-controller: (1) failing_checks items auto-resolve within one reconcile tick when the same check name (or combined rollup) goes green on the same PR, stamped with the resolving event key via new monotonic store.events.resolveAttentionAuto (journal-free); (2) superseded_by_new_manifest_version items auto-resolve on approval of the superseding digest in approveCampaign; (3) bot-placeholder comments (BOT/NONE association grammar, safe until the warren-2ec3 classifier) never open attention, and durable-comment edits dedupe to one item keyed by comment node id. Focused unit tests in src/reconcile/attention-hygiene.test.ts plus a replay of the openclaw#131131 sequence ending with zero stale attention rows. Extension suite 307 pass, repo check:all 12/12 gates passed.

title: manifest amendment flow: append issues / adjust budget via digest-re-approved amendment without spawning a superseded campaign row per edit
description: Every manifest edit today creates a full new campaign row and an unresolved superseded_by_new_manifest_version attention item — the live campaign burned through seven rows (v1-v7) in a day just iterating on prompt and mutation policy. Add an amendment flow: an amendment document references the campaign, carries only the changed fields (append issues, adjust budget caps, update prompt, flip a mutation flag), and is digest-bound and owner-approved exactly like a manifest — approval authority never weakens. On approval the controller applies the amendment as a new campaign version in place: same campaign id, version incremented, amendment journaled, prior planned-unexecuted intents from the old version explicitly invalidated or re-affirmed (declare which, deterministically, in the design note), and no superseded attention row is created for a clean amendment. Removing or reordering issues with work in flight is out of scope — refuse those with an actionable error. Acceptance: amendment schema + digest tests; e2e appends an issue to a completed-issues campaign and the tick dispatches it; zero attention noise from the amendment path.
closeReason: Manifest amendment flow landed in extensions/campaign-controller: validateCampaignAmendment/applyAmendment (src/amendment.ts) with fail-closed schema, canonical digest binding, and owner approval; campaign row is updated IN PLACE (same id, campaignVersion+1, migration 002 campaign_amendments append-only journal) with zero superseded_by_new_manifest_version attention rows; planned never-executed intents invalidated deterministically (permanent_failure/policy_violation + reservation release); CLI commands amendment validate/apply; 16 new unit tests + amendment-append e2e proves appended issue is tick-dispatched with 1 campaign row end to end.
