title: terminal accounting: merged/closed PR -> work-item outcome + campaign report (PRs opened/merged, cost per merged PR, iterations per PR)
description: The controller knows when a PR opens but has no terminal accounting: merged or closed upstream is only visible as raw events, campaign completion means intents executed, and there is no answer to the only questions that matter — how many PRs merged, at what cost, after how many iterations. Add terminal detection to reconcile (pr_merged / pr_closed_unmerged classified events flip the work item to a terminal outcome recorded on the row), and a campaign report assembled from durable state: per work item — issue ref, PR number, outcome, total spend (initial + follow-up runs from the reservation ledger), follow-up iteration count, wall-clock open-to-terminal; per campaign — PRs opened, merged, closed unmerged, still open, total spend, cost per merged PR. Surface it in the status CLI (machine ndjson + pretty) and keep it derivable purely from the store so it works on historical campaigns. Optional: emit the report row into the seeds issue when the tracker link exists. Acceptance: store-level report query tested against a seeded multi-item history; merged and closed-unmerged paths both flip outcomes exactly once; status output golden.
closeReason: Terminal accounting implemented in extensions/campaign-controller: work_items.outcome migration (002), exactly-once recordWorkItemOutcome, classifyTerminalOutcome wired into UpstreamPrReconciler (merged + closed_unmerged + first-outcome-wins tested in reconciler.test.ts), buildCampaignReport (per-item spend/follow-ups/open-to-terminal; per-campaign PRs opened/merged/closed/still-open, total spend, cost per merged PR) tested over a seeded multi-item history in src/report/report.test.ts, surfaced in status CLI output (run.test.ts). Extension bun test 317 pass; repo bun run check:all 12/12 gates passed.

description: Observed 5x in the pl-096b dogfood session (2026-08-28, runs run_ks6sqre5jt5r, run_zb02afg4ry5e, run_r4nvbhgcdqxa, run_6fpqay9at81q, run_6pmxr7ezk79e, provider openrouter model z-ai/glm-5.3-flash): the model's reasoning stream degenerates into endless newline tokens, the turn ends with stopReason=length after burning the full output budget (e.g. reasoning 4095/output 4096), and the agent never commits — runs die as dropped_commit or noChanges after $0.3-$2.4 each (~$4 total wasted). title: K8s cost-cap cancel destroys committed work: pod killed before finalize/salvage/branch push (run_d1y23g1vsdj6 lost 3 commits + passing tests at $5.05)
description: Cost-cap enforcement (event bridge) cancelled run_d1y23g1vsdj6 at capUsd=5/costUsd=5.05. The run pod reached a terminal phase without posting a finalize result or salvage bundle; reap logged branch_push_failed and 'committed work is unrecoverable'. The workspace held 3 complete commits with focused tests passing (37/37) ~1 min before the kill. Cost-cap termination must run the same finalize/salvage/push path as a graceful cancel — the kernel's pushed-workspace-branch guarantee is violated on cost-cap kill under K8sProvider. Evidence: run events 19:14:37.831Z cap event, 19:14:41 finalize errors, campaign cc-14f9c5e9 attempt a1.
closeReason: K8sProvider.cancel (the seam every cost-cap trip routes through — bridge enforceBudgetCap -> provider.cancel) now produces finalize/salvage: the pod agent-entrypoint latches the kubelet SIGTERM (deps.registerCancelSignal, wired in the import.meta.main block), witnesses cancel_requested on the event stream, kills the agent child, and falls through into runFinalizeEntrypoint with a bounded intent poll (WARREN_CANCEL_GRADE... WARREN_CANCEL_FINALIZE_MAX_WAIT_MS, 25s) so the branch is pushed or the no-intent salvage bundle banked inside the grace window. Cancel grace default raised 30s -> 90s to fit the salvage budget. Proof: src/runtime/k8s/agent-entrypoint.cancel-finalize.test.ts (signal-cancel pushes the branch + POSTs the finalize result identical to natural completion; bounded-window test banks the salvage bundle) and the bridge-level budget.test.ts test proving cost-cap cancel yields the same cancelled terminal outcome/path as an operator cancel. bun run check:all 12/12 green.

title: campaign-controller: review verdicts delivered by comment EDIT are invisible — event dedupe keys on node id, so ClawSweeper's edited-in-place review never re-enters the pipeline

title: hydrator: persist derived cost/tokens back to runs so a terminal run is hydrated at most once (write-through in hydrateRunsUsage + backfill on terminal reconciliation; write 0 when no envelopes exist)
description:
WHO: agent-ok. Single PR, no live-infra access needed.

WHY: `hydrateRunsUsage` (src/runs/usage-hydrate.ts) recomputes cost/tokens from events for every terminal run whose `cost_usd` is null, on every GET /runs, GET /analytics/runs and GET /analytics/behavior, and never writes the result back. 27 runs on the live DB are permanently null, so every list call re-reads ~4,800 event rows (~6 MB). That is the Supabase egress overage (659 GB / 250 GB).

DO:
1. In `hydrateRunsUsage`, after `aggregateUsageFromEvents` yields stats for a candidate, persist `costUsd`, `tokensInput`, `tokensOutput`, `tokensCacheRead`, `tokensCacheWrite` onto the run row (add a narrow `RunsRepo.updateUsage(runId, stats)` if none exists). Fire-and-forget is fine but log failures.
2. When a terminal candidate has zero usage envelopes, persist `costUsd = 0` so it stops being a candidate. Leave `cost_basis` untouched.
3. Also backfill at terminal reconciliation (the reap/finalize path that flips state to succeeded/failed/cancelled) so new runs never enter the null state when their envelopes exist. This is the follow-up warren-ab18 explicitly deferred.
4. Tests: candidate with envelopes is persisted and a second call issues no events query; zero-envelope candidate writes 0; non-terminal rows untouched. Both dialects via the existing repo test harness.

DONE WHEN: a second `hydrateRunsUsage` call over the same rows performs no `listUsageEvents` call; `bun run check:all` green.
closeReason: Write-through hydration: hydrateRunsUsage now persists derived cost/token stats onto candidate rows via new narrow RunsRepo.updateUsage (src/db/repos/runs.ts); zero-envelope terminal candidates write costUsd=0 preserving bridge-stamped token columns; backfill at terminal reconciliation via backfillTerminalUsage called from transitionToTerminal (src/runs/reap/state.ts); handlers (src/server/handlers/runs/analytics.ts, lifecycle.ts) pass deps.repos.runs as the persister — no src/db/schema imports. Tests: unit coverage in src/runs/usage-hydrate.test.ts (persist, second-call no-fetch, zero-write, non-terminal untouched, failure logging) and dialect repo tests in src/db/repos/runs.update-usage.test.ts. bun run check:all 12/12 green.

title: hydrator: narrow EventsRepo.listUsageEvents to payload type in (turn_end, result) on both dialects and stop selecting agent_end transcripts; add a regression test pinning the row set
description:
WHO: agent-ok. Single PR.

WHY: `EventsRepo.listUsageEvents` (src/db/repos/events.ts) filters only `kind='state_change' AND stream='system'`. The hydrator reads only pi `turn_end` and claude-code `result` envelopes (see src/core/usage-shape.ts), but the filter also returns `tool_execution_*`, `turn_start`, `message_*` and `agent_end` rows. `agent_end` averages 103 kB because it embeds the whole transcript. On the live DB that is 132k of 214k rows and 195 MB.

DO:
1. Add a payload-type predicate to the query: Postgres `payload_json->>'type' IN ('turn_end','result')`, SQLite `json_extract(payload_json,'$.type') IN (...)`. Source the type list from `usage-shape.ts` so the two never drift.
2. Select only the columns the aggregator reads if that is cheap to do without breaking the `EventRow` contract; otherwise keep the row shape.
3. Consider an expression index on `(run_id, (payload_json->>'type'))` for Postgres only if EXPLAIN shows a seq scan on the partial predicate; do not add one speculatively.
4. Regression test: seed a run with one of each envelope type and assert the returned set is exactly the two usage envelopes, on both dialects.

DONE WHEN: rows returned per candidate run drop from ~200 to ~50 on the fixture; `bun run check:all` green. Pairs with warren-b33e; both must ship before warren-4c27.
closeReason: Narrowed EventsRepo.listUsageEvents with a payload-type predicate on both dialects (pg payload_json->>'type', sqlite json_extract), sourced from the new USAGE_ENVELOPE_TYPES export in src/core/usage-shape.ts so SQL and readers cannot drift; kept the EventRow shape and added no index. Regression test in src/db/repos/events.test.ts seeds turn_start/turn_end/tool_execution_*/message_*/agent_end/result on the state_change+system carrier and asserts exactly turn_end and result return; bun run check:all 12/12 green.

title: postgres: opt-in kustomize component deploy/k8s/components/postgres (postgres:17 StatefulSet, 10Gi standard-rwo PVC, ClusterIP Service, Secret template, NetworkPolicy admitting only the warren pod, 250m/1Gi requests, standard capacity)
description:
WHO: agent-ok. Manifests + docs only; do not apply to any cluster.

WHY: warren under k8s wants a Postgres (RUNBOOK-K8S §1.5). Today that is Supabase across the internet. Ship an in-cluster option as an opt-in kustomize component so a fresh operator can choose it.

Run `kubectl kustomize` in a test (there is precedent in scripts/ for manifest checks) so the component renders. Update RUNBOOK-K8S §1.5 with an "in-cluster Postgres" subsection; the Supabase text stays until warren-a3ed.

closeReason: Shipped opt-in kustomize Component deploy/k8s/components/postgres/ (postgres:17 StatefulSet 1 replica 250m/1Gi req 1/2Gi lim, 10Gi PVC with storageClassName omitted, pg_isready readiness; ClusterIP Service :5432; postgres-credentials placeholder Secret template; NetworkPolicy admitting only control-plane pods in warren, denying warren-runs) with kustomization.yaml; added Components section to deploy/k8s/README.md and 'In-cluster Postgres' subsection to RUNBOOK-K8S §1.5 (DSN postgres://warren:<pw>@postgres.warren.svc:5432/warren, no sslmode); added scripts/postgres-component-manifest.test.ts rendering via kubectl kustomize with clean skip when kubectl is absent. bun run check:all 12/12 green.

title: postgres: backup layer manifests — nightly pg_dump -Fc CronJob to a GCS bucket via Workload Identity, a parameterised restore Job, and a ServiceAccount for both; document retention expectations
description:
WHO: agent-ok. Manifests + docs only; do not create GCP resources.

WHY: an in-cluster database is only acceptable with independent restore paths. This step ships the logical-backup layer as manifests; warren-32bd provisions the bucket and binds identity.

DO: under `deploy/k8s/components/postgres/backup/`:

title: HUMAN: provision the live backup substrate — GCS bucket (versioning, 30-day lifecycle), Workload Identity binding for the backup SA, apply the postgres component to the warren namespace, patch its PV reclaimPolicy to Retain, attach a daily PD snapshot schedule to the disk
description:
WHO: human-only. Creates billable GCP resources and touches the live cluster.

PRE: warren-9f5a and warren-6db7 merged.

DO (project warren-502318, region us-west1):
1. `gcloud storage buckets create gs://warren-db-backups-<suffix> --location=us-west1 --uniform-bucket-level-access`; enable versioning; lifecycle rule deleting noncurrent + >30-day objects.
2. Create GSA `postgres-backup@warren-502318.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, grant `roles/storage.objectAdmin` on the bucket only, bind Workload Identity to `warren/postgres-backup`.

title: postgres: migration tooling — scripts/pg-migrate/ with dump (public + drizzle schemas only, --no-owner --no-privileges), restore, and a DSN-to-DSN parity check (row counts per table, max(events.id), drizzle journal hash) plus a rewritten RUNBOOK-K8S §1.5 cutover procedure
description:
WHO: agent-ok. Scripts + docs; do not run against live databases.

WHY: cutover from Supabase must be verifiable, repeatable, and reversible. A fixed procedure with a parity check removes guesswork from the human step.

title: sizing: analysis of actual run-pod peak memory across August runs versus the 16 GiB live request, with Autopilot's 1:6.5 CPU:memory billing ratio and minimums documented in RUNBOOK-K8S; propose a request/limit pair with the cost delta, operator decides
description:
WHO: agent-ok. Analysis + docs; the operator applies any change.

WHY: the live overlay requests 16 GiB memory per run pod (WARREN_K8S_MEMORY_REQUEST_MIB=16384). Autopilot bills requests, enforces a 1:6.5 vCPU:GiB ratio, so a 1 vCPU / 16 GiB pod is billed as ~2.5 vCPU. Whether 16 GiB is needed is unmeasured.

DO:
1. Pull peak memory per run from what warren already records (src/runtime/k8s/pod-metrics.ts, OOM counters, and any usage the pod watcher stamps on events); if nothing records peak RSS, add a lightweight sample at finalize (container `status` / metrics.k8s.io) so future runs carry it. Do not add a new dependency.
2. From the August runs on the live DB (read-only queries are fine via the events table; ask the operator for a read DSN if needed), tabulate p50/p95/max memory, and the OOM count at the 16 GiB limit.
3. Write RUNBOOK-K8S §5.5-adjacent "Sizing run pods on Autopilot": the ratio rule, minimum request rounding, and a worked cost per pod-hour for the current and a proposed request.
4. Propose a request/limit pair (for example 4 GiB / 8 GiB) with expected monthly delta at ~114 pod-hours and the OOM risk. The operator sets the env var; this seed does not.

DONE WHEN: the table and proposal are in the runbook and on this seed; `bun run check:all` green.
closeReason: Proposal (docs/RUNBOOK-K8S.md §5.6): set WARREN_K8S_MEMORY_REQUEST_MIB=WARREN_K8S_MEMORY_LIMIT_MIB=4096. August data (470 agent pods): p50 1129 MiB, p90 1494, p95 1623, max 10234; buckets <=2GiB 458 / 2-4 3 / 4-8 7 / >8 2; all 8 pods >4GiB were openclaw; 1 oom_killed + 3 evicted. 4096 MiB sits ~2.5x above p95, covers 98% of pods. Autopilot bills the request and clamps the limit to the request, so at 16384 MiB with 1 vCPU the ratio rule inflates billing to 2.5 vCPU => $0.188/pod-h vs $0.0637 at 4096 MiB; at ~114 pod-h/month that is $21.43 => $7.26, saving ~$14.2/mo (~66%). OOM risk: 9/470 (1.9%, all openclaw) peaked above 4096 MiB and would OOM-kill; a per-project request override (future work, keyed off .warren/config.yaml) would let openclaw keep a larger cap. 2048 MiB rejected (only 26% above p90, would have OOM-killed 12 pods). Code: new src/runtime/k8s/pod-memory-sample.ts (never-throwing metrics.k8s.io sampler + unit tests) and a small finalize hook stamping one run_pod_memory_sample system event; no contract/provider restructure. bun run check:all 12/12 gates passed.

title: cancel of a K8s run is classified sandbox_run_lost/provider_error and infra-lost retry redispatches the cancelled run
description: Observed 2026-09-03 (pl-6076 session): POST /runs/run_2g53bxq8m2fh/cancel returned {state:running,...}; the run then finalised as failed/sandbox_run_lost (not cancelled) and src/runs/retry/infra-lost-retry.ts auto-dispatched run_0v5m7qq5t6ys with retryOf=run_2g53bxq8m2fh, doubling the dispatch. title: pi harness: bun run check:all exceeds the 1200 s per-command tool timeout on run pods, losing uncommitted work

title: postgres backup: restore Job cannot be parameterised with kubectl set env (Job template immutable) — ship a templated restore path
description:

WHY: deploy/k8s/components/postgres/backup/restore-job.yaml and the RUNBOOK-K8S Backups subsection say: kubectl set env job/postgres-restore RESTORE_DUMP=<date>, then unsuspend. Observed 2026-09-03 during the pl-6076 rehearsal (warren-49cc); the workaround was to jq-copy the Job with the env value set and create it under a new name (postgres-restore-20260903), which completed and restored 215k events from gs://warren-pg-backups-502318/warren/20260903.dump.

Update the runbook Backups subsection and scripts/postgres-component-manifest.test.ts. Say in the same subsection that the in-cluster DB must be idle (warren scaled to 0) before a restore.

DONE WHEN: a documented command sequence restores a named dump without editing an existing Job; bun run check:all green.
